          ¬Graph.Strategy.InterfaceReplacement.CompressibleSupport Baseline Target object support) →

          ¬row.Realizing ∧ (Handoff row.support ∨ row.Distinguishing)
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.ColdCorridor.row_closed
declarations.doc_string:
**`lem:cold-same-interface-table`.**

*"Every row of the same-interface cold table is routed to one of the already
closed outcomes: a dyadic cycle, a target-defective quotient, an existing Type
B or route-8 handoff, or a target-complete proper-support compression.  In
particular, an equal-length cold bounded germ and a short exceptional
self-return cannot be a terminal cold residual."*

The two hypotheses are the two facts the selected minimal counterexample
already carries and nothing else: it avoids the target, and no proper support
of it admits a target-complete compression.  A realizing row would hand the
object the target it avoids; a row that is neither handed off nor
distinguishing is a compression of its own support.  What is left is exactly
the manuscript's routing, so no row is terminal.

declarations.doc_string:
**`lem:cold-same-interface-table`, at a short exceptional self-return.**

"In particular, an equal-length cold bounded germ **and a short exceptional
self-return** cannot be a terminal cold residual."

The self-return half is the second conjunct of `def:cold-same-interface-table`'s
row family, and it is closed the same way, with one extra step in front: on a
target-avoiding object the self-return's length *is* one of
`lem:cold-short-self-return-filter`'s surviving exceptions, because any accepted
length in its smear interval would be realized through the corresponding
cold-window offset.  Its row is then closed by `row_closed`.

distinct rows.  Every bound is the registered signature's: the boundary size is
two, the retained boundary data is capped by the local target algebra's own
cut-state constant, the offsets range over the registered window order, and the
declared coordinate labels are the signature's finite alphabets.

saturation `(s−2)·p ≤ n`, comparing `τ(θ)` against `a/b` is comparing the
density against the single coefficient `b·s + a·(s−2)` over `a`.

where `1/73` comes from; the numeral is computed by
`Fixtures.ColdCorridorLedger`, never written.

declarations.doc_string:
**`lem:curvature-dependence-routing` for an admissible quotient.**

The first two disjuncts of `AttemptedQuotient.route` cannot occur here — an
admissible quotient is target-complete by definition, which is what `fibrewise`
and `contextUniversal` record — so a rank-reducing admissible quotient falls in
the remaining two by the scope of its determination support: proper, and then it
is a replacement of that support; or the whole graph, and then it is a smaller
closed representative.

Both alternatives are refuted at a selected minimal counterexample —
`InterfaceReplacement.not_replacementSupport` for the first, and the selection's
own minimality for the second.

ambient centres in the incidence component.

declarations.type:
∀ {object : Graph.FiniteObject} {LengthOK : ℕ → Prop} {Uncompressible WindowFree : Finset object.Vertex → Prop}

  (grouped :
    Graph.DecoratedHandoff.GroupedEnvelopes object LengthOK Uncompressible WindowFree HighDegree Absorbing Core)
  (threshold dischargeScale : ℕ) (component : grouped.Component),
  grouped.componentCharge threshold dischargeScale component =
    ↑dischargeScale *
          ↑(∑ core ∈ grouped.componentCores component,
              object.positiveDeficiency (grouped.envelope core).core threshold) -
        ↑dischargeScale * ↑(grouped.componentTokens threshold component) -
      ↑(∑ core ∈ grouped.componentCores component, (grouped.envelope core).core.card)

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.DecoratedHandoff.Separation
declarations.doc_string:
**Two germs through one completion port, separating at a vertex.**

`def:typeA-continuation-classes`' *"they separate at `z`"*: the two germs have
the same continuation class up to `z`, and their next incidences after `z` are
distinct.  *Same continuation class up to `z`* is three conjuncts and all three
are carried here — `z` occurs in both germs and they have the same ordered
prefix from `h` to `z`, which the two decompositions below exhibit (and exhibit
as maximal, so `z` is the pair's first separator), **and the two coordinates
have the same image in the relevant boundary-degree fibre**, which is the last
group of fields.

That third conjunct is not a copied boundary profile.  `S_z` is the
manuscript's own *"finite connected support consisting of the common prefix
from `h` to `z`, the two connector tails from `z` to their first-entry
receivers, the two receiver-entry channels in `X`, the completion port boundary
datum, and the declared supports of the two response coordinates"*, presented
through the framework's existing support-to-atom construction; the two
coordinates' declared readings are then registered in that atom's *generated*
profile certificate, whose constructor is private to the framework so that no
caller registers a guessed profile.  `sameFibre` below reads the manuscript's
conjunct off that registration.

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.DecoratedHandoff.Separation.four_le_degree_of_mem_cutBoundary
declarations.doc_string:
**`z` on the boundary of `S_z` has ambient degree at least `4`.**

The converse branch of the previous theorem, and the one the manuscript takes
when its *"Assume `d_G(z)=3`"* fails: an interface label of `S_z` has a
neighbour outside `S_z`, that neighbour is none of the three incidences the
separation uses -- those all lie in `S_z` -- so `z` has a fourth neighbour.
Nothing is assumed on either side: the two theorems are the two arms of one
decidable split on the framework's own `cutBoundary`.

declarations.doc_string:
**`d_G(z) = 3` leaves `z` off the boundary of `S_z`.**

*"Then the root incidence and the two next incidences used by the separated
germs are all incidences of `z`.  Consequently the switch support `S_z` has no
unused ambient incidence at `z`."*  This is that sentence, computed on the
framework's own `cutBoundary`: at `d_G(z) = 3` the separator's three incidences
are exactly its neighbours, all three lie in `S_z`, so `z` has no neighbour
outside `S_z` and is an internal vertex of the atom rather than an interface
label.  Nothing is assumed -- the manuscript's *"Assume `d_G(z)=3`"* is the
branch `four_le_degree_of_surviving` splits on, and this is what that branch
carries.

`wh` is the root incidence at `z`; otherwise the last edge of the common prefix

distinct next incidences after `z`.  Hence `d_G(z) ≥ 3`."*

registered baseline.

**The declared reading the switch support carries.**

The reading is presented on `S_z`'s own interface, and its realizations are
registered in `S_z`'s own generated profile certificate exactly where the
manuscript registers them: *"Assume `d_G(z)=3`. ... Consequently the switch
support `S_z` has no unused ambient incidence at `z`.  The two separated
responses **therefore** form a finite declared boundaried response state with
the same boundary-degree profile: the boundary records the root incidence, the
two connector tails to their first entries in `X`, and the two receiver-entry
channels."*  That sentence is the `registered` field, in the framework's own
registration vocabulary and against the framework's own computed certificate;
the *"same boundary-degree profile"* half is then derived below rather than
declared.

declarations.doc_string:
**The manuscript's step where `z` is internal to `S_z`.**  Off the
interface of `S_z` the identification of two declared coordinates cannot move
an interface label, so every realization of the reading is a finite declared
boundaried state in `S_z`'s own registered fibre.  The premise is a decidable
property of the residual's own `cutBoundary`, discharged on the branch by
`Separation.separator_notMem_cutBoundary`; it is not an assumption a caller
chooses.

declarations.doc_string:
**A separator with no unused ambient incidence is absorbed.**

*"Consider the quotient that identifies the two separated response coordinates
on this finite state.  If some compatible outside context distinguishes the two
responses, the quotient is target-defective ..., which is exit (4).  Otherwise
the identification is target-complete."*

`lem:context-universality`'s exhaustiveness is
`Response.contextEquivalent_or_targetDefect`; the boundary-degree half of
target-completeness is the reading's `fibre` clause at the exhausted
separator.

declarations.doc_string:
**`lem:typeA-continuation-routing`, at a pair of declared coordinates.**

*"Then either one of exits (4)--(6) of `def:typeA-saturated-exits` occurs, or
`𝒦` has a surviving first separator."*

The two germs are distinct declared coordinates through the same port, so
neither is a prefix of the other and they separate; at that separator the
identification is absorbed — which is exits `(4)`--`(6)` — or it is not, which
is the surviving first separator.

declarations.type:
∀ {object : Graph.FiniteObject} {LengthOK : ℕ → Prop} {Uncompressible WindowFree : Finset object.Vertex → Prop}
  {HighDegree : object.Vertex → Prop} {Absorbing : object.Vertex → object.Vertex → object.Vertex → Prop}
  {envelope : Graph.DecoratedHandoff.Envelope object LengthOK HighDegree Absorbing},
  ¬Graph.HasCycleWithLength LengthOK object →
    WindowFree envelope.core →
      (∀ (piece : Finset object.Vertex), Uncompressible piece) →
        Graph.DecoratedHandoff.Admissible object LengthOK Uncompressible WindowFree envelope
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.DecoratedHandoff.admissible_of_envelope
declarations.doc_string:
**`lem:decorated-fan-admissibility`.**

*"If exit (7) of `def:typeA-saturated-exits` occurs in a saturated Type A
branch, the resulting decorated handoff fan envelope carries exactly the data
required by the Type B fan calculation."*

The counted core is the Type A support `X` used in
`lem:typeA-high-degree-handoff`, so the first three clauses are inherited from
`def:admissible` — here read as the branch's own committed facts — and the
fourth is the geometric clause of the envelope's fan-safe cliques.  Nothing in
the derivation mentions `lem:typeB-exclusion`.

declarations.type:
{object : Graph.FiniteObject} →
  {support : Finset object.Vertex} →
    {receiver outside : object.Vertex} →
      {LengthOK : ℕ → Prop} →
        {HighDegree : object.Vertex → Prop} →
          {Absorbing : object.Vertex → object.Vertex → object.Vertex → Prop} →
            (separation : Graph.DecoratedHandoff.Separation object support receiver outside) →
              (armLeft armRight : List object.Vertex) →
                armLeft.head? = some separation.nextLeft →
                  armRight.head? = some separation.nextRight →
                    List.IsChain object.graph.Adj armLeft →
                      List.IsChain object.graph.Adj armRight →
                        armLeft.Nodup →
                          armRight.Nodup →
                            (∃ terminal, armLeft.getLast? = some terminal ∧ terminal ∈ support) →
                              (∃ terminal, armRight.getLast? = some terminal ∧ terminal ∈ support) →
                                (∀ vertex ∈ armLeft,
                                    vertex ∈ support ∨ vertex = separation.separator → armLeft.getLast? = some vertex) →
                                  (∀ vertex ∈ armRight,
                                      vertex ∈ support ∨ vertex = separation.separator →
                                        armRight.getLast? = some vertex) →
                                    HighDegree separation.separator →
                                      ¬Graph.HasCycleWithLength LengthOK object →
                                        ¬Absorbing separation.separator separation.nextLeft separation.nextRight →
                                          ¬Absorbing separation.separator separation.nextRight separation.nextLeft →
                                            Graph.DecoratedHandoff.Envelope object LengthOK HighDegree Absorbing
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.DecoratedHandoff.envelopeOfSeparation
declarations.doc_string:
**`lem:typeA-high-degree-handoff`.**

*"Let `X` be a Type A support, and let `z` be a surviving first separator for a
finite family of declared response coordinates through one completion port.
Then `z`, together with the separated connector tails from `z` to their
first-entry data in `X`, produces a decorated handoff fan envelope."*

`Y = X` is the counted remainder core and `H = {z}`; the assigned first
neighbours are the two separated next incidences, which are distinct because the
germs separate, and the arms are the two connector tails.  The fan-safe clique
condition on that pair is the geometric clause — discharged from the selected
object's target avoidance — together with the four quotient clauses, which are
the exits already denied on this branch.

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.DecoratedHandoff.four_le_degree_of_surviving
declarations.doc_string:
**`lem:typeA-cubic-switch-absorption`.**  A surviving first separator for
two declared response coordinates through one completion port has

  `d_G(z) ≥ 4`.

*"Hence `d_G(z) ≥ 3` ... Assume `d_G(z) = 3` ... Each of these alternatives is
exactly the absorbed case ... This contradicts that `z` is surviving.  Thus
`d_G(z) ≠ 3`, and the already-proved inequality `d_G(z) ≥ 3` gives
`d_G(z) ≥ 4`."*

          LengthOK (return'.walk.length + 2) → Graph.HasCycleWithLength LengthOK object

declarations.doc_string:
**`lem:bridgeless`.**  A minimal object avoiding the cycle target has a
simple return for every ordered edge whose two endpoint degrees pay for the
contraction: after deleting that edge its endpoints are still joined.
Equivalently, no such edge is a bridge, so every one of them lies on a cycle.

The degree hypothesis is exactly what the merged vertex costs -- the contracted
edge is counted once at each endpoint -- and at the manuscript's baseline of
three it is implied by the baseline alone.

The contraction of the edge is smaller, meets the same baseline, and therefore
carries an accepted cycle; that cycle is a cycle of the source unless it changes
kind at the tail, which would itself be the return.

  (certificate.walk.rotate contraction.tailVertex tailMem).length = certificate.walk.length →
    3 ≤ (certificate.walk.rotate contraction.tailVertex tailMem).length →
      (certificate.walk.rotate contraction.tailVertex tailMem).tail.length + 1 =
          (certificate.walk.rotate contraction.tailVertex tailMem).length →
        (certificate.walk.rotate contraction.tailVertex tailMem).tail.reverse.length =
            (certificate.walk.rotate contraction.tailVertex tailMem).tail.length →
          ¬0 < (certificate.walk.rotate contraction.tailVertex tailMem).tail.reverse.length → False

declarations.doc_string:
**`𝒬₄(w)`**, at a receiver of a support.

`entry` is the receiver's declared reading: a finite family of declared
coordinates, each with the carrier support its declared support uses, presented
on one labelled boundary.  `coordinate` is the canonical coordinate a routed
load is given by `def:declared-coordinate-signature`, and `Generated` is the
family's own generation predicate: `Generated clause base identified` says the
listed construction `clause` generates, from the reading `base`, the quotient
that identifies or forgets exactly `identified`.

No construction is generated here.  A node that owns one of the four clauses
supplies it through `Generated`; every statement below is quantified over the
family, so no row invents a member and none is dropped.

This is the formal content of `def:typeA-exit4-peeling`: a generated member of
the canonical receiver family, a load whose declared coordinate is in that
member's support, two realizations in the same boundary-degree fibre, and a
compatible outside context distinguishing their target predicates.

declarations.doc_string:
**`lem:typeA-exit4-residual-routing`, with the descent it opens.**

*"If `L₄(w) ≥ 4q(w)`, then the unpeeled routed loads at `w` realize one of exits
(1)--(8).  If the realized exit is (4), the peeling set can be enlarged by one
additional unpeeled routed load."*

`step` is that reading: while the peeled residual is still saturated, exit `(4)`
supplies a fresh unpeeled load.  Each enlargement drops `L₄(w)` by exactly one
(`residualLoad_insert`), so the descent terminates, and it terminates at a
peeling set whose residual is unsaturated -- the receiver retested at node
`[89]` with nonnegative charge.

`Retained` is whatever the peeling set is required to carry along the descent;
`def:typeA-exit4-peeling` equips each listed load with one exit-`(4)` witness,
whose future response-semantic refinement must preserve it because each
step supplies its own witness.

declarations.doc_string:
**`lem:typeA-exit4-peeling-charge`.**

*"After the loads in `P₄(w)` have left the Type A receiver calculation through
exit (4), the remaining receiver charge is `q(w) − ¼ − ¼·L₄(w)`.  In particular,
if `L₄(w) ≤ 4q(w) − 1`, then the remaining charge at `w` is nonnegative."*

exactly when the peeled residual is unsaturated -- which is how the receiver is
retested at node `[89]`.

    False

**`lem:typeA-exit4-discharge`.**

*"If exit (4) occurs through a quotient whose declared support contains the
canonical coordinate of an unpeeled routed load `u`, then `P₄(w) ∪ {u}` is a
valid peeling set and the remaining receiver deficit is reduced by exactly
`1/4`."*

`def:typeA-exit4-peeling` -- the load was not in the set -- and drops `L₄(w)` by
exactly one, which by `lem:typeA-exit4-peeling-charge` is exactly one quarter of
remaining deficit.

      False

**The empty peeling set is the loop's entry.**  `P₄(w) = ∅` gives
`L₄(w) = L(w)`, so `lem:typeA-exit4-residual-routing`'s hypothesis
`L₄(w) ≥ s·q(w)` at the empty peeling set *is* node `[89]`'s own saturation.

fact from the saturation already on the ledger instead of restating it.

                ∃ load ∈ object.routedLoads support threshold receiver,

declarations.doc_string:
**Finite saturated-handoff descent from an arbitrary peeling state.**

This is the termination core of `lem:typeA-saturated-handoff`, stated at the
current receiver/peeling state rather than only at the empty peeling set.  If
every saturated retained peeling state either reaches one of the forward
terminal alternatives or supplies a fresh exit-`(4)` load, then the iteration
terminates either at such a terminal state or at an unsaturated peeled
residual.  The proof uses only the strict one-load decrease of
`lem:typeA-exit4-discharge`; it does not choose, transport, or publish any
branch fact.

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FibrePressureStatement
declarations.doc_string:
**Node `[137]`, second production**: `lem:capacity-token-high-load` with
`cor:forced-homogeneous-same-token-scale`,
`thm:sharp-classwise-homogeneous-token-budget` (e) and
`thm:sharp-surplus-overload-audit` (d).

The statement is existential in the ledger: it says the object's *own*
capacity-token ledger realizes the high-load display, so it is not provable
without node `[136]`'s commitment that such a ledger exists.  That commitment is
read by exact key and supplied by the executor, not assumed here.

declarations.doc_string:
**`κ(B)`** of `def:primitive-sparse-blocker-carrier`, clause by clause:

* (a), (b) a vertex or edge-incidence blocker is its own carrier;
* (c) a common shoulder endpoint or cubic buffer vertex is its own carrier;
* (d), (e) a coordinate's carrier is the least item contained in its declared
  support, which is its least vertex because `V(G)` is the first summand of
  `𝔘_sp(G)`;
* (f) a chord-set obstruction's carrier is the least selected surplus port whose
  shoulder chord belongs to the set.

The two selecting clauses are partial: the manuscript's reason that the carrier
exists — the declared support of a sparse pair-response coordinate contains
`T(p) ∪ T(q)`, and the chord set of a suppressed family is nonempty — is a
property of the presentation, so it stays an antecedent here rather than becoming
a hypothesis about the object.

  Graph.FiniteObject.Blocker.carrier object threshold coordinateSupport chordPort
      (Graph.FiniteObject.Blocker.sharedDeclaredSupport (Graph.FiniteObject.CarrierItem.vertex vertex)) =
    some (Sum.inl vertex)

declarations.doc_string:
**The canonical data of `def:active-surplus-demands`, in the concrete form
the six clauses read.**

Clauses (a), (b) and (c) intersect finite vertex sets of the two demands, which
`Graph/PortResponseSupport` builds canonically: `T(p) ∪ Γ(p)` is
`SurplusPort.declaredSupport`, `R_p` is `SurplusPort.returnSupport`, and
`{a_p, b_p, x(p)}` is `SurplusPort.support`.  Nothing here re-derives them; the
fields are the assignment `p ↦ (that data)` over the selected family, which is
what makes a blocker of those clauses an object of `𝔘_sp(G)`.

Clauses (d), (e) and (f) are not data of a port.  They are the coordinates and
chord sets that a *failed* quotient, replacement or suppression produces, so
they enter as the pair-indexed finite families the dependence lemmas hand back.
An empty family is the honest reading of "this pair has no obstruction of that
clause".

**`def:surplus-blockers` as the ledger's applicability relation.**

A declared clause applies to a pair exactly when the pair carries a blocker
object of that clause.  Handing this to `FiniteObject.chargedPairs` at
`canonicalBlockerOrder` is `def:canonical-blocker-ledger` at the manuscript's own
`𝖡𝗅𝗄`: `Π_blk` becomes the pairs with a blocker rather than the pairs standing
in a quantified relation.

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.DemandActivation.blockers
declarations.doc_string:
**`𝖡𝗅𝗄(π)`**: the finite set of sparse surplus blockers of a pair.

The union of the six clauses, each read at the pair's own two demands.  Clauses
(a), (b) and (c) range over the ordered pairs of distinct members of `π`, which
is how an unordered pair supplies "the two declared supports"; the remaining
three are the obstruction families the activation carries.

declarations.type:
∀ {object : Graph.FiniteObject} {Coordinate Chord : Type v} (activation : object.DemandActivation Coordinate Chord)
  (pair : Finset (object.Vertex × object.Vertex)),
  activation.blockers pair =
    ((pair ×ˢ pair).biUnion fun demands =>
        Finset.image Graph.FiniteObject.Blocker.sharedDeclaredSupport
            (Graph.FiniteObject.DemandActivation.sharedItems object (activation.declaredSupport demands.1)
              (activation.declaredSupport demands.2)) ∪
          (Finset.image Graph.FiniteObject.Blocker.sharedReturnSupport
              (Graph.FiniteObject.DemandActivation.sharedItems object (activation.returnSupport demands.1)
                (activation.returnSupport demands.2)) ∪
            Finset.image Graph.FiniteObject.Blocker.sharedLocalBuffer
              (activation.localBuffer demands.1 ∩ activation.localBuffer demands.2))) ∪
      (Finset.image Graph.FiniteObject.Blocker.boundaryProfile (activation.profileObstructions pair) ∪
        (Finset.image Graph.FiniteObject.Blocker.targetResponse (activation.responseObstructions pair) ∪
          Finset.image Graph.FiniteObject.Blocker.arithmeticChordSet (activation.chordObstructions pair)))
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.DemandActivation.blockers.eq_1

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.DemandActivation.sharedItems
declarations.doc_string:
The vertices and edge-incidences contained in both of two vertex sets: the
intersection clauses (a) and (b) take, read at both summands of the carrier.  An
edge-incidence is contained in a support exactly when both of its endpoints
are.

∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (left right : Finset object.Vertex),
  Graph.FiniteObject.DemandActivation.sharedItems object left right =
    Finset.image Graph.FiniteObject.CarrierItem.vertex (left ∩ right) ∪
      Finset.image Graph.FiniteObject.CarrierItem.incidence
        ({pair ∈ object.incidences | pair.1 ∈ left ∧ pair.2 ∈ left ∧ pair.1 ∈ right ∧ pair.2 ∈ right})
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.DemandActivation.sharedItems.eq_1

declarations.type:
∀ {object : Graph.FiniteObject} [inst : DecidableEq object.Vertex] {label : Finset (object.Vertex × object.Vertex)}
  {support ambient : Finset object.Vertex},
  support ⊆ ambient →
    (Graph.DeclaredSignature.Coordinate.restrict (Graph.FiniteObject.DemandActivation.pairCoordinate label ambient)
          support).support =
      Graph.DeclaredSignature.Coordinate.support (Graph.FiniteObject.DemandActivation.pairCoordinate label support)
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.DemandActivation.support_restrict_pairCoordinate
declarations.doc_string:
**The manuscript's closing sentence, as a theorem.**

> Each `r_π` is then viewed as a labelled coordinate of `ρ^ex_{∂X_Π}(X_Π)` by
> restriction to its declared support.

The ambient profile's `π`-labelled coordinate, restricted by clause (D8) to
`X_π`, has support exactly `X_π` — because `X_π ⊆ X_Π`.  So the view of `r_π`
inside `ρ^ex_{∂X_Π}(X_Π)` carries the same declared support as `r_π` itself, and
the manuscript's two readings agree on the datum every later definition reads
off a declared coordinate.

declarations.type:
∀ {object : Graph.FiniteObject} {left right : Finset object.Vertex} {vertex : object.Vertex},
  vertex ∈ left →
    vertex ∈ right →
      Graph.FiniteObject.CarrierItem.vertex vertex ∈ Graph.FiniteObject.DemandActivation.sharedItems object left right
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.DemandActivation.vertex_mem_sharedItems
declarations.doc_string:
A vertex of the intersection is a shared item: the vertex half of clauses
(a) and (b).

declarations.type: (object : Graph.FiniteObject) → Finset object.Vertex → ℕ → object.Vertex → object.Vertex → Prop
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.FullConnected
declarations.doc_string:
**Connectivity through non-receiving vertices.**  A walk inside the support
none of whose vertices is a receiver: each spends *at least* the baseline
internally.  It is written on ambient walks rather than on the induced object so
that no restriction has to be built and no walk has to be transported.

The bound is `≥` rather than `=` because a support may carry vertices above the
baseline -- an assigned Type B fan centre is one -- and the routing argument
below must be able to pass through them.  On a support of zero assigned surplus
no vertex exceeds the baseline, so there the two readings coincide and this is
`lem:typeA-receiver-loads`' own "through full vertices".

declarations.type: (object : Graph.FiniteObject) → ℕ → Finset object.Vertex → Prop
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.InducesWindow
declarations.doc_string:
A support carries an induced window of the given order when it has exactly
that many vertices and induces a path on them.

The cardinality clause is the manuscript's own: `𝒫` is a family of induced
*copies* of the window, so `|V(P)|` is the window order.  Without it a support
could carry a window while being arbitrarily larger, and the packing's internal
degree mass -- which `[28]`--`[29]` spends -- would not be determined.

declarations.type: (object : Graph.FiniteObject) → Finset object.Vertex → Type u
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.InternalWedge
declarations.doc_string:
**A raw internal length-two curvature test of a region.**  A centre
together with an unordered pair of two of its neighbours inside the region.
No response value, quotient image, or rank outcome is stored: the test is the
coordinate, and what a quotient does to it is the quotient's business.

declarations.type: (object : Graph.FiniteObject) → Finset object.Vertex → ℕ → object.Vertex → Prop
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.IsFullDegree
declarations.doc_string:
**A full vertex of a support**: it spends the whole baseline internally, so
it has no port of its own and must be routed to a receiver.

declarations.type: (object : Graph.FiniteObject) → Finset object.Vertex → ℕ → object.Vertex → Prop
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.IsReceiver
declarations.doc_string:
**A receiver of a support.**  Its internal degree is below the baseline, so
`missingPorts` of its ambient incidences leave the support.

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (support : Finset object.Vertex) (threshold : ℕ) (vertex : object.Vertex),
  object.IsReceiver support threshold vertex = (vertex ∈ support ∧ object.internalDegree support vertex < threshold)
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.IsReceiver.eq_1

declarations.type:

support, every vertex but the last is full, and the last is a receiver.

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.MixedTargetCoordinate
declarations.doc_string:
The declared family used by the mixed sparse-spine count: the selected
window coordinates and one labelled response coordinate for every free pair.
The sum tags make the union disjoint, exactly as the manuscript's labelled
copies clause (D8) requires.

declarations.type: (object : Graph.FiniteObject) → Finset object.Vertex → ℕ → ℕ → Prop
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.NegativeNetCharge
declarations.doc_string:
**`def:net-charge`, negative side.**  `N₀(X) < 0`, written without
subtraction: `s·def⁺(X) < |V(X)| + s·σ(X)`.  Multiplying the manuscript's
`def⁺(X) − σ(X) − |V(X)|/s < 0` by the positive `s` and moving both negative
terms across is exactly this, and it is an integer comparison, so no rounding
is introduced by the `1/s`.

declarations.type: (object : Graph.FiniteObject) → Finset object.Vertex → ℕ → ℕ → Prop
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.NonNegativeNetCharge
declarations.doc_string:
**`def:net-charge`, nonnegative side.**  `N₀(X) ≥ 0`, the exact negation of
`NegativeNetCharge`.

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (support : Finset object.Vertex) (threshold dischargeScale : ℕ),
  object.NonNegativeNetCharge support threshold dischargeScale =
    (support.card + dischargeScale * object.ambientSurplus support threshold ≤
      dischargeScale * object.positiveDeficiency support threshold)
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.NonNegativeNetCharge.eq_1

declarations.type: Graph.FiniteObject → Type u
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.PairCoordinate

`def:declared-coordinate-signature` over the object's vertices, labelled by a

declarations.type: (object : Graph.FiniteObject) → Finset object.Vertex → ℕ → ℕ → object.Vertex → Prop
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.Saturated
declarations.doc_string:
**A saturated receiver.**  Its routed load has reached the registered
multiple of its own port count.

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (support : Finset object.Vertex) (threshold scale : ℕ) (receiver : object.Vertex),
  object.Saturated support threshold scale receiver =
    (scale * object.missingPorts support threshold receiver ≤ object.routedLoad support threshold receiver)
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.Saturated.eq_1

declarations.type: ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → Prop
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.SufficientlyLargeForNetCap
declarations.doc_string:
The exact finite predicate used for the manuscript's phrase "for all
sufficiently large `n`" at the net-cap node.

declarations.type:
∀ (threshold dischargeScale windowOrder windowRate surplusScale size : ℕ),
  Graph.FiniteObject.SufficientlyLargeForNetCap threshold dischargeScale windowOrder windowRate surplusScale size =
    (2 * Graph.FiniteObject.netCapWindowCost threshold dischargeScale windowOrder * threshold ≤ size.log2 ∧
      2 * Graph.FiniteObject.netCapErrorScale threshold dischargeScale windowOrder windowRate surplusScale *
            (2 * Graph.FiniteObject.netCapErrorScale threshold dischargeScale windowOrder windowRate surplusScale) ≤
          size ∧
        2 * Graph.FiniteObject.netCapErrorScale threshold dischargeScale windowOrder windowRate surplusScale < size)
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.SufficientlyLargeForNetCap.eq_1

declarations.doc_string:
**The canonical return path `R_p`.**  The lexicographically first simple
`x(p)`--`c(p)` path of `G − c(p)x(p)`, as the framework's own length-major
schedule selects it.

The hypothesis is the ledger fact itself.  Clause (b) is committed as
`Nonempty (PortReturn …)`, and `SimpleGraph.Reachable` is by definition
`Nonempty (Walk …)`, so the existence of the canonical choice needs the
*proposition* and not a chosen witness.  There is nothing to assume: if no
return path existed the port's edge would be a bridge, and
`EdgeContraction.hasReturn_of_minimal` has already refuted that at a selected
minimal counterexample.

**`lem:sparse-port-activation`, clause (b).**

The port's own edge is not a bridge: contracting it gives a strictly smaller
object which still meets the baseline, because the endpoint degree and the
centre's surplus together pay for the merged vertex, so minimality supplies that
contraction an accepted cycle and avoidance turns it into a return.  The first
edge of that return after the endpoint is a shoulder because the only other
incidence of the endpoint is the deleted port edge itself.

and its own minimality, together with the port's shoulder pair -- the same three
ledger facts clause (c) consumes.

**`Γ(p)`, the canonical response support.**

Clause (d) at a triangular port: the triangle `x a_p b_p x` -- whose vertices are
exactly `T(p)` -- together with the return path `R_p`.  Clause (c) at an open
port: the suppression path `Q_p ⊆ G − x(p)`.

the object and the port: neither the return nor the suppression path is a
parameter to be supplied, and neither can fail to exist -- clause (b) is
`lem:bridgeless` and clause (c) is the open-port suppression witness, both
already proved at a selected minimal counterexample.

until its last vertex, which is one.  This is the shape a routed trace has;

observable that the node-`[19]` split compares: on the standing baseline the
handshake gives `Σ_v (d(v) − δ) = 2m − δn`.  So this is not a second surplus
notion, and a window-local surplus can be paid for out of a registered ceiling
on `σ(G)`.

declarations.type: ∀ (baseline d : ℕ), 3 ≤ baseline → baseline ≤ d.choose 2 + 2 * (baseline - d)
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.baseline_le_choose_two_add_two_mul_deficit
declarations.doc_string:
**The per-vertex clause of `lem:wedge-lower`** at a registered baseline
`δ ≥ 3`: one vertex's own wedge contribution, together with twice its own
deficiency below `δ`, always covers `δ`.

Below the baseline the doubled deficiency makes up the gap between `2d` and
`2δ`; at or above it the deficiency vanishes and `C(d,2)` alone suffices,
which is where `3 ≤ δ` is spent.

declarations.type:
∀ (baseline d : ℕ),
  3 ≤ baseline → d < baseline → 2 * d ≤ d.choose 2 + 3 → ¬baseline ≤ d.choose 2 + 2 * (baseline - d) → False
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.baseline_le_choose_two_add_two_mul_deficit._proof_1_1

declarations.type: ∀ (baseline d : ℕ), d ≥ baseline → ¬baseline - d = 0 → False
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.baseline_le_choose_two_add_two_mul_deficit._proof_1_2

declarations.type:
∀ (baseline d : ℕ),

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (support : Finset object.Vertex) (baseline : ℕ),

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.baseline_mul_card_le_internalWedgeCount_add_two_mul_positiveDeficiency
declarations.doc_string:
**`lem:wedge-lower`, subtraction-free.**

  `δ·|X| ≤ W₂(X) + 2·def⁺(X)`

at every region `X` of the object, for every registered baseline `δ ≥ 3`.
This is the manuscript's `W₂(X) ≥ δ|X| − 2def⁺(X)` with the truncation moved
to the side where it cannot silently absorb a failure.

The proof is the manuscript's: sum the per-vertex clause over the region.  Both
of the lemma's displayed inequalities are instances — the componentwise one at
a component of the remainder, and its sum over `R` at the remainder itself.

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.baseline_one_insufficient
declarations.doc_string:
The threshold `3 ≤ δ` is necessary, not merely sufficient: at `δ = 1` a
vertex of internal degree exactly `1` is not deficient and contributes no
wedge, so the per-vertex clause reads `1 ≤ 0`.

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.baseline_two_insufficient
declarations.doc_string:
Likewise at `δ = 2`: a vertex of internal degree exactly `2` is not
deficient and contributes `C(2,2) = 1`, so the clause reads `2 ≤ 1`.

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.boundaryIncidence.eq_1

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) {order threshold : ℕ} {packing : Finset (Finset object.Vertex)},
  object.IsWindowPacking order packing →
    (∀ (vertex : object.Vertex), threshold ≤ object.degree vertex) →
      object.boundaryIncidence (object.remainderSupport packing) + 2 * (order - 1) * packing.card ≤
        threshold * (order * packing.card) + object.ambientSurplus (Graph.FiniteObject.windowSupport packing) threshold
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.boundaryIncidence_add_internal_mass_le
declarations.doc_string:
**`lem:surplus-aware-window-stub`, capacity half:**

`e(R,W) + 2(order − 1)·p ≤ δ·order·p + σ_W`,

the subtraction-free form of the manuscript's
`e(R,W) ≤ (δ·order − 2(order − 1))·p + σ_W`, which at its own presentation is
`e(R,W) ≤ 15p₁₃ + σ_W`: `δ·order` is its `39 = 13·3` and `2(order − 1)` its
`24 = 2·12`, twice the path edges of an induced copy.  Neither numeral appears.

This is the *cut* budget — invariant 23, the window stub capacity — stated
about `e(R,W)` alone, before any deficiency is compared to it.  The manuscript
counts it on the window side ("every `R`--`W` edge leaves some window") and
uses it on the remainder side; `boundaryIncidence_remainderSupport_eq` is that
step, the cut being one number counted from either end.

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) {packing : Finset (Finset object.Vertex)},
  ∑ vertex ∈ Graph.FiniteObject.windowSupport packing,
        object.internalDegree (Graph.FiniteObject.windowSupport packing) vertex ≤
      ∑ vertex ∈ Graph.FiniteObject.windowSupport packing, object.degree vertex →
    ¬∑ vertex ∈ Graph.FiniteObject.windowSupport packing, object.degree vertex -
              ∑ vertex ∈ Graph.FiniteObject.windowSupport packing,
                object.internalDegree (Graph.FiniteObject.windowSupport packing) vertex +
            ∑ vertex ∈ Graph.FiniteObject.windowSupport packing,
              object.internalDegree (Graph.FiniteObject.windowSupport packing) vertex =
          ∑ vertex ∈ Graph.FiniteObject.windowSupport packing, object.degree vertex →
      False
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.boundaryIncidence_add_internal_mass_le._proof_1_1

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) {order threshold : ℕ} {packing : Finset (Finset object.Vertex)},
  object.boundaryIncidence (object.remainderSupport packing) =
      object.boundaryIncidence (Graph.FiniteObject.windowSupport packing) →
    object.boundaryIncidence (Graph.FiniteObject.windowSupport packing) +
          ∑ vertex ∈ Graph.FiniteObject.windowSupport packing,
            object.internalDegree (Graph.FiniteObject.windowSupport packing) vertex =
        threshold * (order * packing.card) +
          object.ambientSurplus (Graph.FiniteObject.windowSupport packing) threshold →
      2 * (order - 1) * packing.card ≤
          ∑ vertex ∈ Graph.FiniteObject.windowSupport packing,
            object.internalDegree (Graph.FiniteObject.windowSupport packing) vertex →
        ¬object.boundaryIncidence (object.remainderSupport packing) + 2 * (order - 1) * packing.card ≤
              threshold * (order * packing.card) +
                object.ambientSurplus (Graph.FiniteObject.windowSupport packing) threshold →
          False
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.boundaryIncidence_add_internal_mass_le._proof_1_2

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (support : Finset object.Vertex),
  object.boundaryIncidence support =

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.boundaryIncidence_eq_sub
declarations.doc_string:
The boundary incidence of a support is its degree sum minus its internal
degree sum.  Truncated subtraction distributes because a vertex never has more
internal neighbours than neighbours.

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (support : Finset object.Vertex) (threshold internalMass : ℕ),
  (∀ (vertex : object.Vertex), threshold ≤ object.degree vertex) →
    internalMass ≤ ∑ vertex ∈ support, object.internalDegree support vertex →
      object.boundaryIncidence support ≤
        threshold * support.card + object.ambientSurplus support threshold - internalMass
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.boundaryIncidence_le_of_internal_mass
declarations.doc_string:
**`lem:surplus-aware-window-stub`, capacity half, in its reduced form.**

`e(W, R) ≤ δ·|W| + σ_W − (internal degree mass of the packing)`.

Read at the packed windows this is the manuscript's
`e(R,W) ≤ 15p₁₃ + σ_W`: the degree sum over `W` is `δ|W| + σ_W`, and every
incidence that stays inside a window is one that does not leave.  The
manuscript evaluates the internal mass as `2(order − 1)` per window -- twice
the path edges of an induced copy -- and `δ|W| = δ·order·p₁₃`, giving
`(δ·order − 2(order − 1))·p₁₃ + σ_W`, which at the registered presentation is
`15p₁₃ + σ_W`.  Neither numeral appears here.

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (packing : Finset (Finset object.Vertex)),
  object.boundaryIncidence (object.remainderSupport packing) =
    object.boundaryIncidence (Graph.FiniteObject.windowSupport packing)
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.boundaryIncidence_remainderSupport_eq
declarations.doc_string:
The incidences across the window/remainder cut are the same number counted

  object.internalDegree (object.remainderSupport packing) vertex +

      False
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.boundaryIncidence_remainderSupport_eq._proof_1_1

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (packing : Finset (Finset object.Vertex)) (vertex : object.Vertex),

region induces, as a duplicate-free index.  The ordering is

declarations.type:
{object : Graph.FiniteObject} →
  {Coordinate Chord : Type v} →
    object.DemandActivation Coordinate Chord →
      object.CarrierPresentation Coordinate Chord →
        ℕ → Finset (Finset object.Vertex) → Finset (object.Vertex × object.Vertex) → Option object.CapacityToken
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.capacityCharge
declarations.doc_string:
**`Θ_cap`**, the four-case canonical charge of `def:capacity-token-ledger`.
It is a function into `Option`, so it is single-valued by construction; `none` is
exactly the case in which no clause fires, which on a blocked pair with a defined
carrier does not happen.

declarations.type:
∀ {object : Graph.FiniteObject} {Coordinate Chord : Type v} (activation : object.DemandActivation Coordinate Chord)
  (presentation : object.CarrierPresentation Coordinate Chord) (threshold : ℕ) (packing : Finset (Finset object.Vertex))
  (pair : Finset (object.Vertex × object.Vertex)),
  Graph.FiniteObject.capacityCharge activation presentation threshold packing pair =
    match Graph.FiniteObject.windowJoinChoice activation presentation packing pair with
    | some incidence => some (Graph.FiniteObject.CapacityToken.boundaryWindow incidence)
    | none =>
      match Graph.FiniteObject.crossWindowChoice activation presentation packing pair with
      | some incidence => some (Graph.FiniteObject.CapacityToken.crossWindow incidence)
      | none =>
        match Graph.FiniteObject.remainderVertexChoice activation presentation threshold packing pair with
        | some vertex =>
          some
            (Graph.FiniteObject.CapacityToken.remainder
              (vertex, Graph.FiniteObject.remainderUnit activation presentation threshold packing vertex pair))
        | none =>
          match Graph.FiniteObject.canonicalBlocker activation pair with
          | none => none
          | some blocker =>
            Option.map Graph.FiniteObject.CapacityToken.primitive
              (Graph.FiniteObject.Blocker.carrier object threshold presentation.coordinateSupport presentation.chordPort
                blocker)
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.capacityCharge.eq_1

declarations.type:
{object : Graph.FiniteObject} →
  (motive : Option object.Vertex → Sort u_2) →

{object : Graph.FiniteObject} →
  (motive : Option (object.Vertex × object.Vertex) → Sort u_2) →
    (x : Option (object.Vertex × object.Vertex)) →

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.capacityCharge.match_3

declarations.type:
∀ {object : Graph.FiniteObject} {Coordinate Chord : Type v} (activation : object.DemandActivation Coordinate Chord)
  (presentation : object.CarrierPresentation Coordinate Chord) (threshold : ℕ) (packing : Finset (Finset object.Vertex))
  {pair : Finset (object.Vertex × object.Vertex)} {token : object.CapacityToken},
  Graph.FiniteObject.capacityCharge activation presentation threshold packing pair = some token →
    token ∈ object.capacityTokens threshold packing
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.capacityCharge_mem_capacityTokens
declarations.doc_string:
**`Θ_cap` lands in `𝔗_cap`.**  Each clause selects inside the family that
builds its own summand of the token universe: the two window incidence families,
the remainder surplus units — the modulus keeps the index inside the vertex's own
range — and `𝔘_sp(G)`.

declarations.type:
∀ {object : Graph.FiniteObject} (threshold : ℕ) (vertex : object.Vertex),
  threshold < object.degree vertex → ¬0 < object.degree vertex - threshold → False
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.capacityCharge_mem_capacityTokens._proof_1_3

declarations.type:
∀ {object : Graph.FiniteObject} {Coordinate Chord : Type u_2} (activation : object.DemandActivation Coordinate Chord)
  (presentation : object.CarrierPresentation Coordinate Chord) (threshold : ℕ) (packing : Finset (Finset object.Vertex))
  {pair : Finset (object.Vertex × object.Vertex)} (vertex : object.Vertex),

        (object.degree vertex - threshold) <
      object.degree vertex - threshold →

            Graph.FiniteObject.remainderRank activation presentation threshold packing vertex pair %
              (object.degree vertex - threshold) ≤
          object.degree vertex - threshold →

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) {threshold order : ℕ},
  (∀ (vertex : object.Vertex), threshold ≤ object.degree vertex) →
    3 ≤ threshold →
      0 < order →
        threshold * object.vertexCount ≤ 2 * object.edgeCount →
          object.edgeCount + 2 ≤ (threshold - 1) * object.vertexCount →
            threshold * order + 2 ≤ 4 * order → object.CapacityTokenLedgerStatement threshold order
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.capacityTokenLedgerStatement
declarations.doc_string:
**Nodes `[134]`--`[136]`, proved.**  Every clause is one of the theorems
above; nothing is assumed about the object beyond the standing baseline, the
registered `3 ≤ δ` and `0 < order`, and the handshake the baseline gives.

declarations.type: Graph.FiniteObject → ℕ → ℕ
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.capacityTokenSupply
declarations.doc_string:
**The manuscript's `8n`, at the registered baseline.**

`lem:capacity-token-supply`'s display is `|𝔗_cap| ≤ 8n + σ(G)`, and its `8n` is
`6n + 2n`: `lem:primitive-carrier-supply`'s own supply plus the internal window
mass `15p₁₃ < 2n`.  At the registered baseline the first summand is
`3(δ − 1)n` and the second is unchanged, so the manuscript's `8` is `3(δ−1)+2`
and no numeral is written.

  object.capacityTokenSupply threshold = object.primitiveCarrierSupply threshold + 2 * object.vertexCount

declarations.type: (object : Graph.FiniteObject) → ℕ → Finset (Finset object.Vertex) → Finset object.CapacityToken
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.capacityTokens
declarations.doc_string:
**`𝔗_cap = 𝔗_prim ⊔ 𝔗_R ⊔ 𝔗_W`**, as a finite set of capacity tokens.  The
four constructors are injective with disjoint ranges, so the union is the
manuscript's disjoint union and the count below is the sum of the four.

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (threshold : ℕ) (packing : Finset (Finset object.Vertex)),
  object.capacityTokens threshold packing =
    Finset.image Graph.FiniteObject.CapacityToken.boundaryWindow (object.windowRemainderIncidences packing) ∪
      (Finset.image Graph.FiniteObject.CapacityToken.crossWindow (object.crossWindowIncidences packing) ∪
        (Finset.image Graph.FiniteObject.CapacityToken.remainder (object.remainderSurplusTokens threshold packing) ∪
          Finset.image Graph.FiniteObject.CapacityToken.primitive (object.primitiveCarrier threshold)))
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.capacityTokens.eq_1

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (threshold : ℕ) (packing : Finset (Finset object.Vertex)) (vertex : object.Vertex),
  (object.capacityTokens threshold packing).Nonempty
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.capacityTokens_nonempty
declarations.doc_string:
**`𝔗_cap ≠ ∅`.**  The primitive summand contains the whole vertex set, so a
single vertex already makes the declared token order an order.

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (source : Finset object.Vertex) (target : object.Vertex → Finset object.Vertex),
  (source.biUnion fun vertex => Finset.image (fun other => (vertex, other)) (target vertex)).card =
    ∑ vertex ∈ source, (target vertex).card
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.card_biUnion_incidenceBlocks
declarations.doc_string:
The blocks of a vertex-indexed incidence family are disjoint, so the family
counts blockwise: each block is the vertex's own neighbour selection tagged with
that vertex.

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (threshold : ℕ) (packing : Finset (Finset object.Vertex)),
  (object.capacityTokens threshold packing).card =
    (object.windowRemainderIncidences packing).card +
      ((object.crossWindowIncidences packing).card +
        (object.ambientSurplus (object.remainderSupport packing) threshold + (object.primitiveCarrier threshold).card))
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.card_capacityTokens
declarations.doc_string:
**`|𝔗_cap| = |𝔘_sp(G)| + σ_R + e(R,W) + 2e_×(W)`**, the first display of
`lem:capacity-token-supply`: the four families are disjoint by their
constructors.

declarations.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [inst : DecidableEq β] {f : α → β} {s : Finset α} {b : β},
  (b ∈ Finset.image f s) = ∃ a ∈ s, f a = b
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.card_capacityTokens._simp_1_2

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.card_capacityTokens._simp_1_3

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) {order threshold : ℕ} {packing : Finset (Finset object.Vertex)},
  object.IsWindowPacking order packing →
    (∀ (vertex : object.Vertex), threshold ≤ object.degree vertex) →
      (object.capacityTokens threshold packing).card + 2 * (order - 1) * packing.card =
        (object.primitiveCarrier threshold).card + threshold * (order * packing.card) + object.degreeSurplus threshold
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.card_capacityTokens_add_internalMass
declarations.doc_string:
**`lem:capacity-token-supply`, the exact display**, in subtraction-free form:

  `|𝔗_cap| + 2(order − 1)p = |𝔘_sp(G)| + δ·order·p + σ(G)`,

which at the registered presentation `δ = 3`, `order = 13` is the manuscript's

  `|𝔗_cap| = |𝔘_sp(G)| + 15p₁₃ + σ(G)`.

The proof is the manuscript's: the four summands are disjoint, the window pair
`e(R,W) + 2e_×(W)` is `lem:exact-window-join-identity`, and
`σ_W + σ_R = σ(G)` is `def:window-remainder-surplus-split`.  Nothing is assumed
about the object beyond the standing baseline and the packing being one.

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) {order threshold : ℕ} {packing : Finset (Finset object.Vertex)},
  (object.capacityTokens threshold packing).card =
      (object.windowRemainderIncidences packing).card +
        ((object.crossWindowIncidences packing).card +
          (object.ambientSurplus (object.remainderSupport packing) threshold +
            (object.primitiveCarrier threshold).card)) →
    (object.windowRemainderIncidences packing).card +
          (2 * (order - 1) * packing.card + (object.crossWindowIncidences packing).card) =
        threshold * (order * packing.card) +
          object.ambientSurplus (Graph.FiniteObject.windowSupport packing) threshold →
      object.ambientSurplus (Graph.FiniteObject.windowSupport packing) threshold +
            object.ambientSurplus (object.remainderSupport packing) threshold =
          object.degreeSurplus threshold →
        ¬(object.capacityTokens threshold packing).card + 2 * (order - 1) * packing.card =
              (object.primitiveCarrier threshold).card + threshold * (order * packing.card) +
                object.degreeSurplus threshold →
          False
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.card_capacityTokens_add_internalMass._proof_1_1

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) {order threshold : ℕ} {packing : Finset (Finset object.Vertex)},
  object.IsWindowPacking order packing →
    (∀ (vertex : object.Vertex), threshold ≤ object.degree vertex) →
      3 ≤ threshold →
        threshold * object.vertexCount ≤ 2 * object.edgeCount →
          object.edgeCount + 2 ≤ (threshold - 1) * object.vertexCount →
            0 < order →
              threshold * order + 2 ≤ 4 * order →
                (object.capacityTokens threshold packing).card ≤
                  object.capacityTokenSupply threshold + object.degreeSurplus threshold
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.card_capacityTokens_le
declarations.doc_string:
**`lem:capacity-token-supply`, the displayed bound**:
`|𝔗_cap| ≤ (3(δ−1)+2)n + σ(G)`, the manuscript's `≤ 8n + σ(G)` at its own
`δ = 3`.

The manuscript's own two steps, both kept as antecedents rather than becoming
hypotheses about the object:

* `|𝔘_sp(G)| ≤ 3(δ−1)n` on the sparse upper envelope `m + 2 ≤ (δ−1)n`, which is
  `lem:primitive-carrier-supply`;
* `15p₁₃ < 2n`, which is `order·p ≤ n` -- derived here from the packing --
  together with the comparison `δ·order + 2 ≤ 4·order` between the two registered
  numbers, the manuscript's `15 ≤ 2·13`.

No numeral is written except as the coefficients of the envelopes that produce
it.

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) {order : ℕ} {threshold : ℕ} {packing : Finset (Finset object.Vertex)},
  0 < order → ¬order - 1 + 1 = order → False
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.card_capacityTokens_le._proof_1_2

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) {order threshold : ℕ} {packing : Finset (Finset object.Vertex)},
  (object.primitiveCarrier threshold).card ≤ object.primitiveCarrierSupply threshold →
    (object.capacityTokens threshold packing).card + 2 * (order - 1) * packing.card =
        (object.primitiveCarrier threshold).card + threshold * (order * packing.card) + object.degreeSurplus threshold →
      order * packing.card ≤ object.vertexCount →
        2 * (order - 1) * packing.card = 2 * ((order - 1) * packing.card) →
          (order - 1) * packing.card + packing.card = order * packing.card →
            threshold * (order * packing.card) + 2 * packing.card ≤ 4 * (order * packing.card) →
              ¬(object.capacityTokens threshold packing).card ≤
                    object.primitiveCarrierSupply threshold + 2 * object.vertexCount + object.degreeSurplus threshold →
                False
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.card_capacityTokens_le._proof_1_3

declarations.type:

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (support excluded : Finset object.Vertex) (threshold scale : ℕ),
  (∀ vertex ∈ support \ excluded, object.internalDegree support vertex ≤ threshold) →
    (∀ vertex ∈ support \ excluded,
        object.internalDegree support vertex = threshold →
          ∃ receiver,
            object.traceReceiver? support threshold vertex = some receiver ∧
              object.IsReceiver support threshold receiver ∧ receiver ∉ excluded) →
      (∀ receiver ∈ object.receivers support threshold \ excluded,
          1 + object.restrictedLoad support excluded threshold receiver ≤
            scale * object.missingPorts support threshold receiver) →
        (support \ excluded).card ≤
          ∑ vertex ∈ support \ excluded, scale * (threshold - object.internalDegree support vertex)

declarations.doc_string:
**The discharging calculation off an exceptional set.**

`Σ_{y ∉ H} ch(y) ≥ 0` on a support whose non-exceptional vertices are all at or
below the baseline, whose non-exceptional full vertices all route to
non-exceptional receivers, and whose non-exceptional receivers are all
unsaturated.  Written subtraction-free at the scale `s`.

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (support : Finset object.Vertex) (threshold : ℕ) (vertex : object.Vertex),

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (support excluded : Finset object.Vertex) (threshold scale : ℕ),
  (object.receivers support threshold \ excluded).card +
        {vertex ∈ support \ excluded | object.internalDegree support vertex = threshold}.card ≤
      ∑ receiver ∈ object.receivers support threshold \ excluded,
        scale * object.missingPorts support threshold receiver →
    {vertex ∈ support \ excluded | object.internalDegree support vertex = threshold}.card =
        {vertex ∈ support \ excluded | object.internalDegree support vertex = threshold}.card →
      (object.receivers support threshold \ excluded).card +
            {vertex ∈ support \ excluded | object.internalDegree support vertex = threshold}.card =
          (support \ excluded).card →
        ¬(support \ excluded).card ≤
              ∑ receiver ∈ object.receivers support threshold \ excluded,
                scale * object.missingPorts support threshold receiver →

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.card_le_scaled_deficiency_off._proof_1_6

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.card_localIncidences_le_of_degenerate
declarations.doc_string:
**A `k`-degenerate graph on `N ≥ k+1` vertices has at most `kN − C(k+1,2)`
edges**, in the subtraction-free doubled form the ordered incidences count:

  `|localIncidences| + k(k+1) ≤ 2kN`.

The proof is the degeneracy order itself: remove a vertex of induced degree at
most `k`, which drops the ordered incidence count by at most `2k`, until only
`k+1` vertices remain, where the count is at most `(k+1)k` because no vertex is
its own neighbour.

        (support.erase vertex).card + 1 = support.card → ¬bound + 1 ≤ (support.erase vertex).card → False
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.card_localIncidences_le_of_degenerate._proof_1_3

declarations.type:

declarations.doc_string:
**`lem:primitive-carrier-supply`, the identity**: `|𝔘_sp(G)| = n + 2m + σ(G)`.

three counts: the vertex count, the handshake, and
`lem:sparse-excess-port-extraction`.

declarations.type:

    3 ≤ threshold →

        object.edgeCount + 2 ≤ (threshold - 1) * object.vertexCount →
          (object.primitiveCarrier threshold).card ≤ object.primitiveCarrierSupply threshold

declarations.doc_string:
**`lem:primitive-carrier-supply`, the bound**: `|𝔘_sp(G)| ≤ 3(δ − 1)n` on the
sparse upper envelope, which at the manuscript's `δ = 3` is its `≤ 6n`.

`n + 2m + σ(G) = 4m − (δ − 1)n` at the registered baseline, and the envelope
`m + 2 ≤ (δ − 1)n` turns that into `3(δ − 1)n − 8`.  Both the envelope and the
baseline's `3 ≤ δ` are hypotheses; nothing about the object is assumed here.

declarations.type: ∀ {object : Graph.FiniteObject} {threshold : ℕ}, 3 ≤ threshold → ¬threshold - 1 + 1 = threshold → False
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.card_primitiveCarrier_le._proof_1_2

      ∀ (room : ℕ),
        threshold * object.vertexCount = room + object.vertexCount →
          object.edgeCount + 2 ≤ room →
            (threshold - 1) * object.vertexCount = room →
              ¬object.vertexCount + 2 * object.edgeCount + object.degreeSurplus threshold ≤ 3 * room → False

declarations.doc_string:

an edge-incidence blocker carries a genuine incidence, and the chord clause
selects inside the excess selector by construction.

∀ {object : Graph.FiniteObject} {Coordinate Chord : Type u_2} {activation : object.DemandActivation Coordinate Chord}
  {threshold : ℕ} {coordinateSupport : Coordinate → Finset object.Vertex}
  {chordPort : Chord → object.Vertex × object.Vertex} {pair : Finset (object.Vertex × object.Vertex)}
  {item : object.Vertex ⊕ object.Vertex × object.Vertex ⊕ object.Vertex × object.Vertex}
  (motive :
    (blocker : object.Blocker Coordinate Chord) →
      blocker ∈ activation.blockers pair →
        Graph.FiniteObject.Blocker.carrier object threshold coordinateSupport chordPort blocker = some item → Prop)
  (blocker : object.Blocker Coordinate Chord) (member : blocker ∈ activation.blockers pair)
  (selected : Graph.FiniteObject.Blocker.carrier object threshold coordinateSupport chordPort blocker = some item),
  (∀ (vertex : object.Vertex)
      (x :
        Graph.FiniteObject.Blocker.sharedDeclaredSupport (Graph.FiniteObject.CarrierItem.vertex vertex) ∈
          activation.blockers pair)
      (selected :
        Graph.FiniteObject.Blocker.carrier object threshold coordinateSupport chordPort
            (Graph.FiniteObject.Blocker.sharedDeclaredSupport (Graph.FiniteObject.CarrierItem.vertex vertex)) =
          some item),
      motive (Graph.FiniteObject.Blocker.sharedDeclaredSupport (Graph.FiniteObject.CarrierItem.vertex vertex)) x
        selected) →
    (∀ (incidence : object.Vertex × object.Vertex)
        (member :
          Graph.FiniteObject.Blocker.sharedDeclaredSupport (Graph.FiniteObject.CarrierItem.incidence incidence) ∈
            activation.blockers pair)
        (selected :
          Graph.FiniteObject.Blocker.carrier object threshold coordinateSupport chordPort
              (Graph.FiniteObject.Blocker.sharedDeclaredSupport (Graph.FiniteObject.CarrierItem.incidence incidence)) =
            some item),
        motive (Graph.FiniteObject.Blocker.sharedDeclaredSupport (Graph.FiniteObject.CarrierItem.incidence incidence))
          member selected) →
      (∀ (vertex : object.Vertex)
          (x :
            Graph.FiniteObject.Blocker.sharedReturnSupport (Graph.FiniteObject.CarrierItem.vertex vertex) ∈
              activation.blockers pair)
          (selected :
            Graph.FiniteObject.Blocker.carrier object threshold coordinateSupport chordPort
                (Graph.FiniteObject.Blocker.sharedReturnSupport (Graph.FiniteObject.CarrierItem.vertex vertex)) =
              some item),
          motive (Graph.FiniteObject.Blocker.sharedReturnSupport (Graph.FiniteObject.CarrierItem.vertex vertex)) x
            selected) →
        (∀ (incidence : object.Vertex × object.Vertex)
            (member :
              Graph.FiniteObject.Blocker.sharedReturnSupport (Graph.FiniteObject.CarrierItem.incidence incidence) ∈
                activation.blockers pair)
            (selected :
              Graph.FiniteObject.Blocker.carrier object threshold coordinateSupport chordPort
                  (Graph.FiniteObject.Blocker.sharedReturnSupport
                    (Graph.FiniteObject.CarrierItem.incidence incidence)) =
                some item),
            motive (Graph.FiniteObject.Blocker.sharedReturnSupport (Graph.FiniteObject.CarrierItem.incidence incidence))
              member selected) →
          (∀ (vertex : object.Vertex)
              (x : Graph.FiniteObject.Blocker.sharedLocalBuffer vertex ∈ activation.blockers pair)
              (selected :
                Graph.FiniteObject.Blocker.carrier object threshold coordinateSupport chordPort
                    (Graph.FiniteObject.Blocker.sharedLocalBuffer vertex) =
                  some item),
              motive (Graph.FiniteObject.Blocker.sharedLocalBuffer vertex) x selected) →
            (∀ (coordinate : Coordinate)
                (x : Graph.FiniteObject.Blocker.boundaryProfile coordinate ∈ activation.blockers pair)
                (selected :
                  Graph.FiniteObject.Blocker.carrier object threshold coordinateSupport chordPort
                      (Graph.FiniteObject.Blocker.boundaryProfile coordinate) =
                    some item),
                motive (Graph.FiniteObject.Blocker.boundaryProfile coordinate) x selected) →
              (∀ (coordinate : Coordinate)
                  (x : Graph.FiniteObject.Blocker.targetResponse coordinate ∈ activation.blockers pair)
                  (selected :
                    Graph.FiniteObject.Blocker.carrier object threshold coordinateSupport chordPort
                        (Graph.FiniteObject.Blocker.targetResponse coordinate) =
                      some item),
                  motive (Graph.FiniteObject.Blocker.targetResponse coordinate) x selected) →
                (∀ (chords : Finset Chord)
                    (x : Graph.FiniteObject.Blocker.arithmeticChordSet chords ∈ activation.blockers pair)
                    (selected :
                      Graph.FiniteObject.Blocker.carrier object threshold coordinateSupport chordPort
                          (Graph.FiniteObject.Blocker.arithmeticChordSet chords) =
                        some item),
                    motive (Graph.FiniteObject.Blocker.arithmeticChordSet chords) x selected) →

declarations.doc_string:
**The blocks of a vertex-indexed selection**, as ordered pairs
`(centre, selected)`.

A selection names, at each vertex, a list of other vertices; the family it
generates is indexed by its centre, so distinct centres contribute disjoint
blocks.  That is the only structure the counting below uses, and it is what both
the excess selector `𝒫_exc` and the edge-incidence family `I_E(G)` are.

declarations.type:

  object.centreBlocks selection =
    Finset.univ.biUnion fun centre => Finset.image (fun endpoint => (centre, endpoint)) (selection centre).toFinset

declarations.doc_string:

blocker has a primitive carrier is charged, so the fibre identity above is read at
the whole blocked family — which is what makes `|Π_blk| = Σ_t ℓ_cap(t)` the
manuscript's display rather than a statement about a subfamily.

  (∀ pair ∈ object.portPairSchedule threshold, ∃ label ∈ order, Applies label pair) →
    object.chargedPairs threshold order Applies decidable = object.portPairSchedule threshold

declarations.doc_string:
**A total assignment charges every pair.**

`Θ_cap` is total on the family it is defined on -- its last case is the
primitive carrier `κ(B_π)`, which is always available -- so the token ledger's
identity is read at the whole family rather than at the part some token happens
to cover.

declarations.doc_string:
Contract the ordered edge `(tail, head)`: delete `head` and transplant its
incidences onto `tail`.  The irreflexivity guard of `SimpleGraph.fromRel` is
what discards the contracted edge itself.

declarations.type:

            object.graph.Adj ↑left ↑right ∨ ↑left = tail ∧ object.graph.Adj head ↑right).Adj
        left right) =
    Decidable
      (left ≠ right ∧
        ((object.graph.Adj ↑left ↑right ∨ ↑left = tail ∧ object.graph.Adj head ↑right) ∨
          object.graph.Adj ↑right ↑left ∨ ↑right = tail ∧ object.graph.Adj head ↑left))

declarations.doc_string:
**Case (b)**: the least cross-window edge contained in `supp(B_π)`, taken at
the least of its two window ends.  The cross-window family carries an entry at
each end, so the least entry of the candidate set is the least endpoint token of
the least such edge.

declarations.type:
∀ {object : Graph.FiniteObject} {Coordinate Chord : Type v} (activation : object.DemandActivation Coordinate Chord)
  (presentation : object.CarrierPresentation Coordinate Chord) (packing : Finset (Finset object.Vertex))
  (pair : Finset (object.Vertex × object.Vertex)),
  Graph.FiniteObject.crossWindowChoice activation presentation packing pair =
    {incidence ∈ object.crossWindowIncidences packing |
          incidence.1 ∈ Graph.FiniteObject.chargeSupport activation presentation pair ∧
            incidence.2 ∈ Graph.FiniteObject.chargeSupport activation presentation pair}.toList.head?
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.crossWindowChoice.eq_1

declarations.type: (object : Graph.FiniteObject) → Finset (Finset object.Vertex) → Finset (object.Vertex × object.Vertex)
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.crossWindowIncidences
declarations.doc_string:
**`2e_×(W)` as a family.**  The ordered adjacent pairs whose two ends lie in
*distinct* packed windows: `(v, w)` with `v` in a packed window and `w` in a
different one.  A cross-window edge contributes one pair at each of its two
window ends.

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (packing : Finset (Finset object.Vertex)),
  object.crossWindowIncidences packing =
    packing.biUnion fun member =>
      member.biUnion fun vertex =>
        Finset.image (fun other => (vertex, other))
          (object.graph.neighborFinset vertex ∩ object.windowSupportOutside packing member)
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.crossWindowIncidences.eq_1

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) {threshold : ℕ},
  3 ≤ threshold →
    (∀ (subgraph : Graph.ProperSubgraph object), ¬Graph.MinimumDegreeAtLeast threshold subgraph.value) →
      (∀ (dart : object.graph.Dart),
          object.degree dart.toProd.1 = threshold ∨ object.degree dart.toProd.2 = threshold) →
        0 < object.edgeCount → object.edgeCount + 2 ≤ (threshold - 1) * object.vertexCount
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.edgeCount_add_two_le
declarations.doc_string:
**`lem:sparse-upper-envelope` as the branch reads it.**

The tight endpoint is not assumed: the branch's own positive surplus exhibits an
edge, and `lem:deletion-critical` puts one of its two ends exactly at the
baseline.

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) {threshold : ℕ},
  3 ≤ threshold →
    (∀ (subgraph : Graph.ProperSubgraph object), ¬Graph.MinimumDegreeAtLeast threshold subgraph.value) →
      ∀ {tight : object.Vertex},
        object.degree tight = threshold → object.edgeCount + 2 ≤ (threshold - 1) * object.vertexCount
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.edgeCount_add_two_le_of_noProperBaseline
declarations.doc_string:
**`lem:sparse-upper-envelope` at the registered baseline.**

`m + 2 ≤ (δ − 1)·n`, the manuscript's `m ≤ 2n − 2` at `δ = 3`.

The two hypotheses are the two facts the manuscript spends and the branch has
already committed: no proper subgraph meets the baseline, and some vertex sits
exactly at it.  Nothing else about the object is used.

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) {threshold : ℕ},
  3 ≤ threshold → ∀ {tight : object.Vertex}, object.degree tight = threshold → ¬threshold = threshold - 1 + 1 → False
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.edgeCount_add_two_le_of_noProperBaseline._proof_1_1

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) {threshold : ℕ} {tight : object.Vertex},
  (object.vertexFinset.erase tight).card + 1 = object.vertexCount →
    ∀ (inner : Finset object.Vertex),
      inner.card ≤ (object.vertexFinset.erase tight).card → ¬inner.card < object.vertexCount → False
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.edgeCount_add_two_le_of_noProperBaseline._proof_1_2

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) {threshold : ℕ} {tight : object.Vertex},
  object.degree tight = threshold →
    threshold = threshold - 1 + 1 →
      ∀ (inner : Finset object.Vertex) (minimal : (object.induce inner).Vertex),
        object.localDegree inner ↑minimal = (object.induce inner).minDegree →
          ¬threshold ≤ (object.induce inner).minDegree → ¬object.localDegree inner ↑minimal ≤ threshold - 1 → False
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.edgeCount_add_two_le_of_noProperBaseline._proof_1_3

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) {threshold : ℕ} {tight : object.Vertex},
  threshold - 1 + 1 + 1 ≤ object.vertexCount →
    (object.vertexFinset.erase tight).card + 1 = object.vertexCount →
      ¬threshold - 1 + 1 ≤ (object.vertexFinset.erase tight).card → False
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.edgeCount_add_two_le_of_noProperBaseline._proof_1_4

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) {threshold : ℕ},
  3 ≤ threshold →
    ∀ {tight : object.Vertex},
      object.degree tight = threshold → threshold = threshold - 1 + 1 → ¬2 ≤ threshold - 1 → False
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.edgeCount_add_two_le_of_noProperBaseline._proof_1_5

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) {threshold : ℕ},
  3 ≤ threshold →
    ∀ {tight : object.Vertex},
      object.degree tight = threshold → threshold = threshold - 1 + 1 → ¬3 ≤ threshold - 1 + 1 → False
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.edgeCount_add_two_le_of_noProperBaseline._proof_1_6

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) {threshold : ℕ} {tight : object.Vertex},
  2 * object.edgeCount = (object.localIncidences (object.vertexFinset.erase tight)).card + 2 * (threshold - 1 + 1) →
    ∀ (cost : ℕ),
      6 ≤ cost →
        (threshold - 1) * (threshold - 1 + 1) = cost →
          ∀ (inner : ℕ),
            (object.localIncidences (object.vertexFinset.erase tight)).card + cost ≤ inner →
              2 * (threshold - 1) * (object.vertexFinset.erase tight).card = inner →
                ∀ (whole : ℕ),
                  inner + 2 * (threshold - 1) = 2 * whole →
                    (threshold - 1) * object.vertexCount = whole → ¬object.edgeCount + 2 ≤ whole → False
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.edgeCount_add_two_le_of_noProperBaseline._proof_1_7

declarations.type: (object : Graph.FiniteObject) → DecidableEq object.Vertex
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.envelopeVertexDecEq
declarations.doc_string: The object's declared vertex equality, as an instance for this module.

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) {order threshold : ℕ} {packing : Finset (Finset object.Vertex)},
  object.IsWindowPacking order packing →
    (∀ (vertex : object.Vertex), threshold ≤ object.degree vertex) →
      (object.windowRemainderIncidences packing).card +
          (2 * (order - 1) * packing.card + (object.crossWindowIncidences packing).card) =
        threshold * (order * packing.card) + object.ambientSurplus (Graph.FiniteObject.windowSupport packing) threshold
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.exact_window_join_identity
declarations.doc_string:
**`lem:exact-window-join-identity`**, in subtraction-free form:

  `e(R,W) + 2(order − 1)p + 2e_×(W) = δ·order·p + σ_W`,

which at the registered presentation `δ = 3`, `order = 13` is the manuscript's

  `e(R,W) + 2e_×(W) = 15p₁₃ + σ_W`,

`15` being `δ·order − 2(order − 1) = 39 − 24`.  The proof is the manuscript's:
sum degrees over the covered support, which is `δ|W| + σ_W` because every vertex
is at the baseline; the same sum counts each internal incidence once from its own
end and each leaving incidence once, and the internal ones are exactly the path
incidences of the packed windows together with the cross-window incidences.

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) {packing : Finset (Finset object.Vertex)},
  ∑ vertex ∈ Graph.FiniteObject.windowSupport packing,
        object.internalDegree (Graph.FiniteObject.windowSupport packing) vertex ≤
      ∑ vertex ∈ Graph.FiniteObject.windowSupport packing, object.degree vertex →
    ¬∑ vertex ∈ Graph.FiniteObject.windowSupport packing, object.degree vertex -
              ∑ vertex ∈ Graph.FiniteObject.windowSupport packing,
                object.internalDegree (Graph.FiniteObject.windowSupport packing) vertex +
            ∑ vertex ∈ Graph.FiniteObject.windowSupport packing,
              object.internalDegree (Graph.FiniteObject.windowSupport packing) vertex =
          ∑ vertex ∈ Graph.FiniteObject.windowSupport packing, object.degree vertex →
      False
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.exact_window_join_identity._proof_1_1

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) {order threshold : ℕ} {packing : Finset (Finset object.Vertex)},
  (object.windowRemainderIncidences packing).card =
      object.boundaryIncidence (Graph.FiniteObject.windowSupport packing) →
    object.boundaryIncidence (Graph.FiniteObject.windowSupport packing) +
          ∑ vertex ∈ Graph.FiniteObject.windowSupport packing,
            object.internalDegree (Graph.FiniteObject.windowSupport packing) vertex =
        threshold * (order * packing.card) +
          object.ambientSurplus (Graph.FiniteObject.windowSupport packing) threshold →
      ∑ vertex ∈ Graph.FiniteObject.windowSupport packing,
            object.internalDegree (Graph.FiniteObject.windowSupport packing) vertex =
          2 * (order - 1) * packing.card + (object.crossWindowIncidences packing).card →
        ¬(object.windowRemainderIncidences packing).card +
                (2 * (order - 1) * packing.card + (object.crossWindowIncidences packing).card) =
              threshold * (order * packing.card) +
                object.ambientSurplus (Graph.FiniteObject.windowSupport packing) threshold →
          False
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.exact_window_join_identity._proof_1_2

declarations.type: (object : Graph.FiniteObject) → ℕ → Finset (object.Vertex × object.Vertex)

**`𝒫_exc` of `def:surplus-ports`**, as ordered pairs `(c(p), x(p))`: the
blocks of the per-centre excess selection.
