declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (support : Finset object.Vertex) (threshold dischargeScale : ℕ),
  object.NegativeNetCharge support threshold dischargeScale →
    ∃ piece ∈ object.canonicalPieces support,
      object.NegativeNetCharge (object.pieceSupport support piece) threshold dischargeScale
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.exists_canonicalPiece_negativeNetCharge
declarations.doc_string:
**`prop:negative-net-charge`, with the canonical index retained.**  A
region of negative net charge has one of its actual canonical connected
components of negative net charge.  Retaining the component is essential for
later refinements: its vertex support can be recovered definitionally, whereas
an arbitrary connected subset cannot be promoted back to the canonical
decomposition.

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (support : Finset object.Vertex) (threshold dischargeScale : ℕ),
  object.NegativeNetCharge support threshold dischargeScale →
    ∃ piece ⊆ support,
      Graph.SupportComponents.Connected.ConnectedOn object piece ∧
        object.NegativeNetCharge piece threshold dischargeScale
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.exists_connected_negativeNetCharge
declarations.doc_string:
**`prop:negative-net-charge`.**  A region of negative net charge has a
connected piece of negative net charge.

The manuscript's proof verbatim: if every piece were nonnegative their sum
could not be negative.  What the statement returns is a *connected* subset of
the region — `SupportComponents.Connected.ConnectedOn` is the walk-based
connectivity of `def:admissible`'s "connected remainder piece", and the piece
is nonempty because it is a component of the order.

declarations.type: ∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject), 0 < object.edgeCount → Nonempty object.graph.Dart
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.exists_dart_of_edgeCount_pos
declarations.doc_string: A positive edge count exhibits an oriented edge, and with it a vertex.

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) {order : ℕ},
  0 < order →
    ∀ {packing : Finset (Finset object.Vertex)},
      object.IsWindowPacking order packing →
        packing.card = object.windowPackingNumber order →
          ∀ {support : Finset object.Vertex},
            object.InducesWindow order support → ∃ member ∈ packing, ¬Disjoint support member
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.exists_mem_not_disjoint_of_card_eq
declarations.doc_string:
**Maximality.**  A packing of maximum cardinality meets every window: an
unchosen window disjoint from all of its members could be added, and the
enlarged family would be a valid packing of strictly greater cardinality.

This is the manuscript's "every unchosen induced window overlaps a chosen
one", derived rather than assumed.

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) {order : ℕ} {packing : Finset (Finset object.Vertex)},
  packing.card = object.windowPackingNumber order →
    ∀ {support : Finset object.Vertex},
      (insert support packing).card = packing.card + 1 →
        (insert support packing).card ≤ object.windowPackingNumber order → False
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.exists_mem_not_disjoint_of_card_eq._proof_1_1

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (support : Finset object.Vertex) (threshold : ℕ),
  (∀ inner ⊆ support, ¬Graph.MinimumDegreeAtLeast threshold (object.induce inner)) →
    ∀ {source : object.Vertex},
      source ∈ support →
        threshold ≤ object.internalDegree support source → ∃ target, object.TraceTo support threshold source target
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.exists_traceTo_of_no_baseline_subsupport
declarations.doc_string:
**Every full vertex of the support traces to a receiver.**

Suppose not.  The vertices reachable from the source through full vertices then
have all of their internal neighbours full and again reachable — a neighbour of
lower internal degree would be a receiver, and the walk extended by that edge,
shortened to a path, would be a trace.  So that region spends the whole baseline
inside itself, and it is a subregion of the support meeting the baseline, which
the hypothesis denies.

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (order : ℕ),
  ∃ packing, object.IsWindowPacking order packing ∧ packing.card = object.windowPackingNumber order
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.exists_windowPacking_card_eq
declarations.doc_string: Some valid packing attains the packing number.

declarations.type:
(object : Graph.FiniteObject) →
  ℕ →

declarations.type: (object : Graph.FiniteObject) → Finset object.Vertex → ℕ → Finset object.Vertex

that induces one.

declarations.type: (object : Graph.FiniteObject) → Finset object.Vertex → object.Vertex → ℕ

declarations.doc_string: The number of neighbours a vertex has inside a support.

declarations.type:

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.internalDegree_add_internalDegree_compl
declarations.doc_string: A vertex's neighbours split between a support and its complement.

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) {packing : Finset (Finset object.Vertex)} {member : Finset object.Vertex},
  member ∈ packing →
    ∀ (vertex : object.Vertex),
      object.internalDegree member vertex + object.internalDegree (object.windowSupportOutside packing member) vertex =
        object.internalDegree (Graph.FiniteObject.windowSupport packing) vertex
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.internalDegree_add_internalDegree_windowSupportOutside
declarations.doc_string:
**Inside one window, or across to another.**  A packed window's vertex has
its `W`-internal neighbours split between the window itself and the rest of the
covered support; there is no third possibility.

declarations.type: ∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {a : α} {s₁ s₂ : Finset α}, (a ∈ s₁ ∩ s₂) = (a ∈ s₁ ∧ a ∈ s₂)
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.internalDegree_add_internalDegree_windowSupportOutside._simp_1_1

declarations.type: ∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {s t : Finset α} {a : α}, (a ∈ s \ t) = (a ∈ s ∧ a ∉ t)
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.internalDegree_add_internalDegree_windowSupportOutside._simp_1_7

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) {member : Finset object.Vertex} (vertex : object.Vertex) (this : FinEnum object.Vertex)
  (this_1 : DecidableRel object.graph.Adj) (other : object.Vertex)
  (motive : other ∈ object.graph.neighborFinset vertex ∧ other ∈ member → Prop)

declarations.type:

  (other : object.Vertex)

    (other ∈ object.graph.neighborFinset vertex ∧ other ∈ Graph.FiniteObject.windowSupport packing) ∧ other ∈ member →
      Prop)

    (other ∈ object.graph.neighborFinset vertex ∧ other ∈ Graph.FiniteObject.windowSupport packing) ∧ other ∈ member),

  object.internalDegree support vertex ≤ object.degree vertex
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.internalDegree_le_degree
declarations.doc_string: A vertex has no more neighbours inside a support than it has overall.

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.internalDegree_mono
declarations.doc_string: Enlarging the support cannot lose an internal neighbour.

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (support : Finset object.Vertex)

**`d_{X_i}(u) = d_R(u)`.**  Inside a connected component, a vertex's
neighbours in the component are exactly its neighbours in the whole region: a
neighbour that stays in the region is joined to it by an edge of the induced
graph, so it lies in the same component.

The neighbours a vertex has inside a support.  Its cardinality is
`internalDegree`, which is how it is defined.

declarations.type: (object : Graph.FiniteObject) → Finset object.Vertex → ℕ

**`W₂(X)`.**  The internal length-two wedges of a region: `C(d_X(v), 2)`
summed over the region, where `d_X` counts only neighbours inside `X`.

∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (support : Finset object.Vertex),

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.internalWedgeCount.eq_1

declarations.type: (object : Graph.FiniteObject) → (support : Finset object.Vertex) → Finset (object.InternalWedge support)
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.internalWedgeFamily
declarations.doc_string:
**`𝒲₂(X)`**: the exact finite family of raw internal curvature tests of a
region.

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.internalWedgeFamily.eq_1

declarations.type:

  (object.internalWedgeFamily support).card = object.internalWedgeCount support

The family has exactly as many members as the count counts: `|𝒲₂(X)| =
W₂(X)`.  This is what lets a rank taken over the family be compared with the
wedge lower bound proved for the count.

declarations.type: {object : Graph.FiniteObject} → {region : Finset object.Vertex} → object.InternalWedge region → Finset object.Vertex
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.internalWedgeSupport

The declared support of a raw internal curvature test: the wedge's centre
together with the two neighbours it joins (`def:declared-coordinate-signature`,
clause (D4) — a raw curvature coordinate is indexed by its internal length-two
wedge, and its support is that wedge).

**The internal degree mass of the whole packing.**

The packed windows are pairwise disjoint, so the mass on `W` is at least the
sum of the masses each window already carries inside itself.

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.isomorphic_refl

declarations.type:

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.le_minDegree_of_forall_le_degree

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.lexicographicSize

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.lexicographicSize.eq_1

Isomorphic packed graphs have exactly the same progress measure, even
when their hidden vertex types and execution schedules differ.

Replacing the right graph by an isomorphic representation does not change
whether a strict reduction holds.

∀ {smaller : Graph.FiniteObject} {larger : Graph.FiniteObject},

    smaller.vertexCount < larger.vertexCount ∨
      smaller.vertexCount = larger.vertexCount ∧ smaller.edgeCount < larger.edgeCount

declarations.doc_string: Fewer vertices always give strict graph progress.

declarations.type: (object : Graph.FiniteObject) → Finset object.Vertex → object.Vertex → ℕ

The number of neighbours a vertex has inside an explicit support: the degree
of the induced restriction, read on the ambient object.

declarations.doc_string:
**`q(w)`.**  The ports a receiver still has leaving the support: the
baseline less what it spends inside.  On a support whose vertices sit exactly at
the baseline this is the number of ambient edges from the vertex to the
complement.

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) {Baseline : Graph.FiniteObject → Prop} {LengthOK : ℕ → Prop}
  {baselineDegree order deficitScale : ℕ} {Coordinate Chord : Type u},
  2 ≤ baselineDegree →
    Graph.cubicBaselineEdgeCount object.vertexCount baselineDegree ≤ object.edgeCount →
      ∀ (baseline : object.BaselineWindowDemand Baseline LengthOK baselineDegree order deficitScale)
        (activation : object.DemandActivation Coordinate Chord),
        Core.TargetRank.targetRank
              (Graph.FiniteObject.declaredQuotientSystem Baseline (Graph.HasCycleWithLength LengthOK) object
                (object.mixedTargetFamily baseline.bits (Graph.FiniteObject.windowSupport baseline.packing)
                  (activation.pairFamily (activation.freePairs baselineDegree)))
                object.mixedTargetSupport) =
            (object.mixedTargetFamily baseline.bits (Graph.FiniteObject.windowSupport baseline.packing)
                (activation.pairFamily (activation.freePairs baselineDegree))).card →
          object.MixedSpinePairDemand Baseline LengthOK baselineDegree order deficitScale baseline activation

declarations.doc_string:

and the exit-free facts already present on the incoming residual.  The entropy
inequality is the package's positive node-`[21]` arm; the sandwich is then the
paper's exact cancellation argument.

    0 < threshold →
      2 * (windowOrder - 1) ≤ threshold * windowOrder →
        Graph.FiniteObject.netCapWindowCost threshold dischargeScale windowOrder * threshold < 2 * windowRate →
          Graph.FiniteObject.SufficientlyLargeForNetCap threshold dischargeScale windowOrder windowRate surplusScale
              size →
            2 * (windowRate * size.log2 * packingCard) ≤
                (size.log2 + 1) * (threshold * size + surplusScale * Core.ceilSqrt size) →
              windowOrder * packingCard + support.card = size →
                object.positiveDeficiency support threshold + 2 * (windowOrder - 1) * packingCard ≤
                    threshold * (windowOrder * packingCard) + surplusScale * Core.ceilSqrt size →
                  object.NegativeNetCharge support threshold dischargeScale

      object.NegativeNetCharge support threshold dischargeScale
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.negativeNetCharge_of_stubSupply_of_strictCap
declarations.doc_string:
**The exact finite net-cap implication.**

Suppose the positive deficiency of a support is paid by a boundary capacity
after adding a common debit, and suppose that capacity is strictly below the
support size after both sides are scaled and the same debit is restored.  Then
the support has negative net charge.

For the packed-window remainder, instantiate

* `debit = 2 * (order - 1) * packing.card`,
* `capacity = threshold * (order * packing.card) + slack`.

The first hypothesis is the exact finite form of `lem:stub-positive`; the
second is the cleared-denominator form of the strict quarter-cap.  The proof is
only multiplication and cancellation, so no asymptotic notation or rounding
enters.

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (support : Finset object.Vertex) (threshold dischargeScale debit capacity : ℕ),
  dischargeScale * capacity < dischargeScale * debit + support.card →
    dischargeScale * object.positiveDeficiency support threshold + dischargeScale * debit ≤ dischargeScale * capacity →
      ¬dischargeScale * object.positiveDeficiency support threshold <
            support.card + dischargeScale * object.ambientSurplus support threshold →
        False
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.negativeNetCharge_of_stubSupply_of_strictCap._proof_1_1

`e(R,W) ≤ 15p₁₃ + σ_W ≤ 15p₁₃ + σ(G)`, "since the windows are vertex-disjoint
and surplus is nonnegative".  It is the form that a registered ceiling on
`σ(G)` can be spent against: the manuscript spends `def:near-cubic-spine`'s
`σ(G) = O(√n) = o(n)` and reads off `def⁺(R) ≤ 15p₁₃ + o(n)`, and a spine
carrying an exact ceiling on `σ(G)` reads off the exact analogue.

`def⁺(R) ≤ e(R, W)`.

The manuscript's argument verbatim: on the standing baseline every vertex of
the remainder already has ambient degree at least `δ`, so it is deficient
*inside* the remainder only because some of its incidences leave.  Writing
`d_G(v) = d_R(v) + e_v` gives `max{0, δ − d_R(v)} ≤ e_v` pointwise, and summing
over the remainder gives the claim.

No near-cubic hypothesis is used, exactly as the manuscript notes.

∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (support : Finset object.Vertex) (threshold : ℕ),
  object.receivers support threshold = {vertex ∈ support | object.internalDegree support vertex < threshold}
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.receivers.eq_1
Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.receivers_eq_filter_not
declarations.doc_string:
**A support of zero assigned surplus has no vertex above the baseline
inside it.**  Every vertex of it that is not full is a receiver, so the two
finsets are complementary in the support.

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (support : Finset object.Vertex) (threshold : ℕ) (vertex : object.Vertex),
  object.internalDegree support vertex < threshold → object.internalDegree support vertex = threshold → False

declarations.type:
∀ {object : Graph.FiniteObject} {support : Finset object.Vertex} {threshold : ℕ} {vertex : object.Vertex},

declarations.type: ∀ {α : Type u_1} {p : α → Prop} [inst : DecidablePred p] {s : Finset α} {a : α}, (a ∈ Finset.filter p s) = (a ∈ s ∧ p a)
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.receivers_eq_filter_not._simp_1_3

declarations.type:
{object : Graph.FiniteObject} →

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.remainderCohort

**`𝒫_v`**: the pairs for which the first two cases fail and whose least
high-degree remainder vertex is `v`.

declarations.type:
{object : Graph.FiniteObject} →
  {Coordinate Chord : Type v} →
    object.DemandActivation Coordinate Chord →

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.remainderRank
declarations.doc_string: **`rk_v(π)`**: the rank of `π` in `𝒫_v` under the canonical pair order.

declarations.type: (object : Graph.FiniteObject) → Finset (Finset object.Vertex) → Finset object.Vertex
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.remainderSupport
declarations.doc_string: `R = G − W`: the vertices the packing leaves uncovered.

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (packing : Finset (Finset object.Vertex)),
  object.remainderSupport packing = Finset.univ \ Graph.FiniteObject.windowSupport packing
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.remainderSupport.eq_1

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) {order : ℕ} {packing : Finset (Finset object.Vertex)},
  object.IsWindowPacking order packing →
    (object.remainderSupport packing).card + order * packing.card = object.vertexCount
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.remainderSupport_card_add_eq
declarations.doc_string:
`|R| + order·p = n` at a packing: the two counts above, composed.  This is
the form nodes `[55]`--`[56]` compare the packing density against.

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (packing : Finset (Finset object.Vertex)),
  (object.remainderSupport packing).card + (Graph.FiniteObject.windowSupport packing).card = object.vertexCount
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.remainderSupport_card_add_windowSupport_card
declarations.doc_string:
`|R| + |W| = n`: the remainder is the complement of the covered support, so
the two counts exhaust the object.  This is the manuscript's
`|R| = n − 13p₁₃`, written without subtraction.

declarations.type: (object : Graph.FiniteObject) → ℕ → Finset (Finset object.Vertex) → Finset (object.Vertex × ℕ)
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.remainderSurplusTokens
declarations.doc_string:
**`𝔗_R = {(v,j) : v ∈ R, 1 ≤ j ≤ d_G(v) − δ}`**: one token per surplus unit
carried by a remainder vertex.  A remainder vertex at the baseline contributes
none, which is why the count is the remainder's own surplus.

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (threshold : ℕ) (packing : Finset (Finset object.Vertex)),
  object.remainderSurplusTokens threshold packing =
    (object.remainderSupport packing).biUnion fun vertex =>
      Finset.image (fun index => (vertex, index)) (Finset.Icc 1 (object.degree vertex - threshold))
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.remainderSurplusTokens.eq_1

declarations.type:
{object : Graph.FiniteObject} →
  {Coordinate Chord : Type v} →
    object.DemandActivation Coordinate Chord →
      object.CarrierPresentation Coordinate Chord →
        ℕ → Finset (Finset object.Vertex) → object.Vertex → Finset (object.Vertex × object.Vertex) → ℕ
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.remainderUnit
declarations.doc_string:
**`j(π) = 1 + (rk_v(π) mod (d_G(v) − δ))`**, the surplus unit of `𝔗_R` the
third case charges to.

declarations.type:
{object : Graph.FiniteObject} →
  {Coordinate Chord : Type v} →
    object.DemandActivation Coordinate Chord →
      object.CarrierPresentation Coordinate Chord →
        ℕ → Finset (Finset object.Vertex) → Finset (object.Vertex × object.Vertex) → Option object.Vertex
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.remainderVertexChoice
declarations.doc_string:
**Case (c), the vertex**: the least high-degree remainder vertex contained in
`supp(B_π)`.

declarations.type:
∀ {object : Graph.FiniteObject} {Coordinate Chord : Type v} (activation : object.DemandActivation Coordinate Chord)
  (presentation : object.CarrierPresentation Coordinate Chord) (threshold : ℕ) (packing : Finset (Finset object.Vertex))
  (pair : Finset (object.Vertex × object.Vertex)),
  Graph.FiniteObject.remainderVertexChoice activation presentation threshold packing pair =
    {vertex ∈ object.remainderSupport packing |

            threshold < object.degree vertex}.toList.head?
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.remainderVertexChoice.eq_1

declarations.type: (object : Graph.FiniteObject) → Finset object.Vertex → Finset object.Vertex → ℕ → object.Vertex → ℕ
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.restrictedLoad
declarations.doc_string: **`L(w)` restricted to the non-exceptional full vertices.**

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (support excluded : Finset object.Vertex) (threshold : ℕ) (receiver : object.Vertex),
  object.restrictedLoad support excluded threshold receiver =
    {source ∈ support \ excluded |
        object.internalDegree support source = threshold ∧
          object.traceReceiver? support threshold source = some receiver}.card
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.restrictedLoad.eq_1

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (support : Finset object.Vertex) {small large : Finset object.Vertex},
  small ⊆ large →
    ∀ (threshold : ℕ) (receiver : object.Vertex),
      object.restrictedLoad support large threshold receiver ≤ object.restrictedLoad support small threshold receiver
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.restrictedLoad_antitone
declarations.doc_string:
**A larger exceptional set counts fewer arrivals.**  `restrictedLoad` counts
the non-exceptional full vertices routed to a receiver, so enlarging the
exceptional set can only remove arrivals.  This is what lets one saturation
question serve two different post-ledger cores: the answer at the smaller core
implies the answer at the larger one.

declarations.type: (object : Graph.FiniteObject) → Finset object.Vertex → ℕ → object.Vertex → ℕ
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.routedLoad
declarations.doc_string:
**`L(w)`.**  The number of full vertices the canonical routing sends to a
receiver.

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (support : Finset object.Vertex) (threshold : ℕ) (receiver : object.Vertex),
  object.routedLoad support threshold receiver = (object.routedLoads support threshold receiver).card
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.routedLoad.eq_1

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (support : Finset object.Vertex) (threshold : ℕ) (receiver : object.Vertex),
  object.routedLoad support threshold receiver = (object.routedLoads support threshold receiver).card
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.routedLoad_eq_card
declarations.doc_string: `L(w)` is the size of `ℒ(w)`: the two readings are the same object.

declarations.type: (object : Graph.FiniteObject) → Finset object.Vertex → ℕ → object.Vertex → Finset object.Vertex
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.routedLoads
declarations.doc_string:
**`ℒ(w) = {u : r(u) = w}`.**  The full vertices the canonical routing sends
to a receiver.

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (support : Finset object.Vertex) (threshold scale : ℕ) {receiver : object.Vertex},
  object.internalDegree support receiver < threshold →
    scale * object.missingPorts support threshold receiver =
      scale * (threshold - 1 - object.internalDegree support receiver + 1)
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.saturationThreshold_eq
declarations.doc_string:
**The saturation threshold, indexed by how far the receiver is below the
baseline.**  A receiver of internal degree `threshold − 1 − j` has
`q(w) = j + 1`, so its threshold is `scale·(j + 1)`.

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (support : Finset object.Vertex) (threshold : ℕ) {receiver : object.Vertex},
  object.internalDegree support receiver < threshold →
    ¬threshold - object.internalDegree support receiver = threshold - 1 - object.internalDegree support receiver + 1 →
      False
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.saturationThreshold_eq._proof_1_1

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (support : Finset object.Vertex) (threshold scale : ℕ) (receiver : object.Vertex),
  scale * object.missingPorts support threshold receiver ≤ scale * threshold
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.saturationThreshold_le
declarations.doc_string:
**The raw ceiling.**  A receiver's threshold never exceeds the scale times
the baseline, because it never has more missing ports than the baseline.

declarations.type: (object : Graph.FiniteObject) → ℕ → object.Vertex → List object.Vertex
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.selectedPortEndpoints
declarations.doc_string:
**The ports selected at one centre.**  The first `d_G(h) − δ` neighbours of
`h` in the object's own ordered neighbour list.  At a centre sitting at or below
the baseline the count is zero and the selection is empty.

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (threshold : ℕ) (centre : object.Vertex),
  object.selectedPortEndpoints threshold centre =
    List.take (object.degree centre - threshold) (object.orderedNeighbors centre)
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.selectedPortEndpoints.eq_1

declarations.type:
∀ {object : Graph.FiniteObject} {threshold : ℕ} (centre : object.Vertex),
  (object.selectedPortEndpoints threshold centre).length = object.degree centre - threshold
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.selectedPortEndpoints_length
declarations.doc_string:
A centre contributes exactly `d_G(h) − δ` selected endpoints: the ordered
neighbour list has `d_G(h)` entries, so the truncation is not shortened.

declarations.type:
∀ {object : Graph.FiniteObject} {threshold : ℕ} (centre : object.Vertex),
  ¬min (object.degree centre - threshold) (object.degree centre) = object.degree centre - threshold → False
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.selectedPortEndpoints_length._proof_1_2

declarations.type:
∀ {object : Graph.FiniteObject} {threshold : ℕ} (centre : object.Vertex),
  (object.selectedPortEndpoints threshold centre).Nodup
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.selectedPortEndpoints_nodup

declarations.type:
∀ {object : Graph.FiniteObject} {threshold : ℕ} (centre : object.Vertex),
  (object.selectedPortEndpoints threshold centre).Sublist (object.orderedNeighbors centre)
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.selectedPortEndpoints_sublist

declarations.type:
∀ (threshold dischargeScale windowOrder windowRate surplusScale size packingCard supportCard : ℕ),
  0 < windowOrder →
    0 < threshold →
      2 * (windowOrder - 1) ≤ threshold * windowOrder →
        Graph.FiniteObject.netCapWindowCost threshold dischargeScale windowOrder * threshold < 2 * windowRate →
          Graph.FiniteObject.SufficientlyLargeForNetCap threshold dischargeScale windowOrder windowRate surplusScale
              size →
            2 * (windowRate * size.log2 * packingCard) ≤
                (size.log2 + 1) * (threshold * size + surplusScale * Core.ceilSqrt size) →
              windowOrder * packingCard + supportCard = size →
                dischargeScale * (threshold * (windowOrder * packingCard) + surplusScale * Core.ceilSqrt size) <
                  dischargeScale * (2 * (windowOrder - 1) * packingCard) + supportCard
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.strictCap_of_densityCap_of_sufficientlyLarge
declarations.doc_string: The exact arithmetic content of the paper's asymptotic net-cap step.

declarations.type:
∀ (threshold dischargeScale windowOrder windowRate surplusScale size packingCard supportCard : ℕ),
  0 < windowOrder → ¬0 < dischargeScale * (threshold * windowOrder - 2 * (windowOrder - 1)) + windowOrder → False
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.strictCap_of_densityCap_of_sufficientlyLarge._proof_1_2

declarations.type:
∀ (threshold dischargeScale windowOrder windowRate surplusScale size packingCard supportCard : ℕ),
  0 < size.log2 → ¬size.log2 + 1 ≤ 2 * size.log2 → False
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.strictCap_of_densityCap_of_sufficientlyLarge._proof_1_3

declarations.type:
∀ (threshold dischargeScale windowOrder windowRate surplusScale size packingCard supportCard : ℕ),
  2 * (windowOrder - 1) ≤ threshold * windowOrder →
    ¬threshold * windowOrder = 2 * (windowOrder - 1) + (threshold * windowOrder - 2 * (windowOrder - 1)) → False
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.strictCap_of_densityCap_of_sufficientlyLarge._proof_1_4

declarations.type:
∀ (threshold dischargeScale windowOrder windowRate surplusScale size : ℕ),
  Graph.FiniteObject.netCapCutoff threshold dischargeScale windowOrder windowRate surplusScale ≤ size →
    Graph.FiniteObject.SufficientlyLargeForNetCap threshold dischargeScale windowOrder windowRate surplusScale size
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.sufficientlyLargeForNetCap_of_cutoff

declarations.type:
∀ (threshold dischargeScale windowOrder windowRate surplusScale size : ℕ),
  2 ^ (2 * Graph.FiniteObject.netCapWindowCost threshold dischargeScale windowOrder * threshold) ≤ size →
    0 < 2 ^ (2 * Graph.FiniteObject.netCapWindowCost threshold dischargeScale windowOrder * threshold) →
      size = 0 → False
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.sufficientlyLargeForNetCap_of_cutoff._proof_1_1

declarations.type:
∀ (threshold dischargeScale windowOrder windowRate surplusScale size : ℕ),
  2 * Graph.FiniteObject.netCapErrorScale threshold dischargeScale windowOrder windowRate surplusScale + 1 ≤ size →
    ¬2 * Graph.FiniteObject.netCapErrorScale threshold dischargeScale windowOrder windowRate surplusScale < size → False
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.sufficientlyLargeForNetCap_of_cutoff._proof_1_2

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (support : Finset object.Vertex) (threshold : ℕ),
  ∑ piece ∈ object.canonicalPieces support, object.ambientSurplus (object.pieceSupport support piece) threshold =
    object.ambientSurplus support threshold
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.sum_ambientSurplus_canonicalPieces
declarations.doc_string:
`Σ_i σ(X_i) = σ(R)`: the assigned surplus credit of
`def:canonical-decomp` (ii).  Every surplus unit belongs to the unique piece
containing its carrier, so the assignment is the partition itself.

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (support : Finset object.Vertex) (weight : object.Vertex → ℕ),
  ∑ piece ∈ object.canonicalPieces support, ∑ vertex ∈ object.pieceSupport support piece, weight vertex =
    ∑ vertex ∈ support, weight vertex
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.sum_canonicalPieces
declarations.doc_string:
**The pieces partition the region.**  Every vertex of the region lies in
exactly one piece, so any vertex-local count sums over the pieces to its value
on the region.  This is the single combinatorial fact
`lem:netcharge-superadd` is assembled from.

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (support : Finset object.Vertex) (threshold : ℕ),
  (∀ (vertex : object.Vertex), threshold ≤ object.degree vertex) →
    ∑ vertex ∈ support, object.degree vertex = threshold * support.card + object.ambientSurplus support threshold
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.sum_degree_eq_threshold_mul_card_add_ambientSurplus
declarations.doc_string:
The degree sum over a support splits into its baseline part and its
surplus: `Σ_{v∈X} d_G(v) = δ·|X| + σ(X)`.  This is the `39p₁₃ + σ_W` of
`lem:exact-window-join-identity` with the numerals left to the caller.

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (support : Finset object.Vertex) (threshold : ℕ),
  ¬∑ x ∈ support, (object.degree x - threshold) + threshold * support.card =
        threshold * support.card + ∑ vertex ∈ support, (object.degree vertex - threshold) →
    False
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.sum_degree_eq_threshold_mul_card_add_ambientSurplus._proof_1_2

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (left right : Finset object.Vertex),
  ∑ vertex ∈ left, object.internalDegree right vertex = ∑ vertex ∈ right, object.internalDegree left vertex
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.sum_internalDegree_comm
declarations.doc_string:
**The boundary incidence is symmetric.**  Counting the incidences that
leave a support from inside it, and counting them from outside, give the same
number: both are the number of adjacent ordered pairs across the cut.

This is what lets `def⁺(R) ≤ e(R,W)`, proved on the remainder side, chain with
the capacity bound, proved on the window side.

declarations.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} (G : SimpleGraph V) (v : V) [inst : Fintype ↑(G.neighborSet v)] (w : V),
  (w ∈ G.neighborFinset v) = G.Adj v w
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.sum_internalDegree_comm._simp_1_2

declarations.type: ∀ {V : Type u} (G : SimpleGraph V) (u v : V), G.Adj u v = G.Adj v u
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.sum_internalDegree_comm._simp_1_3

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) {order : ℕ} {support : Finset object.Vertex},
  object.InducesWindow order support → ∑ vertex ∈ support, object.internalDegree support vertex = 2 * (order - 1)
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.sum_internalDegree_window
declarations.doc_string:
**The internal degree mass of a packed window is `2(order − 1)`.**

The window has exactly `order` vertices and its induced subgraph is a path on
that many, so the path embedding is a bijection and the degree sums agree.

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) {order : ℕ} {packing : Finset (Finset object.Vertex)},
  object.IsWindowPacking order packing →
    ∑ vertex ∈ Graph.FiniteObject.windowSupport packing,
        object.internalDegree (Graph.FiniteObject.windowSupport packing) vertex =
      2 * (order - 1) * packing.card + (object.crossWindowIncidences packing).card
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.sum_internalDegree_windowSupport
declarations.doc_string:
**The internal mass of `W`, exactly.**
`Σ_{w ∈ W} d_W(w) = 2(order − 1)p + |I_×(W)|`: an incidence that stays inside the
covered support either stays inside its own packed window -- and each window
carries exactly `2(order − 1)` of those, being an induced copy of the window --
or it crosses to another packed window.

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (support : Finset object.Vertex),
  ∑ piece ∈ object.canonicalPieces support, (object.pieceSupport support piece).card = support.card
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.sum_pieceSupport_card

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (support : Finset object.Vertex) (threshold : ℕ),
  ∑ piece ∈ object.canonicalPieces support, object.positiveDeficiency (object.pieceSupport support piece) threshold =
    object.positiveDeficiency support threshold
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.sum_positiveDeficiency_canonicalPieces
declarations.doc_string:
`Σ_i def⁺(X_i) = def⁺(R)`.  The manuscript's "the positive deficiencies add
exactly", with its reason: the components are components.

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (support excluded : Finset object.Vertex) (threshold : ℕ),
  (∀ vertex ∈ support \ excluded,
      object.internalDegree support vertex = threshold →
        ∃ receiver,
          object.traceReceiver? support threshold vertex = some receiver ∧
            object.IsReceiver support threshold receiver ∧ receiver ∉ excluded) →
    ∑ receiver ∈ object.receivers support threshold \ excluded,
        object.restrictedLoad support excluded threshold receiver =
      {vertex ∈ support \ excluded | object.internalDegree support vertex = threshold}.card
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.sum_restrictedLoad
declarations.doc_string:
**`Σ_w L(w) = |{non-exceptional full vertices}|`**, with the routing
restricted to the non-exceptional vertices on both sides.

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (support : Finset object.Vertex) (threshold : ℕ),
  (∀ vertex ∈ support,
      object.internalDegree support vertex = threshold →
        ∃ receiver,
          object.traceReceiver? support threshold vertex = some receiver ∧
            object.IsReceiver support threshold receiver) →
    ∑ receiver ∈ object.receivers support threshold, object.routedLoad support threshold receiver =
      (object.fullVertices support threshold).card
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.sum_routedLoad
declarations.doc_string:
**`Σ_w L(w) = |{full vertices}|`.**

The canonical routing is a function on the full vertices, so its fibres over the
receivers partition them.  This is `lem:typeA-receiver-loads`' only quantitative
consequence, and the only place the routing is counted.

declarations.type:
{object : Graph.FiniteObject} →
  {threshold : ℕ} →
    {pair : object.Vertex × object.Vertex} → pair ∈ object.excessPorts threshold → object.SurplusPort threshold
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.surplusPortOfMem
declarations.doc_string:
**A selected port, as `def:surplus-ports` declares it.**  Reading a member of
the selector back as a `SurplusPort` is what gives a consumer the shoulder set
and the endpoint's baseline degree without re-deriving either.

declarations.type:
{object : Graph.FiniteObject} →
  {Coordinate Chord : Type v} →
    object.DemandActivation Coordinate Chord →
      object.CarrierPresentation Coordinate Chord →
        ℕ → Finset (Finset object.Vertex) → object.CapacityToken → Finset (Finset (object.Vertex × object.Vertex))
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.tokenFibre
declarations.doc_string:
**`H_t` of `def:same-token-patterns`**: the pairs charged to one token, read
as the edge set of a graph on the active family `𝒜₀`.  Its vertex set is the
active family and its edges are `Π_t = Θ_cap^{-1}(t)`.

declarations.type:
∀ {object : Graph.FiniteObject} {Coordinate Chord : Type v} (activation : object.DemandActivation Coordinate Chord)
  (presentation : object.CarrierPresentation Coordinate Chord) (threshold : ℕ) (packing : Finset (Finset object.Vertex))
  (token : object.CapacityToken),
  Graph.FiniteObject.tokenFibre activation presentation threshold packing token =
    {pair ∈ object.portPairSchedule threshold |
      Graph.FiniteObject.capacityCharge activation presentation threshold packing pair = some token}
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.tokenFibre.eq_1

declarations.type:
∀ {object : Graph.FiniteObject} {Coordinate Chord : Type v} (activation : object.DemandActivation Coordinate Chord)
  (presentation : object.CarrierPresentation Coordinate Chord) (threshold : ℕ) (packing : Finset (Finset object.Vertex))
  (token : object.CapacityToken),
  Graph.FiniteObject.tokenFibre activation presentation threshold packing token ⊆ object.portPairSchedule threshold
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.tokenFibre_subset

declarations.type:
(object : Graph.FiniteObject) →
  Finset object.Vertex → ℕ → (source target : object.Vertex) → Option (object.graph.Path source target)
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.tracePath?
declarations.doc_string:
**`T_u`, the canonical trace.**  The first path of the object's own finite
path schedule from the source to the given receiver that has the trace shape.
The schedule is `Graph.FinitePathSelection.pathSchedule`, the framework's fixed
order — shortest first, then Mathlib's own enumeration — so no application
chooses a trace and no trace is an arbitrary witness.

declarations.type: (object : Graph.FiniteObject) → Finset object.Vertex → ℕ → object.Vertex → Option object.Vertex
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.traceReceiver?
declarations.doc_string:
**The canonical routing.**  The object's own vertex schedule is scanned once
and the first receiver the source traces to is returned.  Nothing outside this
declaration chooses a route, and the result is an `Option`: a source that traces
to no receiver is *not* silently routed somewhere.

declarations.type:

    (∀ vertex ∈ support,
        object.internalDegree support vertex = threshold →
          ∃ receiver,
            object.traceReceiver? support threshold vertex = some receiver ∧
              object.IsReceiver support threshold receiver) →
      (∀ (receiver : object.Vertex),
          object.IsReceiver support threshold receiver →
            1 + object.routedLoad support threshold receiver ≤ scale * object.missingPorts support threshold receiver) →
        support.card ≤ scale * object.positiveDeficiency support threshold
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.FiniteObject.unsaturatedDischarge
declarations.doc_string:
**`lem:typeA-unsaturated-discharge`.**

A support of zero assigned surplus every receiver of which is unsaturated has
`defp(X) ≥ |V(X)|/s`, that is `No(X) ≥ 0`.

The three hypotheses are the manuscript's own: the surplus is zero, so no
internal degree exceeds the baseline; the canonical routing is total, which is
`lem:typeA-receiver-loads` and is node `[88]`'s committed fact; and every
receiver is unsaturated, which is node `[90]`'s.  The conclusion is stated in
the subtraction-free form `def:net-charge` compares, so nothing rounds.

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (support : Finset object.Vertex) (threshold scale : ℕ),
  (object.receivers support threshold).card + (object.fullVertices support threshold).card ≤
      ∑ receiver ∈ object.receivers support threshold, scale * object.missingPorts support threshold receiver →
    (object.receivers support threshold).card + (object.fullVertices support threshold).card = support.card →
      ¬support.card ≤
            ∑ receiver ∈ object.receivers support threshold, scale * object.missingPorts support threshold receiver →
        False

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.HomogeneousCapsCloseStatement
declarations.doc_string:
**Node `[144]`, the near-cubic outcome**:
`cor:homogeneous-same-token-caps-close` at the counted `L_geom`, together with
`thm:homogeneous-overload-geometric-closure`'s edge-count half.

`M₀ = Cap_hom(L_geom)` and the token supply are both derived -- the first from
the counted routing-label alphabet, the second from
`lem:capacity-token-supply`, which the ledger carries -- so neither is a
parameter.  The fourth conjunct is `m = (3/2)n + O(√n)`, which is the surplus
bound spent against `lem:sparse-slack-surplus`'s `2m = δn + σ(G)`.

declarations.type: Graph.FiniteObject → ℕ → ℕ → (Label : Type) → [Fintype Label] → Prop
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.HomogeneousCapsHold
declarations.doc_string:
**The subbranch hypothesis of
`thm:homogeneous-overload-geometric-closure`.**

*"On the subbranch in which sparse surplus exits are absent and all decorated
Type B handoff data have been routed into the Type B fan ledger, the three fixed
homogeneous caps `L_W = L_R = L_P = L_geom` hold."*  Read at the object: no
capacity token, at any declared presentation, supports a role-homogeneous
same-token `L_geom`-matching or `L_geom`-star.  `L_geom = Q_geom + 1` is the
counted routing-label alphabet of `def:same-token-routing-germs`, so the three
caps are one number and it is derived.

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.InducedPathFreeGraph
declarations.doc_string:
Induced `P_order`-freeness stated directly on a labelled graph, at the level
`def:remainder-entropy`'s class `\mathcal G(R)` needs it.

`HasInducedObstruction` reads nothing off a `FiniteObject` except its `graph`
field, so the finite execution data (`vertices`, `decideAdj`) is inessential to
the predicate.  Spelling that out lets a class of *candidate* graphs on a fixed
vertex set be cut out by this constraint without packing every candidate into a
`FiniteObject` first -- there is no new notion here, only the same one at the
arity its consumer needs.

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.IsBaselineSpineDemand
declarations.doc_string:
**`def:baseline-spine-demand`.**

A family `ℐ_spine` of declared target coordinates is a *baseline spine demand
with deficit `E_spine(n)`* when it is independently target-testable and
`|ℐ_spine| ≥ B₀(n) − E_spine(n)`.

Independent target-testability is the framework's own: the family attains full
target rank under the admissible quotient system it is presented with, which is
`Core.TargetRank`'s `targetRank = card`.  The demand inequality is stated with
the logarithm cleared, `C(N,m₀) ≤ 2^{|ℐ_spine| + E_spine(n)}`, which is
`|ℐ_spine| ≥ B₀(n) − E_spine(n)` before taking `log₂` of the baseline.

declarations.type:

  {family : Finset Coordinate} →

          (t : Graph.IsBaselineSpineDemand system vertexCount baselineDegree deficit) →
            ((independent : Core.TargetRank.targetRank system = family.card) →
                (demand : Graph.cubicBaselineBudget vertexCount baselineDegree ≤ 2 ^ (family.card + deficit)) →
                  motive ⋯) →
              motive t
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.IsBaselineSpineDemand.casesOn

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.IsHighCentre
declarations.doc_string:
A vertex is a **high centre** when its degree is strictly above the
registered baseline.  For the manuscript's `δ = 3` this is `d_G(h) ≥ 4`, the
`def:heavy-center-triangular-port` notion of a high center.

  Graph.IsHighCentre object threshold centre = (threshold < object.degree centre)
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.IsHighCentre.eq_1

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.IsOpenPort
declarations.doc_string:
**`def:heavy-center-triangular-port`, open.**  The shoulder chord is absent.
The word records only that absence; no suppressed graph is associated to the
port.

declarations.type:

  Graph.IsOpenPort object centre endpoint = ¬Graph.IsTriangularPort object centre endpoint
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.IsOpenPort.eq_1

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.IsShoulder
declarations.doc_string:
**`s(p)`, membership form.**  `z` is a shoulder of the port `(centre,
endpoint)` when it is a neighbour of the endpoint other than the centre.

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (centre endpoint z : object.Vertex),
  Graph.IsShoulder object centre endpoint z = (object.graph.Adj endpoint z ∧ z ≠ centre)
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.IsShoulder.eq_1

declarations.doc_string:
**`def:heavy-center-triangular-port`, triangular.**  The shoulder chord
`e_p^* = a_p b_p` lies in `G`.  Adjacency is irreflexive, so two adjacent
shoulders are automatically distinct and this is exactly the manuscript's
condition once the endpoint is cubic.

specialized once and for all to the finite class of labelled graphs on `n`
vertices: any canonical state map on graphs with `n` vertices realizes no
more states than `Nat.card (LabelledOn n)`. This is the one instantiation
`S07`'s entropy cap needs from `Ambient` -- everything past this point
(the pigeonhole inequality itself, its `2 ^ k` form, the rate-floor
compounding) is the already-built, fully generic `Core.FiniteEntropy`
machinery; `LabelledOn n` only supplies the finite carrier that machinery
was missing.

manuscript's `|Labels order|`; the *cap* direction proved here is only helped by

declarations.doc_string:
**A separated coordinate family.**

`slot` is where each coordinate reads: for coordinate `c`, the vertex it attaches
from and the set of vertices it may attach to.  `separated` is the manuscript's
selection — distinct coordinates read disjoint targets — and `outside` is that
the attaching vertex is not itself one of them.

The manuscript's instance is one coordinate per packed window per selected dyadic
scale, with `reads` the window's own support; the `O(1)` scales whose completions
collide are simply not in `Coordinate`.

declarations.doc_string:
**`lem:skeleton-dominates` at the separated package.**

The package's joint state count is realized inside the labelled graphs on the
object's own order with exactly the ambient edge count, so it is bounded by
`C(C(n,2), m)` — the manuscript's `|𝒢_{n,m}|`.

The two side conditions are the counting conditions and nothing more: the
coordinate slots fit inside the ambient edge count, and the reserved pool is at
least that large.

  (family.filled assign).card ≤ edgeCount →
    ¬(family.filled assign).card + (edgeCount - (family.filled assign).card) = edgeCount → False

      graph :=
        SimpleGraph.fromEdgeSet ↑(family.filled assign ∪ family.completion (edgeCount - (family.filled assign).card)) }

**The realization is injective.**  Two joint assignments differing at any
single coordinate differ as labelled graphs.

**Separation.**  Distinct coordinates read disjoint vertex sets, so setting
one leaves every other coordinate's reading fixed.

{object : Graph.FiniteObject} →
  {Coordinate : Type} →
    [Fintype Coordinate] →
      Graph.PackedWindowRealization.SeparatedFamily object Coordinate → Finset (Sym2 (Fin object.vertexCount))
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.PackedWindowRealization.SeparatedFamily.slots
declarations.doc_string:
The slots the coordinates of the package occupy: one unordered pair per
coordinate root and readable target.

  (family : Graph.PackedWindowRealization.SeparatedFamily object Coordinate),
  family.slots =
    {edge |
      ∃ coordinate,

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.PackedWindowRealization.SeparatedFamily.sourcesOutside
declarations.doc_string:
**The testers are rooted outside the package.**  No coordinate's attaching
vertex is read by any coordinate — the manuscript's outside completions are
rooted outside the packed windows.  Taking it at every pair, not just the
diagonal, is what stops one coordinate's root being mistaken for another
coordinate's target.

declarations.type:
∀ {object : Graph.FiniteObject} {Coordinate : Type} [inst : Fintype Coordinate] [DecidableEq Coordinate]

declarations.doc_string:
**The rate form the entropy cap consumes.**  If every selected coordinate
carries at least `2 ^ rate` states, the family realizes at least
`2 ^ (rate · #coordinates)` of them inside the ambient labelled class.

At the manuscript's instance `#coordinates` is one per packed window per selected
scale and `rate` is the audited `c₁₃`, so this is
`2 ^ (c₁₃ · (selected scales) · p) ≤ |𝒢|` — `lem:p13-window-package`'s displayed
bound, with no rate constant named here.

declarations.type:
∀ {object : Graph.FiniteObject} {Coordinate : Type} [inst : Fintype Coordinate] [DecidableEq Coordinate]
  (family : Graph.PackedWindowRealization.SeparatedFamily object Coordinate) (edgeCount rate : ℕ),
  (∀ (coordinate : Coordinate), 2 ^ rate ≤ Nat.card (family.State coordinate)) →
    family.slots.card ≤ edgeCount →
      edgeCount ≤ family.pool.card →
        2 ^ (rate * Fintype.card Coordinate) ≤ (object.vertexCount.choose 2).choose edgeCount
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.PackedWindowRealization.SeparatedFamily.two_pow_rate_mul_card_le_skeletonBudget
declarations.doc_string:
**`lem:p13-window-package` against the manuscript's own budget.**

If every selected coordinate carries at least `2 ^ rate` states, the package
realizes at least `2 ^ (rate · #coordinates)` labelled skeletons of the ambient
edge count.  At the manuscript's instance `#coordinates` is one per packed window
per selected scale and `rate` is the audited `c₁₃`, so this is
`2 ^ (c₁₃ · scales · p) ≤ C(C(n,2), m)` — the comparison the entropy cap makes.
No rate constant, scale count, or numeral is named here.

declarations.type: ℕ → ℕ → Type
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.PackedWindowRealization.Skeleton
declarations.doc_string: `𝒢_{n,m}`: the labelled simple graphs on `[n]` carrying exactly `m` edges.

  (designated : object.Vertex),

          ((Graph.PackedWindowRealization.vertexLabel object) designated)
          ((Graph.PackedWindowRealization.vertexLabel object) (↑window index)) ↔
        index ∈ assign window
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.PackedWindowRealization.adj_realizeAttachment_iff
declarations.doc_string:
**The reading of the realization.**  The assignment is recovered from the
realized graph's adjacency, one window at a time.

This is where the two hypotheses do their work.  `outside` makes the attachment
a genuine edge rather than a loop, so `fromEdgeSet` retains it; and
`supports_pairwise_disjoint` is what stops a *different* window from having
produced the same edge — which is the manuscript's "the tester for one window
does not change the label state assigned to another packed window".

declarations.type:
{object : Graph.FiniteObject} →
  {order : ℕ} →
    (profile : Graph.InducedPathMaximalPacking.Profile object order) →
      object.Vertex →
        (Graph.PackedWindowRealization.PackedWindow profile →
            Graph.PackedWindowRealization.AttachmentState object order) →
          Set (Sym2 (Fin object.vertexCount))
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.PackedWindowRealization.attachmentEdges
declarations.doc_string:
The edge set a joint assignment prescribes: from the designated outside
vertex to exactly the window positions each window's own coordinate names.

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (order : ℕ),
  Nat.card (Graph.PackedWindowRealization.AttachmentState object order) = 2 ^ order
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.PackedWindowRealization.card_attachmentState
declarations.doc_string: The per-window state count of the attachment coordinates.

declarations.type: ∀ {remainder order : ℕ}, remainder ≤ order → Nat.card (Graph.LabelledOn remainder) ≤ Nat.card (Graph.LabelledOn order)
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.PackedWindowRealization.card_labelled_mono
declarations.doc_string:
**`|𝒢_{|R|}| ≤ |𝒢_n|` whenever `|R| ≤ n`.**

`def:remainder-entropy` puts its class `𝒢(R)` on `V(R)`, the remainder's own
vertex set, while `lem:skeleton-dominates` counts the ambient class `𝒢_n` on
`[n]`.  A labelled graph on `[|R|]` is a labelled graph on `[n]` transported
along the inclusion `[|R|] ↪ [n]`, and transport along an embedding is
injective on graphs, so the remainder class never outnumbers the ambient one.
This is the inclusion `𝒢(R) ⊆ 𝒢_n` that `lem:skeleton-dominates` uses when it
pays the remainder's realized states out of the labelled-skeleton budget.

declarations.type:
∀ {object : Graph.FiniteObject} {order : ℕ} (profile : Graph.InducedPathMaximalPacking.Profile object order),
  Nat.card (Graph.PackedWindowRealization.PackedWindow profile) = profile.selected.length
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.PackedWindowRealization.card_packedWindow
declarations.doc_string:
**`p₁₃` is the packing's own cardinality.**

The window index type lists each selected occurrence exactly once -- that is
what `selected_nodup` buys -- so its cardinality is the length of the selected
list.  For the profile read off the ledger's `ObstructionPackingClosure.Packing`
that length is literally the `packingCount` the density comparison is run at,
which is why the window package's multiplicative demand and the density node's
`stateDemand` speak about the same `p₁₃`.

declarations.type:
∀ {object : Graph.FiniteObject} {order : ℕ} {profile : Graph.InducedPathMaximalPacking.Profile object order}
  {State : Graph.PackedWindowRealization.PackedWindow profile → Type v} (n : ℕ)
  (stateOf : Graph.LabelledOn n → Graph.PackedWindowRealization.JointState State),
  Nat.card ↑(Graph.LabelledOn.Realized stateOf) ≤ Nat.card (Graph.LabelledOn n)
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.PackedWindowRealization.card_realized_le
declarations.doc_string:
**`lem:state-count-comparison` for a packed-window assignment.**  The
window states the proof actually realizes never outnumber the labelled
skeletons of the same order.

This is `Graph.LabelledOn.card_realized_le` at the packed-window joint state
type, and it needs no realization hypothesis: `realize` is the canonical choice
inside a state's own fibre and `realize_injective` is a theorem.

declarations.type: ∀ (n m : ℕ), Nat.card (Graph.PackedWindowRealization.Skeleton n m) = (n.choose 2).choose m
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.PackedWindowRealization.card_skeleton
declarations.doc_string:
**`lem:skeleton-dominates`'s count, proved.**  `|𝒢_{n,m}| =
binom(binom(n,2), m)`: a labelled simple graph on `[n]` is determined by its
edge set, an `m`-element subset of the `binom(n,2)` unordered pairs.

declarations.type:
∀ {object : Graph.FiniteObject} {order : ℕ} (profile : Graph.InducedPathMaximalPacking.Profile object order),
  Graph.PackedWindowRealization.Packed profile →
    ∀ {State : Graph.PackedWindowRealization.PackedWindow profile → Type v}
      {Observed : Graph.PackedWindowRealization.PackedWindow profile → Type w}
      (observe : (window : Graph.PackedWindowRealization.PackedWindow profile) → State window → Observed window),
      (∀ (window : Graph.PackedWindowRealization.PackedWindow profile), Function.Injective (observe window)) →
        Function.Injective fun state window => observe window (state window)
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.PackedWindowRealization.coordinate_independence
declarations.doc_string:
**`coordinate_independence`.**  Packed windows carry independent
coordinates: local observations that separate each window's own states
separate every joint state.

The packedness hypothesis is what makes this the *manuscript's* independence
rather than a formal restatement — it is the reason a per-window observation
may be read off the induced structure on that window's support without any
other window's support interfering, i.e. `lem:p13-window-package`'s "no
coordinate is counted twice".  The lift itself is
`Core.FiniteEntropy.injective_pi_of_forall_injective`, owned by Core.

declarations.type:
{object : Graph.FiniteObject} →
  {order : ℕ} →
    {profile : Graph.InducedPathMaximalPacking.Profile object order} →
      (Graph.PackedWindowRealization.PackedWindow profile → Type v) → ℕ
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.PackedWindowRealization.demand
declarations.doc_string:
The exact multiplicative state demand of the window package, derived from
the local carriers rather than declared.

declarations.type:
∀ {object : Graph.FiniteObject} {order : ℕ} {profile : Graph.InducedPathMaximalPacking.Profile object order}
  (State : Graph.PackedWindowRealization.PackedWindow profile → Type v)
  [∀ (window : Graph.PackedWindowRealization.PackedWindow profile), Finite (State window)] (localDemand : ℕ),
  (∀ (window : Graph.PackedWindowRealization.PackedWindow profile), Nat.card (State window) = localDemand) →
    Graph.PackedWindowRealization.demand State = localDemand ^ profile.selected.length
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.PackedWindowRealization.demand_eq_pow_of_uniform
declarations.doc_string:
**`lem:p13-window-package` at a uniform per-window carrier.**

Every packed window carries the same finite package -- the registered barrier
schedule declared at every separated dyadic scale is the same schedule at each
window -- so the joint demand is that one local count raised to the number of
packed windows:

  `demand State = localDemand ^ p₁₃`.

That is the exact shape the density comparison's `stateDemand` has, with
`localDemand` the derived `safeProduct` and `p₁₃` the ledger packing's own
cardinality.  The exponent is not chosen: it is `card_packedWindow`.

declarations.type:
∀ {object : Graph.FiniteObject} {order : ℕ} {profile : Graph.InducedPathMaximalPacking.Profile object order}
  (State : Graph.PackedWindowRealization.PackedWindow profile → Type v)
  [∀ (window : Graph.PackedWindowRealization.PackedWindow profile), Finite (State window)],
  Graph.PackedWindowRealization.demand State = ∏ window, Nat.card (State window)
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.PackedWindowRealization.demand_eq_product
declarations.doc_string:
**`lem:p13-window-package`'s multiplicative form.**  The window package's
demand is the product of the per-window demands — the exact statement that the
packed coordinates are independent, with `log₂` turning the product into the
manuscript's sum over windows.

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.PackedWindowRealization.demand_le_card_labelled
declarations.doc_string:
**`state_card_le`.**  A packed-window package whose *whole* joint family is
realized by labelled skeletons has demand at most the labelled-skeleton count.

The hypothesis is exactly the manuscript's "all target-complete window states
are realized by labelled near-cubic skeletons": surjectivity of the canonical
assignment onto the joint family.  Nothing else is assumed, and in particular
no injection is supplied — `Nat.card_le_card_of_surjective` is the pigeonhole
in the direction a *demand* travels.

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.PackedWindowRealization.demand_le_card_labelled_of_injective
declarations.doc_string:
The same comparison from an injective realization of the joint family,
which is the shape a per-window realization produces after
`coordinate_independence`.

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.PackedWindowRealization.demand_le_skeletonBudget
declarations.doc_string:
**`lem:state-count-comparison` against the near-cubic class.**  A
packed-window package realized inside `𝒢_{n,m}` has demand at most
`binom(binom(n,2), m)`, which is the labelled skeleton budget the finite
density budget registers.

This is `prop:p13-density`'s middle step verbatim: "since all target-complete
window states are realized by labelled near-cubic skeletons under
`def:near-cubic-spine`, `lem:independent-target-entropy, lem:skeleton-dominates`
give ...".  Both `n` and `m` come from the realization's own class; nothing is
chosen here.

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.PackedWindowRealization.entropy_cap
declarations.doc_string:
**`entropy_cap`.**  A realized packed-window package cannot overflow the
labelled-skeleton count.  This is the closing step of every entropy-cap
argument in the manuscript, here as an eliminator on the overflow branch.

declarations.type:
∀ {object : Graph.FiniteObject} {order : ℕ} (profile : Graph.InducedPathMaximalPacking.Profile object order),
  Finite (Graph.PackedWindowRealization.PackedWindow profile)
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.PackedWindowRealization.instFinitePackedWindow

declarations.type: ∀ (n m : ℕ), Finite (Graph.PackedWindowRealization.Skeleton n m)
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.PackedWindowRealization.instFiniteSkeleton

declarations.type:
{object : Graph.FiniteObject} →
  {order : ℕ} →
    (profile : Graph.InducedPathMaximalPacking.Profile object order) →
      Fintype (Graph.PackedWindowRealization.PackedWindow profile)
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.PackedWindowRealization.instFintypePackedWindow

declarations.type:
∀ {object : Graph.FiniteObject} {order : ℕ} (profile : Graph.InducedPathMaximalPacking.Profile object order),
  Graph.PackedWindowRealization.Packed profile
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.PackedWindowRealization.packed
declarations.doc_string: The canonical packing is packed.  A theorem, never a hypothesis.

declarations.type:
{object : Graph.FiniteObject} →
  {order : ℕ} →
    (profile : Graph.InducedPathMaximalPacking.Profile object order) →
      object.Vertex →
        (Graph.PackedWindowRealization.PackedWindow profile →
            Graph.PackedWindowRealization.AttachmentState object order) →
          Graph.LabelledOn object.vertexCount
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.PackedWindowRealization.realizeAttachment
declarations.doc_string:
**The realization.**  The labelled graph on the object's own order whose only
edges are the attachments the joint assignment prescribes.

declarations.type:
∀ {object : Graph.FiniteObject} {order : ℕ} (profile : Graph.InducedPathMaximalPacking.Profile object order)
  (designated : object.Vertex)
  (assign :
    Graph.PackedWindowRealization.PackedWindow profile → Graph.PackedWindowRealization.AttachmentState object order),

    { graph := SimpleGraph.fromEdgeSet (Graph.PackedWindowRealization.attachmentEdges profile designated assign) }
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.PackedWindowRealization.realizeAttachment.eq_1

declarations.type:
∀ {object : Graph.FiniteObject} {order : ℕ} (profile : Graph.InducedPathMaximalPacking.Profile object order)
  (designated : object.Vertex),
  (∀ (window : Graph.PackedWindowRealization.PackedWindow profile),
      designated ∉ Graph.PackedWindowRealization.support profile window) →
    Function.Injective (Graph.PackedWindowRealization.realizeAttachment profile designated)
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.PackedWindowRealization.realizeAttachment_injective
declarations.doc_string:
**The realization is injective**, so the package's joint state count is
bounded by the labelled-skeleton count.  Two assignments differing at any single
window differ as graphs, because that window's edge slots are its own.

declarations.type:
{object : Graph.FiniteObject} →
  {order : ℕ} →
    (profile : Graph.InducedPathMaximalPacking.Profile object order) →
      Graph.PackedWindowRealization.PackedWindow profile → Finset object.Vertex
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.PackedWindowRealization.support
declarations.doc_string:
The coordinate support of a packed window is its literal embedded vertex
set: `Graph.InducedPathMaximalPacking.support` at the selected occurrence, with
no re-derivation.

declarations.type:
∀ {object : Graph.FiniteObject} {order : ℕ} (profile : Graph.InducedPathMaximalPacking.Profile object order)
  (left right : Graph.PackedWindowRealization.PackedWindow profile),
  left ≠ right →
    Disjoint (Graph.PackedWindowRealization.support profile left) (Graph.PackedWindowRealization.support profile right)
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.PackedWindowRealization.supports_pairwise_disjoint
declarations.doc_string:
**Canonical packing disjointness at the coordinate-support boundary.**

This is the packing's own `pairwiseDisjoint` field, restated at the subtype of
selected windows.  For `maximalProfile` that field is
`maximalWindowSet_admissible`, so nothing here is assumed.

declarations.type: ∀ (n : ℕ), 2 ^ n.choose 2 ≤ Nat.card (Graph.LabelledOn n)
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.PackedWindowRealization.two_pow_choose_two_le_card_labelled
declarations.doc_string:
**`|𝒢_n| ≥ 2 ^ binom(n,2)`.**

A labelled simple graph on `[n]` is determined by its edge set, and every
subset of the complete graph's edge set is the edge set of one: the
`2 ^ binom(n,2)` subsets of `⊤.edgeFinset` therefore inject into `LabelledOn n`.
The equality holds too, but only this direction is consumed.

declarations.type:
∀ (n : ℕ),
  Nat.card ↥⊤.edgeFinset.powerset ≤ Nat.card (Graph.LabelledOn n) →
    Nat.card ↥⊤.edgeFinset.powerset = 2 ^ n.choose 2 → ¬2 ^ n.choose 2 ≤ Nat.card (Graph.LabelledOn n) → False
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.PackedWindowRealization.two_pow_choose_two_le_card_labelled._proof_1_1
Hypostructure.Graph.PackedWindowRealization.two_pow_le_card_labelled
declarations.doc_string:
**`lem:independent-target-entropy` at the canonical packing.**

`2 ^ k ≤ |𝒢|`: whatever exponent the window package's demand certifies is
certified against the labelled-skeleton count.  The manuscript's `k` is
`(c₁₃ − o(1)) p₁₃ log₂ n`; here it is any exponent the multiplicative demand
already dominates, so no rate constant is named.

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.PackedWindowRealization.two_pow_le_skeletonBudget
declarations.doc_string:
**`lem:independent-target-entropy` against the near-cubic class.**

`2 ^ k ≤ |𝒢_{n,m}|`.  Composed with the exponent bookkeeping of
`Graph.Strategy.FiniteDensityBudget`, this is the whole of `prop:p13-density`:
whatever exponent the window package's own multiplicative demand certifies is
paid out of the labelled skeleton budget, so the density cap is produced by a
realization rather than observed.

declarations.type:
∀ {object : Graph.FiniteObject} {order : ℕ} (profile : Graph.InducedPathMaximalPacking.Profile object order)
  (designated : object.Vertex),
  (∀ (window : Graph.PackedWindowRealization.PackedWindow profile),
      designated ∉ Graph.PackedWindowRealization.support profile window) →
    2 ^ (order * profile.selected.length) ≤ Nat.card (Graph.LabelledOn object.vertexCount)
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.PackedWindowRealization.two_pow_order_mul_packing_le_card_labelled
declarations.doc_string:
**`lem:independent-target-entropy` at the attachment coordinates, with no
hypothesis left.**

The package of one attachment coordinate per packed window realizes
`2 ^ (order · p)` distinct labelled graphs, so that many states are available
inside the ambient labelled class.  `p` is the packing's own length, read by
`card_packedWindow`; no rate constant and no numeral is named.

This is the first consumed realization in the tree: it discharges the antecedent
of `demand_le_card_labelled_of_injective`, which until now nothing supplied.

declarations.type: (object : Graph.FiniteObject) → object.Vertex ≃ Fin object.vertexCount
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.PackedWindowRealization.vertexLabel
declarations.doc_string:
**The object's own vertex enumeration**, as the relabelling
`lem:skeleton-dominates` states the labelled adjacency matrix against.  This is
the deterministic tie-breaking rule; nothing below depends on *which*
enumeration it is, only on its being a bijection.

declarations.type: {V : Type u} → Finset (Finset V) → Prop
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.PatternFamily.IsMatching
declarations.doc_string: **A matching**: distinct members of the family share no vertex.

declarations.type:
∀ {V : Type u} (family : Finset (Finset V)),
  Graph.PatternFamily.IsMatching family =
    ∀ edge ∈ family, ∀ other ∈ family, edge ≠ other → ∀ vertex ∈ edge, vertex ∉ other
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.PatternFamily.IsMatching.eq_1

declarations.type:
∀ {V : Type u} {family sub : Finset (Finset V)},
  Graph.PatternFamily.IsMatching family → sub ⊆ family → Graph.PatternFamily.IsMatching sub
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.PatternFamily.IsMatching.subset
declarations.doc_string: A subfamily of a matching is a matching.

declarations.type: {V : Type u} → Finset (Finset V) → V → Prop
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.PatternFamily.IsStar
declarations.doc_string: **A star with a given centre**: every member of the family contains it.

declarations.type: ℕ → ℕ → ℕ
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.PatternFamily.capCharge
declarations.doc_string:
**`Cap_hom(L)`** of `def:homogeneous-token-charge`, with the role bound a
parameter rather than a numeral: the caller's own alphabet supplies `Q_st`.

declarations.type:
∀ (roleBound patternBound : ℕ),
  Graph.PatternFamily.capCharge roleBound patternBound = roleBound * ((patternBound - 1) * (2 * patternBound - 3))
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.PatternFamily.capCharge.eq_1

declarations.type:
∀ {V : Type u} {Role : Type w} [inst : DecidableEq Role] (family : Finset (Finset V)) (role : Finset V → Role)

that cover counts every member at least once and every matching member exactly
twice, while the same sum is at most `|cover|·Δ ≤ 2ν·Δ`.

fibre, where every member carries one colour, the pattern it produces is

*"Consequently, any quotient identifying `w(u)` with `w(v)` is either
context-universal or target-defective."*

exactly these two outcomes: either no outside context separates them, or one
does and is exhibited.  There is no third possibility, and in particular no
outcome in which the identification is valid for some contexts without a
witness for the rest.  This is the exhaustiveness a context-validity branch
splits on.

declarations.doc_string:
**`lem:typeA-internal-quotient-mixed`, the framework mechanism.**

*"Failure of target-completeness gives a compatible outside context and two
realizations ... with the same image in the quotient, but with different target
predicates after gluing.  ...  The two realizations have the same image in the
quotient, so a distinguishing event must use at least one coordinate forgotten
by it."*

When the smaller reading can only realize *fewer* targets -- which is what an
edge-forgetting quotient does to a monotone target -- the distinguishing
context is forced to sit on the larger side: it realizes the target after
gluing `right` and fails to after gluing `left`.  So every witness of the
distinguishing realization uses something `left` forgot.  Nothing here is
specific to carriers; it is the one-sidedness of a defect under a monotone
target.

declarations.doc_string:
**`prop:typeA-route8-carrier-reduction`.**

*"Suppose that no indexed route-8 entry in `𝒳` is two-carrier.  Then every
`ξ` has at least three private essential carriers ... `floor·N_basin ≤ def⁺(R)`
... combining the two inequalities is impossible.  Thus a surviving large-budget
route-8 collection must contain a two-carrier route-8 entry."*

The census bound is `card_mul_le_ambient`, the collision is
`census_contradiction`, and the conclusion is stated exactly as the manuscript's
"contains a two-carrier route-8 entry".  The private-carrier floor
`threshold + 1` is *derived* from the negation of the two-carrier condition, so
no caller supplies it.

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.Route8.Data
declarations.doc_string:
**The route-8 carrier data of an object.**

This is `def:typeA-route8-carriers`' indexed family `Ξ(𝒳)` together with the
numbers a census reads: the boundary-incidence supply the collection is counted
inside, the discharge scale of `lem:typeA-route8-burden`, the private-carrier
threshold of a two-carrier entry, the deficit `D_A(𝒳)`, and the remainder size
`|R|`.

It carries **no mathematical clause**.  Every statement the manuscript attaches
to a route-8 residual -- the absence clause (R2) of
`def:typeA-true-route8-residual`, the target-complete-minimality (R4) of the
assigned trace basins, the burden of `lem:typeA-route8-burden`, the large-budget
deficit of `def:typeA-large-budget-deficit`, and the registered rate condition --
is a *fact*, published on the canonical ledger by the row that establishes the
arm and read from it by exact key.  The only propositions below are the
well-formedness of the data itself: a coordinate is recorded by a simple cycle,
and an entry's own cut lies inside the collection's supply.

declarations.doc_string:
**The surviving trace of one indexed entry**: clauses (R2) and (R4) of
`def:typeA-true-route8-residual` composed exactly as
`lem:typeA-one-terminal-collapse` composes them.

`def:typeA-trace-basin` makes the assigned basin target-complete-minimal, so a
*nontrivial* target-complete quotient of its reading fires one of the four
alternatives (a)--(d), which are exits `(4)`, `(5)`, `(6)`, `(7)`; (R2) says
those are absent.  The quotient in question is the manuscript's `ρ°_𝒞`, which
retains the boundary profile and forgets exactly the coordinates whose declared
support crosses the entry's cut, so the composite says: `ρ°_𝒞` is a *proper*
quotient -- it does not agree with the core reading.

declarations.doc_string:
**`lem:typeA-route8-burden`, proved.**

*"For each `X ∈ 𝒳` ... `lem:typeA-silent-excess-count` applies to `X` and gives
`S_sil^exc(X) ≥ 4(¼|V(X)| − def⁺(X))`.  By `lem:typeA-reduced-silent-residual`,
every unpaid silent excess vertex counted by `S_sil^exc(X)` has a
target-complete-minimal trace basin unless one of exits (4)--(7) occurs.  Those
exits are absent by hypothesis.  Counting the resulting indexed pairs `(u, B_u)`
and summing the displayed inequality over `X ∈ 𝒳` proves
`N_basin(𝒳) ≥ 4·D_A(𝒳)`."*

The two cited readings are the hypotheses; the counting and the summation are
this proof.  `N_basin(𝒳)` is `|Ξ(𝒳)|` and the indexed entries are partitioned by
the support they live on, which is what turns the per-support inequalities into
the collection-wide one.

declarations.doc_string:
**`def:typeA-trace-basin` clause (c), at one presented entry.**

The equality of two declared coordinates of `ρ_u(B_u)` that becomes
target-complete only after adjoining the larger connected support `Z ⊋ B_u`.

The admissibility of the identification at `Z` is `DeclaredQuotient`: its
`connected` field is the clause's *connected* support, its `carries` field is
that `Z` carries the declared coordinate family, its `fibrewise` and
`contextUniversal` fields are target-completeness at `Z`, and its two
representative fields are `def:admissible-rank-quotient`'s proper and closed
clauses.  Nothing here re-derives them.

declarations.doc_string:
**`lem:typeA-one-terminal-collapse`, the collapse itself.**

*"Assume `|𝒞| ≤ 1` ... we claim that `ρ|_𝒞 → ρ°_𝒞` is target-complete ... The
nontrivial target-complete quotient above is precisely failure alternative (b)
in the definition of target-complete-minimality, unless one of the other
alternatives occurs first."*

The claim is the previous theorem: with a small core the internal-forgetting
reading *is* the core reading, so nothing separates them.  What the alternatives
are is not decided here -- `minimality` is the reading's own
target-complete-minimality clause, and this theorem is the proof that its
hypothesis is met.

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.Route8.census_contradiction
declarations.doc_string:
**`prop:typeA-route8-carrier-reduction`, the arithmetic.**

Three integer readings collide:

* `deficit` -- `ambient ≤ basins + discharge·supply`, the node-`[113]` bound
  `D_A ≥ (1/discharge − τ)·|R|` cleared of denominators and with the burden
  `N_basin ≥ discharge·D_A` already substituted for the deficit;
* `budget`  -- `floor·N_basin ≤ supply`, the disjoint private carriers against
  the boundary-incidence supply;
* `rate`    -- `(floor·discharge + 1)·supply < floor·ambient`, the registered
  rate condition.  At the manuscript's `floor = 3` and `discharge = 4` it is
  `13·τ_win|R| < 3|R|`, i.e. `τ_win < 3/13`.

No constant appears: every one of them is a reading the branch carries.

declarations.type:
∀ {floor discharge basins supply ambient : ℕ},
  floor * basins ≤ supply →
    (floor * discharge + 1) * supply < floor * ambient →
      floor * ambient ≤ floor * basins + floor * discharge * supply →
        floor * (discharge * supply) = floor * discharge * supply →
          (floor * discharge + 1) * supply = floor * discharge * supply + supply → False
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.Route8.census_contradiction._proof_1_1

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.SameTokenBlockerRoles.canonicalBlockerOrder
declarations.doc_string:
**`def:canonical-sparse-blocker-order`**: the declared total order on the
blocker types, in the clause order (a)--(f) of `def:surplus-blockers`.

The order is what makes `def:canonical-blocker-ledger` single-valued: a pair
blocked by several types is charged to the first of them in this list, and
nothing else chooses.

declarations.type: Graph.SameTokenBlockerRoles.canonicalBlockerOrder.Nodup
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.SameTokenBlockerRoles.canonicalBlockerOrder_nodup
declarations.doc_string:
The declared order lists each blocker type once, so the ledger's fibre sum
runs over the alphabet without repetition.
