declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.TypeBFanClosedPorts.fanClosedPortHybridEntry
declarations.doc_string:
**`prop:fan-closed-port-typeB-routing`, clause (c)**, manuscript node
`[72]` closed by node `[74]`.

At a certificate-marked centre `h` carrying a family `𝒬` of `r ≥ 2` fan-closed
surplus ports, the hybrid B1 ledger supplies local incidence capacity at least
`D_B(𝔉_h)`, and the paying incidences include the two non-`h` incidences
`x a_p` and `x b_p` of every fan-closed port `p = (h, x) ∈ 𝒬`, each classified
by `def:typeB-window-incidence-profile` as a window incidence or a non-window
fan incidence.

Parts (a) and (b) are `fanClosedPortTypeBRouting`; this completes the
proposition's local content.

declarations.type:
∀ {object : Graph.FiniteObject} (profile : Graph.TypeBFanClosedPorts.Profile object)
  (ledger : Graph.ReceiverLoad.LoadCapacityProfile),
  Graph.NormalForm object 3 profile.marked.fan.hub →
    ledger.loadMultiplier = 4 →
      ∀ {ports : Finset object.Vertex},
        (∀ vertex ∈ ports, profile.IsFanClosed vertex) →
          2 ≤ ports.card →
            ports.card ≤ profile.closedCount ∧
              ↑ports.card - (3 - (↑(object.degree profile.marked.fan.hub) + 1) * (1 / ↑ledger.loadMultiplier)) ≤
                  profile.closedNeighbourDeficit ledger ∧
                (↑(object.degree profile.marked.fan.hub) + 1) * (1 / ↑ledger.loadMultiplier) - 1 ≤
                    profile.closedNeighbourDeficit ledger ∧
                  0 < profile.closedNeighbourDeficit ledger
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.TypeBFanClosedPorts.fanClosedPortTypeBRouting
declarations.doc_string:
`prop:fan-closed-port-typeB-routing`, parts (a) and (b), manuscript node
`[72]`.

At a certificate-marked fan centre `h` of degree `k` carrying a family of
`r ≥ 2` fan-closed surplus ports:

* the ports contribute at least `r` cubic-closed neighbours;
* `D_B(𝔉_h) ≥ r - (3 - (k+1)α) ≥ (k+1)α - 1 > 0`.

`k ≥ 4` is `Marked.highDegree`, already part of the certificate-marked fan, so
no degree hypothesis is added here.  The strict positivity is the sharp instance
of the recorded design constraint
`ReceiverLoad.LoadCapacityProfile.dischargeRate_gt` (`5α > 1`): at `c = 2` and
`k = 4` the deficit is exactly `5α - 1`, so this is the place the constraint was
read off, and no hypothesis is added here either.  At `α = 1/4` the three
displayed quantities are the manuscript's `r - (11-k)/4`, `(k-3)/4` and
`1/4 > 0`.

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.TypeBFanIncidence.degreeFourProfile
declarations.doc_string:
**`[79]`, the degree-four fan profile.**

At a high centre sitting exactly one above the baseline: the centre surplus is
`1`, the cubic-closed count is at most the degree, and the deficit is
`s·c − s·δ + (δ + 2)`.  At the manuscript's `δ = 3`, `s = 4` and `k = 4` those
three readings are its *centre surplus `1`, `0 ≤ c ≤ 4`, `D_B = c − 7/4*`; the
`7/4` is `(δ − (k+1)/s)` evaluated, never written.

The lower and upper bounds on the deficit are the same three quantities read at
`c = 0` and at `c = k`, which is where `[81]`'s `c ≤ 1` / `c ≥ 2` split gets its
range.

      ¬Graph.TypeBFanIncidence.closedCount object threshold envelope centre ≤ threshold + 1 → False

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (threshold dischargeScale : ℕ) (envelope : Finset object.Vertex)

declarations.doc_string:
**A positive-deficit fan is exactly a fan that is not certificate-closed.**

The two alternatives of the Type B local ledger are complementary by
construction, which is why no node has to offer a third.

declarations.type: (object : Graph.FiniteObject) → ℕ → ℕ → Finset object.Vertex → object.Vertex → ℤ
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.TypeBFanIncidence.scaledDeficit
declarations.doc_string:
**`s·D_B`**, the closed-neighbour deficit at the discharge scale.

`D_B = c − (δ − (k+1)·α)` with `α = 1/s`, multiplied through by `s`.  Carried in
`ℤ` because the deficit is genuinely signed: its sign is the certificate-closed
test.

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (threshold dischargeScale : ℕ) (envelope : Finset object.Vertex)
  (centre : object.Vertex),
  Graph.TypeBFanIncidence.scaledDeficit object threshold dischargeScale envelope centre =
    ↑dischargeScale * ↑(Graph.TypeBFanIncidence.closedCount object threshold envelope centre) -
        ↑dischargeScale * ↑threshold +
      (↑(object.degree centre) + 1)
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.TypeBFanIncidence.scaledDeficit.eq_1

declarations.type:

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.TypeBFanIncidence.surplus_eq_one
declarations.doc_string: **The centre surplus of a degree-`δ+1` centre is one.**

declarations.type: Graph.FiniteObject → (Graph.FiniteObject → Prop) → (ℕ → Prop) → ℕ → Prop
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.TypeBHandoffStatement
declarations.doc_string:
**Node `[144]`, the bottleneck arm's fact: the Type B handoff itself.**

`prop:nonnear-cubic-sharp-overload-routing` opens *"If a sparse surplus exit
occurs, there is nothing to route.  Otherwise…"* — so on the branch that reaches
`[144]`, which is node `[125]`'s survivor, outcome (b) is already excluded and
the manuscript's trichotomy is a *dichotomy*: the fixed caps close to the
near-cubic spine, or the bottleneck produces decorated Type B fan data.

This is that second outcome, at every declared routed bottleneck of the object:
`d_G(z) ≥ 4` and the separated tails are admissible decorated Type B handoff fan
data.  It is `lem:same-token-bottleneck-routing` with its absorbed case refuted
by survival, which is the manuscript's *"Thus every surviving separated case
enters the Type B fan ledger."*

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (threshold : ℕ) (envelope windowSupport : Finset object.Vertex)

      (Graph.TypeBHybridIncidence.nonWindowIncidenceSet object threshold envelope windowSupport centre).card
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.TypeBHybridIncidence.card_incidences_eq_card_window_add_card_nonWindow
declarations.doc_string: The cardinal partition follows from the literal disjoint union.

∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (threshold : ℕ) (envelope windowSupport : Finset object.Vertex)

declarations.doc_string:
**A cubic-closed neighbour has exactly `δ − 1` non-`h` incidences.**  It sits
at the baseline and the centre is one of its neighbours.

declarations.type:
∀ {object : Graph.FiniteObject} {LengthOK : ℕ → Prop} {threshold : ℕ} {envelope : Finset object.Vertex}
  {centre left right shared : object.Vertex},
  ¬Graph.HasCycleWithLength LengthOK object →
    LengthOK 4 →
      Graph.TypeBFanIncidence.IsCubicClosed object threshold envelope centre left →
        Graph.TypeBFanIncidence.IsCubicClosed object threshold envelope centre right →
          left ≠ right →
            shared ∈ Graph.TypeBHybridIncidence.nonHubIncidences object centre left →
              shared ∈ Graph.TypeBHybridIncidence.nonHubIncidences object centre right → False
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.TypeBHybridIncidence.endpoints_not_shared
declarations.doc_string:
**No vertex other than the centre is incident with two distinct cubic-closed
neighbours.**

`u − h − v − z − u` is a simple `4`-cycle: `u ≠ v` by hypothesis, `z ≠ h` by
hypothesis, and the remaining distinctness is adjacency.  An object avoiding the
accepted lengths carries none, once the quadrilateral is accepted.

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (threshold dischargeScale : ℕ) (envelope windowSupport : Finset object.Vertex)
  (centre : object.Vertex),

    object.degree centre + 1 ≤ dischargeScale * threshold →
      2 * Graph.TypeBFanIncidence.scaledDeficit object threshold dischargeScale envelope centre ≤
        ↑dischargeScale *
          (↑(Graph.TypeBHybridIncidence.windowIncidences object threshold envelope windowSupport centre) +
            ↑(Graph.TypeBHybridIncidence.nonWindowIncidences object threshold envelope windowSupport centre))
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.TypeBHybridIncidence.hybridCapacity_pays
declarations.doc_string:
**`s·D_B ≤ ½·s·(I_W + I_N)` at the scale `2s`: the hybrid entry pays.**

The two hypotheses are the manuscript's: `δ ≥ 3`, so a cubic-closed neighbour
carries at least two incidences, and the marked-fan slack `k + 1 ≤ s·δ`, which is
where `k ≤ α(D)` is spent — the manuscript's "and `k ≤ 8`, this total capacity
pays `D_B` with slack at least `(11−k)/4 ≥ 3/4`".

∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (threshold dischargeScale : ℕ) (envelope windowSupport : Finset object.Vertex)

The paper's actual non-hub incidence carriers, with the same packed-window
support that classifies them into `I_W` and `I_N`.  The support parameter is
part of the carrier's type-level provenance even though the union of the two
classes is independent of which side an endpoint lies on.

  Graph.TypeBHybridIncidence.incidences object threshold envelope windowSupport centre =
    (Graph.TypeBFanIncidence.closedNeighbours object threshold envelope centre).biUnion fun owner =>
      Finset.image (fun other => (owner, other)) (Graph.TypeBHybridIncidence.nonHubIncidences object centre owner)

declarations.doc_string:

centre.  For a cubic-closed neighbour these are the manuscript's `xa_p` and

  (centre : object.Vertex),

      Graph.TypeBHybridIncidence.nonWindowDemand object threshold dischargeScale envelope windowSupport centre ≤
        ↑dischargeScale *

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.TypeBHybridIncidence.nonWindowCredit_ge_demand
declarations.doc_string:
**The non-window half-credit covers the remaining demand.**

`½I_N = c − ½I_W ≥ D_B − ½I_W`, and the demand is that quantity truncated at
zero, so the available non-window credit is at least `D_N`.  This is the second
half of `lem:typeB-hybrid-incidence-budget`.

declarations.type: (object : Graph.FiniteObject) → ℕ → ℕ → Finset object.Vertex → Finset object.Vertex → object.Vertex → ℤ

declarations.doc_string: **`D_N(𝔉)`** at the scale `2s`: `max{0, D_B − ½I_W}`.

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.TypeBHybridIncidence.positive_deficit_of_two_le_closedCount
declarations.doc_string:
**`r` fan-closed ports make the deficit positive.**

(a) is the count: the ports' vertices are cubic-closed neighbours, so `c ≥ r`;
that is the caller's, since which ports the profile records is fan data.  (b) is
this arithmetic: at `r ≥ 2` the deficit is at least `2 − (δ − (k+1)α)`, which the
registered slack makes positive — the manuscript's
`D_B ≥ r − (11−k)/4 ≥ (k−3)/4 > 0`.

so the two counts split the `(δ − 1)·c` incidences the cubic-closed neighbours
carry.  At the manuscript's `δ = 3` this is its `2c`.

**A marked Type B fan** (`def:marked-typeB-fan`): a high-degree centre `h`,
its neighbour set `N(h)` carried by a proof-carrying decorated fan, and a
fan-certificate labelling `S_h : N(h) → 𝓛` with `C₂(S_h u, S_h v) = 1` for
distinct neighbours.

No degree cap is recorded here: `Marked.degree_le_eight` derives it.

declarations.type: {object : Graph.FiniteObject} → Graph.TypeBMarkedFan.Marked object → Finset object.Vertex → object.Vertex → Prop
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.TypeBMarkedFan.Marked.IsCubicClosed
declarations.doc_string:
A fan neighbour `u` is *cubic-closed* in the marked fan relative to an
assigned support when its two non-`h` incidences are also carried by that
support.  Deletion criticality forces `d_G(u) = 3` at every neighbour of a
high-degree centre, which is the form recorded here.

declarations.type:
∀ {object : Graph.FiniteObject} (marked : Graph.TypeBMarkedFan.Marked object) (support : Finset object.Vertex)
  (u : object.Vertex),
  marked.IsCubicClosed support u =
    (u ∈ marked.fan.rim ∧
      object.degree u = 3 ∧ ∀ (w : object.Vertex), object.graph.Adj u w → w ≠ marked.fan.hub → w ∈ support)
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.TypeBMarkedFan.Marked.IsCubicClosed.eq_1

declarations.type: ℕ
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.TypeBMarkedFan.packingCap
declarations.doc_string:
**The fan-degree cap of `rem:fan-finite`, as a computed quantity.**

The cap is the number of blocks of the clique cover above, i.e. the number of
distinct values `packingClass` takes on the window coordinates.  It is not
written as a numeral anywhere: it is read off the cover, which in turn is
determined by the two data of the label algebra — the window order (`Index`,
the coordinates of a packed `P₁₃`) and the forbidden wedge gaps `{0, 4, 12}`
of `isDyadic_wedgeCycle_iff`, i.e. the target's dyadic length set.

It is *not* a function of the presentation's baseline degree.  The baseline
`k` never enters `DAdj`, `packingClass` or any statement below; the manuscript
says the same in `rem:fan-finite` ("the clique bound `d_G(h) ≤ ω(𝔉safe_h)` is
an explicit structural consequence of the label algebra"), and the numeral it
records — `8` — is `packingCap_eq_eight`, a computation on the label algebra
alone.

declarations.type: Graph.TypeBMarkedFan.packingCap = 8
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.TypeBMarkedFan.packingCap_eq_eight
declarations.doc_string:
The cover has eight blocks, so `rem:fan-finite`'s recorded cap is `8`.
This is the *only* place the numeral is produced, and it is produced by
computing the cover rather than by declaring it.

declarations.doc_string:
An explicit cover of `D` by cliques:
`{0,4} {8,12} {1,5} {9} {2,6} {10} {3,7} {11}`.
Each block is an edge or an isolated vertex of `D`, so an independent set of
`D` meets each block at most once.  This is where the cap of
`rem:fan-finite` comes from.

  Graph.TypeBRefinedSupport.augmentedLedger object threshold dischargeScale piece.vertices =
    ∑ vertex ∈ ledger.removedVertices,

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.TypeBProfileSchedule.hybridEntry_of_isHybridEligible
declarations.doc_string:
**The hybrid entry conclusion in scannable form.**  For *any* assigned
profile recording at least two cubic-closed remainder-side fan neighbours:

* the local incidence capacity covers the deficit, `D_B(𝔉) ≤ ½ I_W(𝔉) + D_N(𝔉)`;
* the reserve it calls for is available, `D_N(𝔉) ≤ ½ I_N(𝔉)`;
* `D_B(𝔉) ≥ (k+1)α - 1 ≥ 5α - 1 > 0`, the manuscript's
  `D_B(𝔉) ≥ (k-3)/4 ≥ 1/4 > 0` at the registered `α = 1/4`.

No structural input and no hypothesis beyond the scan predicate: the degree
window `4 ≤ k ≤ 8` is carried by the certificate-marked fan itself
(`Marked.highDegree`, `Marked.degree_le_eight`), and the two facts about the
chosen rate are the recorded design constraints
`ReceiverLoad.LoadCapacityProfile.dischargeRate_gt` (`5α > 1`, which is the
strict positivity, read off at this very instance `c = 2`, `k = 4`) and
`dischargeRate_le` (`9α ≤ 3`, which is the fan credit `3 - (k+1)α` being
nonnegative and so is what makes the reserve available).

the centres the schedule leaves out.  One direction is
`isFanCertificateResidual_of_nine_le_degree`; the other is the canonical
labelling, which supplies a certificate at every centre of the degree window.
This is what makes the defining filter of `fanCentres` a *complete* enumeration
rather than a smuggled side condition.

declarations.type:
∀ {object : Graph.FiniteObject} {threshold dischargeScale : ℕ} {packing : Finset (Finset object.Vertex)}
  {piece : Graph.TypeBRefinedSupport.CanonicalPiece object packing}
  (obstruction : Graph.TypeBRefinedSupport.OverlapObstruction object threshold dischargeScale piece)
  (hub : object.Vertex),
  Graph.TypeBRefinedSupport.RawOverlapCoordinate.IsFor obstruction
      (Graph.TypeBRefinedSupport.RawOverlapCoordinate.missingCandidate hub) =
    (hub ∈ obstruction.demands ∧
      Graph.TypeBRefinedSupport.candidateFamily object threshold dischargeScale piece hub = [])
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.TypeBRefinedSupport.RawOverlapCoordinate.IsFor.eq_1

declarations.type:
∀ {object : Graph.FiniteObject} {threshold dischargeScale : ℕ} {packing : Finset (Finset object.Vertex)}
  {piece : Graph.TypeBRefinedSupport.CanonicalPiece object packing}
  (obstruction : Graph.TypeBRefinedSupport.OverlapObstruction object threshold dischargeScale piece)
  (left right : object.Vertex) (leftEntry rightEntry : Graph.TypeBRefinedSupport.CandidateData object)
  (atom : Graph.TypeBRefinedSupport.SupportAtom object),
  Graph.TypeBRefinedSupport.RawOverlapCoordinate.IsFor obstruction
      (Graph.TypeBRefinedSupport.RawOverlapCoordinate.supportConflict left right leftEntry rightEntry atom) =
    (left ∈ obstruction.demands ∧
      right ∈ obstruction.demands ∧
        left ≠ right ∧
          leftEntry ∈ Graph.TypeBRefinedSupport.candidateFamily object threshold dischargeScale piece left ∧
            rightEntry ∈ Graph.TypeBRefinedSupport.candidateFamily object threshold dischargeScale piece right ∧
              atom ∈ leftEntry.supportAtoms threshold packing left ∧

declarations.doc_string:
All proof-free coordinates obtainable from the literal finite candidate
families.  The semantic filter below removes equal-demand and nonempty-family
`missingCandidate` records.

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (threshold dischargeScale : ℕ) {packing : Finset (Finset object.Vertex)}
  (piece : Graph.TypeBRefinedSupport.CanonicalPiece object packing)
  (obstruction : Graph.TypeBRefinedSupport.OverlapObstruction object threshold dischargeScale piece),
  Graph.TypeBRefinedSupport.rawOverlapCoordinateSchedule object threshold dischargeScale piece obstruction =
    List.map Graph.TypeBRefinedSupport.RawOverlapCoordinate.missingCandidate obstruction.demands.toList ++
      List.flatMap
        (fun left =>
          List.flatMap
            (fun right =>
              List.flatMap
                (fun leftEntry =>
                  List.flatMap
                    (fun rightEntry =>
                      List.map
                          (fun atom =>
                            Graph.TypeBRefinedSupport.RawOverlapCoordinate.supportConflict left right leftEntry
                              rightEntry atom)
                          (leftEntry.supportAtoms threshold packing left ∩
                              rightEntry.supportAtoms threshold packing right).toList ++
                        List.map
                          (fun unit =>
                            Graph.TypeBRefinedSupport.RawOverlapCoordinate.reserveConflict left right leftEntry
                              rightEntry unit)
                          (leftEntry.consumedReserveUnits threshold piece left ∩
                              rightEntry.consumedReserveUnits threshold piece right).toList)
                    (Graph.TypeBRefinedSupport.candidateFamily object threshold dischargeScale piece right))
                (Graph.TypeBRefinedSupport.candidateFamily object threshold dischargeScale piece left))
            obstruction.demands.toList)
        obstruction.demands.toList
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.TypeBRefinedSupport.rawOverlapCoordinateSchedule.eq_1

**Exit `(2)` through one completion port**: two receiver-entry returns
through `⃗e = (w,h)` are internally vertex-disjoint as anchored paths, and their
lengths sum to an accepted cycle length.

`⃗e` at node `[93]` -- it is the port carrying the visible receiver-entry
returns -- and then walks the exit list of *that* port.

**Clause (Q1) as a generation predicate.**

`Q1Generated clause base identified` holds exactly when `clause` is the

clause is generated here: (Q2)--(Q4) are other nodes' constructions, and a

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.VisibleEntry.card_le_sum_silentExcess_add_positiveDeficiency
declarations.doc_string:
**`lem:typeA-silent-excess-count`.**

*"Suppose that no saturated receiver of `X` has a completion port carrying `s`
visible receiver-entry returns, and form the visible-first excess basins.  Then
`S_sil^exc(X) ≥ n_δ − Σ_w c(w) = s·D_A(X)`."*

Cleared of the division and the subtraction, `s·D_A(X) = |V(X)| − s·def⁺(X)`,
so the statement is `|V(X)| ≤ S_sil^exc(X) + s·def⁺(X)`.  The three hypotheses
are the manuscript's own: the support is capped at the baseline and its vertices
sit exactly there (no ambient surplus), the routing is total (`node [88]`), and
no saturated receiver has a port carrying `s` visible returns (the branch this
count lives on).

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (support : Finset object.Vertex) (threshold scale : ℕ),

          (Graph.VisibleEntry.silentExcess object support threshold scale x).card +
        scale * object.positiveDeficiency support threshold →
    (object.receivers support threshold).card + (object.fullVertices support threshold).card = support.card →
      ¬support.card ≤
            ∑ receiver ∈ object.receivers support threshold,
                (Graph.VisibleEntry.silentExcess object support threshold scale receiver).card +
              scale * object.positiveDeficiency support threshold →
        False

Scanning a walk that starts outside the support and ends inside it, the first

the vertices of the support sit at the baseline.  Nothing is assumed about the
return beyond its being one.

completion port.**

branch, not an assumption about this port, and the conclusion is the negation

declarations.doc_string:
**`lem:typeA-silent-excess-count` at one receiver.**

*"If `L(w) ≤ c(w)`, then `w` contributes no unpaid routed vertex.  If
`L(w) > c(w)`, then `w` is saturated; since `w` has exactly `q(w)` completion
ports and no port carries `s` visible receiver-entry returns, `L_vis(w) ≤
(s−1)q(w) ≤ c(w)`, so the visible-first order pays every visible routed load
before the payable set is exhausted, and every unpaid routed vertex at `w` is
silent."*

Written without subtraction, that is `1 + L(w) ≤ |𝒰(w)| + s·q(w)`.  The port
hypothesis is needed only at a saturated receiver, exactly as the manuscript
uses it.

**(Q1)'s declared routed-load support.**

*"In (Q1) it is the set of visible routed loads whose response coordinates are

∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (support : Finset object.Vertex) (threshold scale : ℕ) (receiver : object.Vertex),

declarations.type: {order : ℕ} → Finset (Fin order) → Prop
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.WindowCurvature.FanIndependent
declarations.doc_string:
**The manuscript's `D`.**  A set of window coordinates is *fan-independent*
when no two distinct members close an accepted cycle through the length-two
wedge.  This is exactly "independent set in `D`".

declarations.type: ℕ → ℕ → Prop
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.WindowCurvature.ForbiddenGap
declarations.doc_string:
A coordinate difference is *forbidden at `shift`* when the cycle it closes
is accepted by the registered dyadic target.  This is the only place a
forbidden difference is ever named, and it names none: it asks the target.

*Provenance.* Consumes `Core.DyadicLength.PowerOfTwoLength` at
`Core/DyadicLength.lean:21`.

declarations.type:
∀ (shift difference : ℕ),
  Graph.WindowCurvature.ForbiddenGap shift difference =
    Core.DyadicLength.PowerOfTwoLength (Graph.WindowCurvature.closingLength shift difference)
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.WindowCurvature.ForbiddenGap.eq_1

declarations.type: ℕ → Type
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.WindowCurvature.Label
declarations.doc_string:
The set of path coordinates an outside vertex attaches to.  The manuscript's
`S(x) ⊆ {0, …, order-1}`.

*Provenance.* Follows `Graph.TypeBMarkedFan.Label` at
`Graph/TypeBMarkedFan.lean:155`, the order-`13`-fixed copy of this carrier.

declarations.type: (order : ℕ) → Finset (Graph.WindowCurvature.Label order)
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.WindowCurvature.Labels
declarations.doc_string:
`Labels`: the legal nonempty labels of a path of the given order.

*Provenance.* Follows `Graph.TypeBMarkedFan.compatibleParts` at
`Graph/TypeBMarkedFan.lean:338`.

declarations.type: ∀ (order : ℕ), Graph.WindowCurvature.Labels order = Finset.filter Graph.WindowCurvature.Legal Finset.univ
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.WindowCurvature.Labels.eq_1

declarations.type: {order : ℕ} → Graph.WindowCurvature.Label order → Prop
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.WindowCurvature.Legal
declarations.doc_string:
A nonempty label is legal exactly when a single outside vertex carrying it
closes no accepted cycle through the path: the manuscript's legality is the
safety relation at outside length zero, applied to the label against itself.

*Provenance.* Follows `Graph.TypeBMarkedFan.IsLegal` at
`Graph/TypeBMarkedFan.lean:122`.

declarations.type:
∀ {order : ℕ} (label : Graph.WindowCurvature.Label order),
  Graph.WindowCurvature.Legal label = (Finset.Nonempty label ∧ Graph.WindowCurvature.Safe 0 label label)
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.WindowCurvature.Legal.eq_1

declarations.type: {order : ℕ} → ℕ → Graph.WindowCurvature.Label order → Graph.WindowCurvature.Label order → Prop
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.WindowCurvature.Safe
declarations.doc_string:
The manuscript's safety relation: `C_shift(source, target) = 1` iff
`shift + 2 + |i - j| ∉ Pow` for all `i ∈ source`, `j ∈ target`.  An outside
path of length `shift` between vertices carrying these labels is safe through
the induced path exactly when this holds.

*Provenance.* Follows `Graph.TypeBMarkedFan.SafeAtDistance` at
`Graph/TypeBMarkedFan.lean:175`.

declarations.type:
∀ {order : ℕ} (family : Finset (Graph.WindowCurvature.Label order)),
  (∀ label ∈ family, Graph.WindowCurvature.Legal label) →
    (∀ source ∈ family, ∀ target ∈ family, source ≠ target → Graph.WindowCurvature.Safe 2 source target) →
      family.card ≤ Graph.WindowCurvature.fanPackingCap order
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.WindowCurvature.card_le_fanPackingCap
declarations.doc_string:
**`lem:fan-certificate`, first sentence.**

A family of legal labels that is pairwise `C₂`-compatible has size at most
`α(D)`.

The manuscript's argument exactly: choose a representative from each label; the
compatibility relation says no cross-difference between two labels of the family
closes an accepted cycle, so the representatives are pairwise non-adjacent in
`D`, and they are *distinct* because a repeated representative would be a
cross-difference of `0`, which `forbiddenGap_two_zero` forbids.  A family of
distinct pairwise non-adjacent coordinates is an independent set of `D`.

declarations.type:
∀ {order : ℕ} {indices : Finset (Fin order)},
  Graph.WindowCurvature.FanIndependent indices → indices.card ≤ Graph.WindowCurvature.fanPackingCap order
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.WindowCurvature.card_le_fanPackingCap_of_fanIndependent

declarations.type:
∀ {order : ℕ} (family : Finset (Graph.WindowCurvature.Label order)),
  ∀ label ∈ family,
    (∀ other ∈ family, Graph.WindowCurvature.Legal other) →
      (∀ source ∈ family, ∀ target ∈ family, source ≠ target → Graph.WindowCurvature.Safe 2 source target) →
        family.card ≤
          1 + Graph.WindowCurvature.fanPackingCapAvoiding order (Graph.WindowCurvature.fanClosedNeighbourhood label)
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.WindowCurvature.card_le_one_add_fanPackingCapAvoiding
declarations.doc_string:
**`lem:fan-certificate`, second sentence.**

A pairwise `C₂`-compatible family containing the label `S` has size at most
`1 + α(D[A])`, where `A` is the complement of `N_D[S]`.

The manuscript's argument exactly: every *other* label of the family is
compatible with `S`, so none of its indices lies in `N_D[S]`; the
representatives of the others therefore form an independent set of `D` avoiding
`N_D[S]`.  The manuscript then computes `α(D[A]) ≤ 6` when `S` is a
non-singleton, which is where its `≤ 7` comes from; that computation is a
consequence of this bound at the registered order, not a separate hypothesis.

declarations.type:
∀ {order : ℕ} (family : Finset (Graph.WindowCurvature.Label order)) (label : Graph.WindowCurvature.Label order),
  family.card - 1 ≤
      Graph.WindowCurvature.fanPackingCapAvoiding order (Graph.WindowCurvature.fanClosedNeighbourhood label) →
    (family.erase label).card = family.card - 1 →
      1 ≤ family.card →
        ¬family.card ≤
              1 +
                Graph.WindowCurvature.fanPackingCapAvoiding order (Graph.WindowCurvature.fanClosedNeighbourhood label) →
          False
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.WindowCurvature.card_le_one_add_fanPackingCapAvoiding._proof_1_1

declarations.type: ℕ → ℕ → ℕ
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.WindowCurvature.closingLength
declarations.doc_string:
The cycle closed through the induced path by an outside path of length
`shift` between coordinates at distance `difference`: the `difference` edges of
the subpath, the `shift` outside edges, and the two attachment edges.  This is
the manuscript's `s + 2 + |i - j|`.

*Provenance.* Follows `Graph.TypeBMarkedFan.outsideCycleLength` at
`Graph/TypeBMarkedFan.lean:117`.

declarations.type: (order : ℕ) → ℕ → BitVec order → BitVec order → Bool
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.WindowCurvature.codeCompatible
declarations.doc_string:
The bitwise form of the manuscript's `C_s`: no coordinate of `source` and
coordinate of `target` may sit at a difference whose closing cycle the target
accepts.  The differences tested are `forbiddenGaps`, i.e. they are derived, not
scheduled.

*Provenance.* Follows `Core.FiniteBitRelationBarrier.Profile.flatCount` at
`Core/FiniteBitRelationBarrier.lean:34`, the framework's own bitwise `&&&`
composition test on packed rows.

declarations.type:
∀ (order shift : ℕ) (source target : BitVec order),
  Graph.WindowCurvature.codeCompatible order shift source target =
    decide
      (∀ gap ∈ Graph.WindowCurvature.forbiddenGaps order shift,
        source &&& target >>> gap = 0#order ∧ target &&& source >>> gap = 0#order)
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.WindowCurvature.codeCompatible.eq_1

declarations.type: {order : ℕ} → List ℕ → BitVec order → BitVec order → Bool
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.WindowCurvature.codeCompatibleWith
declarations.doc_string:
The bitwise safety test folded over an explicitly scheduled difference
list.  This is `codeCompatible` with its quantifier replaced by a fold; the
schedule it is run at is supplied, so a caller can compute it once.

*Provenance.* Follows `codeCompatible` above.

declarations.type:
∀ {order : ℕ} (gaps : List ℕ) (source target : BitVec order),
  Graph.WindowCurvature.codeCompatibleWith gaps source target =
    gaps.all fun gap => source &&& target >>> gap == 0#order && target &&& source >>> gap == 0#order
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.WindowCurvature.codeCompatibleWith.eq_1

declarations.type:
∀ (order shift : ℕ) (source target : BitVec order),
  Graph.WindowCurvature.codeCompatibleWith (Graph.WindowCurvature.gapSchedule order shift) source target =
    Graph.WindowCurvature.codeCompatible order shift source target
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.WindowCurvature.codeCompatibleWith_gapSchedule
declarations.doc_string:
**The executable test is the quantified one.**

*Provenance.* Consumes `mem_gapSchedule` above.

declarations.type:
∀ (order shift : ℕ) (source target : BitVec order),
  Graph.WindowCurvature.codeCompatible order shift source target = true ↔
    Graph.WindowCurvature.Safe shift (Graph.WindowCurvature.labelOfCode source)
      (Graph.WindowCurvature.labelOfCode target)
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.WindowCurvature.codeCompatible_eq_true_iff
declarations.doc_string:
**The code relation is the manuscript's `C_s`.**  The bitwise test on two
packed codes holds exactly when the labels those codes name are safe at that
outside length.

*Provenance.* Consumes `WindowCurvature.safe_iff_notMem_forbiddenGaps`.

declarations.type: ∀ (order : ℕ) (left right : Fin order), ↑left ≤ ↑right → ¬↑left - ↑right + (↑right - ↑left) + ↑left = ↑right → False
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.WindowCurvature.codeCompatible_eq_true_iff._proof_1_2

declarations.type: ∀ (order : ℕ) (left right : Fin order), ↑right ≤ ↑left → ¬↑left - ↑right + (↑right - ↑left) + ↑right = ↑left → False
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.WindowCurvature.codeCompatible_eq_true_iff._proof_1_3

declarations.type: ∀ (order gap index : ℕ), ¬index - (gap + index) + (gap + index - index) = gap → False
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.WindowCurvature.codeCompatible_eq_true_iff._proof_1_4

declarations.type: ∀ (order gap index : ℕ), ¬gap + index - index + (index - (gap + index)) = gap → False
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.WindowCurvature.codeCompatible_eq_true_iff._proof_1_5

declarations.type: (order : ℕ) → BitVec order → Bool
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.WindowCurvature.codeLegal
declarations.doc_string:
The bitwise form of the manuscript's legality: a nonzero code no two of
whose set bits sit at a forbidden difference.

*Provenance.* Follows `Core.FiniteBitRelationBarrier.Profile.flatCount` at
`Core/FiniteBitRelationBarrier.lean:34`.

declarations.type:
∀ (order : ℕ) (code : BitVec order),
  Graph.WindowCurvature.codeLegal order code =
    (!code == 0#order && Graph.WindowCurvature.codeCompatible order 0 code code)
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.WindowCurvature.codeLegal.eq_1

∀ (order : ℕ) (code : BitVec order),
  Graph.WindowCurvature.codeLegal order code = true ↔
    Graph.WindowCurvature.Legal (Graph.WindowCurvature.labelOfCode code)
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.WindowCurvature.codeLegal_eq_true_iff
declarations.doc_string:
**The code legality test is the manuscript's legality.**

*Provenance.* Consumes `codeCompatible_eq_true_iff` above.

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.WindowCurvature.codeRelation
declarations.doc_string:
The code-indexed safety relation of a certificate row.

*Provenance.* Follows
`Core.FiniteBitRelationBarrier.SemanticCertificate.row_semantic` at
`Core/FiniteBitRelationBarrier.lean:93`, the code-indexed relation a generated
table is audited against.

declarations.type:

  Graph.WindowCurvature.codeRelation order shift source target =

∀ (order shift : ℕ) (source target : Fin (Graph.WindowCurvature.legalCodeList order).length),

        (Graph.WindowCurvature.labelAtIndex order target))

declarations.doc_string:

relation a generated bit table is audited against *is* the manuscript's `C_s`
on the labels its indices name.

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.WindowCurvature.curvatureTwo
declarations.doc_string:
`Ω₂(S, A, T) = C₁(S,A) · C₁(A,T) · (1 - C₂(S,T))`: two individually safe
outside edges composing into an unsafe outside path of length two.

*Provenance.* Follows `Graph.TypeBMarkedFan.WedgeSafe` at
`Graph/TypeBMarkedFan.lean:180`, which is its third factor.

declarations.type:
∀ {order : ℕ} (source middle target : Graph.WindowCurvature.Label order),
  Graph.WindowCurvature.curvatureTwo source middle target =
    (decide (Graph.WindowCurvature.Safe 1 source middle) && decide (Graph.WindowCurvature.Safe 1 middle target) &&
      !decide (Graph.WindowCurvature.Safe 2 source target))
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.WindowCurvature.curvatureTwo.eq_1

declarations.type:
∀ {order : ℕ} (source middle target : Graph.WindowCurvature.Label order),
  Graph.WindowCurvature.curvatureTwo source middle target = true ↔
    Graph.WindowCurvature.Safe 1 source middle ∧
      Graph.WindowCurvature.Safe 1 middle target ∧ ¬Graph.WindowCurvature.Safe 2 source target
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.WindowCurvature.curvatureTwo_eq_true_iff

*Provenance.* Follows `Graph.TypeBMarkedFan.wedgeSafe_iff` at
`Graph/TypeBMarkedFan.lean:196`.

excluded by `S` when some index of `S` closes an accepted cycle with it through
the wedge.  Because `forbiddenGap_two_zero` holds, `S ⊆ N_D[S]`, so the
neighbourhood really is closed.

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.WindowCurvature.forbiddenGap_two_zero

`closingLength 2 0 = 4`, and the quadrilateral is accepted.  This is what makes
distinct `C₂`-compatible labels carry distinct representatives, the manuscript's
"since `C₂(S,S) = 0`".

declarations.doc_string:
**A shared window violating the legal-label relation `C_s`.**

Two outside vertices attach to one packed window; the simple path joining them
avoids the window; and the closing length their two attachment coordinates
determine is accepted by the target.  `labelCollision_iff_not_safe` is the
statement that this last clause *is* failure of `C_s` at the registered dyadic
target, so nothing here restates the relation.

The connector is a `Walk`, so the `s = 0` case is the single outside vertex of
`lem:labels`: `source = target` and the connector is empty.

declarations.doc_string:
**The collision clause is exactly `¬ C_s(S, T)`.**

`Graph.WindowCurvature.Safe` is `∀ i ∈ S, ∀ j ∈ T, ¬ ForbiddenGap s |i − j|`,
and `ForbiddenGap` is the registered dyadic target applied to the closing
length.  So the existential clause of `LabelCollision`, read at that target, is
its negation.  This is why the alternative below is the manuscript's own exit
`(3)` and not a surrogate for it.

∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (baselineDegree : ℕ),
  (∀ (vertex : object.Vertex), baselineDegree ≤ object.degree vertex) →
    baselineDegree * object.vertexCount ≤ 2 * object.edgeCount
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.baselineDegree_mul_vertexCount_le_two_mul_edgeCount
declarations.doc_string:
**The complementary near-cubic edge bound, also read rather than assumed.**

`two_mul_edgeCount_le_of_degreeSurplus_le` caps `2m` from above off the node
`[19]` branch.  The density comparison also needs `2m` from *below*, and that
half is not a branch fact at all: it is the handshake against the presentation's
own closed minimum-degree baseline, `Σ_v deg v = 2m` with `deg v ≥ δ` at every
vertex, i.e. `δ n ≤ 2m`.

The proof is the handshake itself and nothing else: summing the constant `δ`
over the vertices is `δ n`, summing the degrees is `2m`, and the baseline
compares the two summands pointwise.  `δ` is the baseline the presentation
registered to produce `degreeSurplus`, the same one
`two_mul_edgeCount_le_of_degreeSurplus_le` subtracts.

declarations.type:
∀ {Baseline : Graph.FiniteObject → Prop} {LengthOK : ℕ → Prop} {object : Graph.FiniteObject} {Coordinate : Type u}
  {family : Finset Coordinate} {coordinateSupport : Coordinate → Finset object.Vertex},
  Graph.SurvivesSparseExits Baseline (Graph.HasCycleWithLength LengthOK) LengthOK object →
    (∀ (support : Finset object.Vertex),
        ¬Graph.Strategy.InterfaceReplacement.ReplacementSupport Baseline (Graph.HasCycleWithLength LengthOK) object
            support) →
      ∀
        (attempt :
          Graph.AttemptedQuotient Baseline (Graph.HasCycleWithLength LengthOK) object family coordinateSupport),
        ¬Set.InjOn attempt.label ↑family →
          (∃ left right, attempt.Identifies left right ∧ left.boundaryDegreeProfile ≠ right.boundaryDegreeProfile) ∨
            ∃ left right,
              attempt.Identifies left right ∧ Graph.Response.TargetDefect (Graph.HasCycleWithLength LengthOK) left right
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.blockerSeparation_of_reducing
declarations.doc_string:
**`lem:sparse-pair-dependence-exit` and `lem:mixed-sparse-spine-dependence`,
at a survivor.**

> Suppose the coordinate family `ℛ_Π` does not survive every admissible rank
> quotient.  Then either `G` has a sparse surplus exit, or some `π ∈ Π` has a
> sparse surplus blocker of type (d) or (e).

The two exit alternatives the manuscript's proof produces are discharged by the
survivor's own hypotheses — the whole-graph case is the delocalization exit, and
the proper-support case is `lem:replacement` — so what a rank-reducing attempted
determination leaves is precisely the blocker: two realizations it identifies
which are separated by their boundary degree profiles (type (d)) or by a
boundaried context (type (e)).

Both witnesses are the concrete finite objects `def:surplus-blockers` names,
which is what `DemandActivation.blocks_boundaryProfile` and
`blocks_targetResponse` record on the ledger.

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.choose_le_pow_of_three_mul_le
declarations.doc_string:
**The upper binomial estimate, cleared of `e`.**

`C(N,k) ≤ base^k` whenever `3N ≤ k·base`.  This is `C(N,k) ≤ (eN/k)^k` with the
division cleared and `e` replaced by Stirling's `⌈e⌉`: `k! · C(N,k) ≤ N^k` is the
descending-factorial bound, and `k^k ≤ 3^k·k!` converts the `k!` into the `k^k`
the hypothesis compares against.

identity `C(N,k+1)·(k+1) = C(N,k)·(N−k)` bounds the ratio by `N/(k+1)`, and the
hypothesis bounds that by `n`.

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.choose_two_le_mul

skeleton stratum at the cubic baseline edge count.

declarations.type:

declarations.type:

      (2 * vertexCount) ^ Graph.cubicBaselineEdgeCount vertexCount baselineDegree
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.cubicBaselineBudget_le_pow
declarations.doc_string:
**`lem:exact-cubic-baseline-budget`, upper half:** `C(N, m₀) ≤ (2n)^{m₀}`.

Taking `log₂`, this is `B₀(n) ≤ m₀·(log₂ n + 1) = (δ/2)n log₂ n + O(n)`, the
manuscript's upper bound at the registered baseline.  The alphabet comparison
`3N ≤ m₀·2n` is `m₀ ≥ n` (which is `2 ≤ δ`) against `2N = (n−1)n ≤ n²`.

declarations.type:

  2 ≤ baselineDegree →

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.cubicBaselineBudget_le_two_pow
declarations.doc_string: The baseline stratum fits in its own bit count.

declarations.type:

      Graph.cubicBaselineBudget vertexCount baselineDegree ≤
        2 ^ (lowerBound + Graph.spineDeficit vertexCount baselineDegree lowerBound)
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.cubicBaselineBudget_le_two_pow_add_spineDeficit
declarations.doc_string:
The deficit is admissible at its own package: `B₀(n) ≤ L + E_spine(n)` in
bits, for every lower bound `L`.  This is what makes `spineDeficit` an output
rather than a registered constant.

declarations.type:
∀ (vertexCount : ℕ) {baselineDegree : ℕ} (lowerBound : ℕ),

        lowerBound + (Graph.cubicBaselineExponent vertexCount baselineDegree - lowerBound) →
    False

demand is residual-derived.

additive loss absorbing endpoint collisions with the finitely many reserved
boundary and tie-breaking choices inside the canonical packing; that bounded
loss is exactly what its `c₁₃ - o(1)` per-window rate carries, and it does not
change the `log₂ n` growth registered here.

  0 < ∑ edgeCount ∈ edgeCounts, Graph.edgeStratumCount vertexCount edgeCount →
    0 < edgeCounts.card →
      0 < edgeCounts.sup (Graph.edgeStratumCount vertexCount) →
        Graph.edgeFamilyEntropy vertexCount edgeCounts ≤
          Real.logb 2 ↑edgeCounts.card + Graph.largestStratumEntropy vertexCount edgeCounts
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.edgeFamilyEntropy_le_card_add_largest

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (baselineDegree : ℕ),
  Graph.cubicBaselineEdgeCount object.vertexCount baselineDegree ≤ object.edgeCount →
    object.edgeCount - Graph.cubicBaselineEdgeCount object.vertexCount baselineDegree ≤
      object.degreeSurplus baselineDegree
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.edgeSlack_le_degreeSurplus
declarations.doc_string:
The number of edges above the cubic baseline is at most the degree
surplus.  This is the exact form of `s <= sigma/2 + 1` needed by the final
quadratic absorption (and is deliberately a slightly weaker integral bound).

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (baselineDegree : ℕ),
  ¬baselineDegree * object.vertexCount ≤ 2 * ((baselineDegree * object.vertexCount + 1) / 2) → False
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.edgeSlack_le_degreeSurplus._proof_1_1

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (baselineDegree : ℕ),
  Graph.cubicBaselineEdgeCount object.vertexCount baselineDegree ≤ object.edgeCount →
    baselineDegree * object.vertexCount ≤ 2 * Graph.cubicBaselineEdgeCount object.vertexCount baselineDegree →
      ¬object.edgeCount - Graph.cubicBaselineEdgeCount object.vertexCount baselineDegree ≤
            2 * object.edgeCount - baselineDegree * object.vertexCount →
        False
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.edgeSlack_le_degreeSurplus._proof_1_2

declarations.type: ℕ → ℕ → ℕ
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.edgeStratumCount
declarations.doc_string:
The number of labelled simple graphs on a fixed `vertexCount`-element
vertex set with exactly `edgeCount` edges.

declarations.type: ∀ (vertexCount edgeCount : ℕ), Graph.edgeStratumCount vertexCount edgeCount = (vertexCount.choose 2).choose edgeCount
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.edgeStratumCount.eq_1

declarations.type:
∀ (vertexCount : ℕ) {edgeCounts : Finset ℕ} {edgeCount : ℕ},
  edgeCount ∈ edgeCounts →
    Graph.edgeStratumCount vertexCount edgeCount ≤ Graph.variableEdgeBudget vertexCount edgeCounts
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.edgeStratumCount_le_variableEdgeBudget
declarations.doc_string:
The pointwise form of the same union bound: one admissible stratum is
dominated by the whole family's budget.  This is what a node holding a single
exact edge count needs in order to state `rem:budget-robustness` — that its
retained bound survives when the edge count is only known to lie in the family
— and it is the elementary half of
`sum_edgeStratumCount_le_variableEdgeBudget`: the exact stratum is one of the
family's, so it is below the family's supremum, and the family is nonempty, so
the supremum is below the budget's `card * sup`.

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) {baselineDegree spineCount freeCount deficit : ℕ},
  2 ≤ baselineDegree →
    Graph.cubicBaselineEdgeCount object.vertexCount baselineDegree ≤ object.edgeCount →
      2 ^ (spineCount + freeCount) ≤ Graph.skeletonBudget object →
        Graph.cubicBaselineBudget object.vertexCount baselineDegree ≤ 2 ^ (spineCount + deficit) →
          2 ^ freeCount ≤
            2 ^ deficit *
              object.vertexCount ^ (object.edgeCount - Graph.cubicBaselineEdgeCount object.vertexCount baselineDegree)
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.entropySandwich
declarations.doc_string:
**`prop:sparse-entropy-sandwich-with-blockers`, with the logarithms
cleared.**

  `2^{|ℐ_spine| + |Π_free|} ≤ C(N,m)`  and  `C(N,m₀) ≤ 2^{|ℐ_spine| + E}`
  ⟹ `2^{|Π_free|} ≤ 2^{E} · n^{m − m₀}`.

Taking `log₂` gives the manuscript's

  `|Π_free| ≤ E_spine(n) + (m − m₀)·log₂ n`,

and `m − m₀ ≤ ½σ(G) + 1` is the branch's own slack identity, which is why the
display carries `(½σ(G) + 1) log₂ n`.

The proof is the manuscript's three steps and nothing else: the entropy count on
the mixed family, `lem:incremental-skeleton-room` at the object's own edge count,
and the baseline demand.  The spine count cancels because it appears on both
sides, which is the sense in which the sandwich charges only the *free* pairs.

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) {baselineDegree spineCount pairCount deficit : ℕ},
  2 ≤ baselineDegree →
    Graph.cubicBaselineEdgeCount object.vertexCount baselineDegree ≤ object.edgeCount →
      2 ^ (spineCount + pairCount) ≤ Graph.skeletonBudget object →
        Graph.cubicBaselineBudget object.vertexCount baselineDegree ≤ 2 ^ (spineCount + deficit) →
          2 ^ pairCount ≤
            2 ^ deficit *
              object.vertexCount ^ (object.edgeCount - Graph.cubicBaselineEdgeCount object.vertexCount baselineDegree)
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.entropySandwich_of_unblocked
declarations.doc_string:
**`prop:sparse-entropy-sandwich`**: the same bound at the *full* pair
schedule.

The manuscript states it for `C(|𝒜₀|,2)` rather than for `|Π_free|`, under the
stronger hypothesis that *no* pair has a blocker — in which case `Π_free` is the
whole schedule.  So it is `entropySandwich` read at `freeCount = C(|𝒜₀|,2)`, and
nothing is proved twice.

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) {pairCount : ℕ},
  2 ^ (0 + pairCount) ≤ Graph.skeletonBudget object → 2 ^ pairCount ≤ Graph.skeletonBudget object
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.entropySaturation_of_unblocked
declarations.doc_string:
**`cor:sparse-pair-entropy-saturation`, with the logarithm cleared.**

> If `G` survives the sparse surplus exits and no pair in `C(𝒜₀,2)` has a sparse
> surplus blocker, then `C(|𝒜₀|,2) ≤ log₂ C(C(n,2), m)`.

This is the entropy count at `ℐ_spine = ∅`: `2^{C(|𝒜₀|,2)} ≤ C(N,m)`, which is
`Graph.skeletonBudget` at the object's own order and edge count.  The manuscript
derives it from `prop:sparse-pair-independence-dichotomy` together with
`lem:independent-target-entropy` and `lem:skeleton-dominates`, and that is
exactly the composition the `entropy` hypothesis names.

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (exponent baselineDegree : ℕ),
  2 ^ exponent ≤ Graph.skeletonBudget object →
    baselineDegree * object.vertexCount ≤ 2 * object.edgeCount →
      3 ≤ baselineDegree → exponent ≤ (Graph.dyadicScaleCount object + 1) * object.edgeCount
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.exponent_le_dyadicScaleCount_succ_mul_edgeCount
declarations.doc_string:
**The linear form of the surviving cap: `exponent ≤ (log₂ n + 1) · m`.**

`two_pow_le_pow_pred_vertexCount` bounds the cap's exponent by `(n-1)^m`; the
object's own dyadic scale count converts that base to a power of two through
`lt_two_pow_succ_dyadicScaleCount`, giving the entropy statement the manuscript
writes as

  `c₁₃ · p₁₃ · log₂ n ≤ m · log₂ n + O(m)`.

Both `log₂ n` and `m` are read off the residual object.  The `+1` is the exact
`Nat` cost of `n` not being a power of two; it is the only slack in the whole
chain and it is `m` bits against a budget of `m log₂ n`.  The slack-free
statement is `two_pow_le_pow_pred_vertexCount` itself.

declarations.type: ∀ (exponent base budgetLog count : ℕ), 2 ^ exponent ≤ base ^ count → base ≤ 2 ^ budgetLog → exponent ≤ budgetLog * count
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.exponent_le_of_two_pow_le_pow
declarations.doc_string:
The entropy (`log₂`) form of an exact power comparison: a base bounded by
`2 ^ budgetLog` turns `2 ^ exponent ≤ base ^ count` into the linear bound
`exponent ≤ budgetLog · count`.  Nothing here is graph-specific; it is the
`Nat` replacement for taking logarithms.

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject),
  object.edgeCount.factorial * Graph.skeletonBudget object ≤ object.vertexCount.choose 2 ^ object.edgeCount
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.factorial_mul_skeletonBudget_le_pow
declarations.doc_string:
**The skeleton budget carries its own `m!`.**

`skeletonBudget_le_two_pow` is far too weak to bound a packing density: it
throws away the whole `m`-subset structure and leaves `2 ^ C(n,2)`, which is
`n²` in the exponent where the manuscript has `n log₂ n`.  The exact statement
is that the labelled skeleton class is an `m`-subset family, so its count times
`m !` is at most `C(n,2) ^ m`:

  `m ! · C(C(n,2), m) = descFactorial (C(n,2)) m ≤ C(n,2) ^ m`.

Taking `log₂`, the `m !` is exactly the factor that turns the crude
`m · log₂ C(n,2) ≈ 2 · (3/2) n log₂ n` into the manuscript's
`(3/2) n log₂ n + O(n)` of `lem:near-cubic-budget` — a factor `2` in the
leading term, and the whole difference between a vacuous and a live density
cap.  Both `n` and `m` are read off the residual object; nothing is chosen
here.

declarations.type:
∀ {object : Graph.FiniteObject} {threshold : ℕ} {centre left right : object.Vertex},
  Graph.NormalForm object threshold centre →
    object.graph.Adj centre left →
      object.graph.Adj centre right →
        left ≠ right →
          ¬object.graph.Adj left right →
            Graph.IsOpenPort object centre left →
              Graph.IsOpenPort object centre right → Graph.FanCompatible object centre left right
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.fanCompatible_of_endpoints_nonadjacent
declarations.doc_string:
**`lem:same-center-open-port-compatibility`.**  Distinct open ports at the
same high centre whose endpoints are nonadjacent are fan-compatible.

`x ∉ s(q)` and `y ∉ s(p)` are immediate from `xy ∉ E(G)`, since a shoulder of a
port is a neighbour of its endpoint.  Disjointness is part (c) of the normal
form: a common shoulder would be a common neighbour of the nonadjacent
`x, y ∈ N_G(h)` outside `{h}`.

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (threshold order : ℕ),
  (∀ (data : Graph.CapacityPresentation object order),
      Nonempty (Graph.ObjectCapacityLedger object threshold order data)) →
    Graph.FibrePressureStatement object threshold order
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.fibrePressureStatement

declarations.type:
{Demand Token : Type u} →
  DecidableEq Demand →
    Finset (Finset Demand) →
      List Token →
        (Eligible : Token → Finset Demand → Prop) →
          ((token : Token) → (pair : Finset Demand) → Decidable (Eligible token pair)) → Finset (Finset Demand)
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.freeSide
declarations.doc_string:
The free side of a presented ledger, spelled with the decidability the
presentation itself supplies.  A structure field cannot open a `letI`, so the
instances are threaded explicitly here and the field below reads this.

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.glue
declarations.doc_string:
The glued graph with its finite schedule derived from the three disjoint
vertex families.

declarations.type:

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.glue.eq_1

declarations.type:
{boundary : Graph.Boundary} →

    (outside : Graph.OutsideContext boundary) → SimpleGraph (Graph.GluedVertex piece outside)
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.glueGraph
declarations.doc_string: Identify common boundary labels and take the union of the two owned sides.

declarations.type:

  Graph.glueGraph piece outside =
    SimpleGraph.map (⇑(Graph.pieceEmbedding piece outside)) piece.graph ⊔

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.glueGraph.eq_1

declarations.type:
∀ {boundary : Graph.Boundary} (piece : Graph.BoundaryPiece boundary) (outside : Graph.OutsideContext boundary)

  (Graph.glueGraph piece outside).Adj left right ↔ Graph.OwnedAdjacency piece outside left right
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.glueGraph_adj_iff
declarations.doc_string: Adjacency in a gluing is exactly adjacency owned by one finite side.

declarations.type:
∀ {boundary : Graph.Boundary} (piece : Graph.BoundaryPiece boundary) (outside : Graph.OutsideContext boundary),

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.glueGraph_eq_contribution_sup

declarations.type:
∀ {boundary : Graph.Boundary} {piece : Graph.BoundaryPiece boundary} (outside : Graph.OutsideContext boundary)
  (smaller : SimpleGraph (boundary.Vertex ⊕ piece.Internal)) (decide : DecidableRel smaller.Adj),
  smaller ≤ piece.graph →
    Graph.glueGraph
        { Internal := piece.Internal, internalVertices := piece.internalVertices, graph := smaller,
          decideAdj := decide }
        outside ≤
      Graph.glueGraph piece outside
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.glueGraph_mono
declarations.doc_string:
**Deleting owned edges from a piece deletes edges from the gluing.**  The
outside context and the boundary are untouched, so the two gluings share a
vertex carrier and the smaller piece's gluing is a subgraph of the larger's.

declarations.type:

    piece.boundaryDegree vertex + outside.ownedBoundaryDegree vertex
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.glue_boundaryDegree_add_overlap
declarations.doc_string: Exact boundary-degree inclusion--exclusion for unrestricted gluing.

declarations.type:
∀ {boundary : Graph.Boundary} {source replacement : Graph.BoundaryPiece boundary}

  outside.NoBoundaryEdges →
    replacement.boundaryDegreeProfile = source.boundaryDegreeProfile →
      ∀ (vertex : boundary.Vertex),
        (Graph.glue replacement outside).degree (Sum.inl vertex) = (Graph.glue source outside).degree (Sum.inl vertex)
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.glue_boundaryDegree_eq_of_local_eq_of_context_noBoundaryEdges
declarations.doc_string:
Under normalized context ownership, local boundary-degree equality
transfers directly to final glued boundary-degree equality.

declarations.type:
∀ {boundary : Graph.Boundary} {source replacement : Graph.BoundaryPiece boundary}
  (outside : Graph.OutsideContext boundary),
  replacement.boundaryDegreeProfile = source.boundaryDegreeProfile →
    Graph.boundaryOverlapDegreeProfile replacement outside = Graph.boundaryOverlapDegreeProfile source outside →
      ∀ (vertex : boundary.Vertex),
        (Graph.glue replacement outside).degree (Sum.inl vertex) = (Graph.glue source outside).degree (Sum.inl vertex)
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.glue_boundaryDegree_eq_of_local_eq_of_overlap_eq
declarations.doc_string:
Equality of local boundary degrees transfers to glued boundary degrees only
when the actual overlap-degree profiles against the context also agree.

declarations.type:
∀ {boundary : Graph.Boundary} {source replacement : Graph.BoundaryPiece boundary}
  (outside : Graph.OutsideContext boundary) (vertex : boundary.Vertex),
  (Graph.glue replacement outside).degree (Sum.inl vertex) + Graph.boundaryOverlapDegree replacement outside vertex =
      replacement.boundaryDegree vertex + outside.ownedBoundaryDegree vertex →
    (Graph.glue source outside).degree (Sum.inl vertex) + Graph.boundaryOverlapDegree source outside vertex =
        source.boundaryDegree vertex + outside.ownedBoundaryDegree vertex →
      replacement.boundaryDegree vertex = source.boundaryDegree vertex →
        Graph.boundaryOverlapDegree replacement outside vertex = Graph.boundaryOverlapDegree source outside vertex →
          ¬(Graph.glue replacement outside).degree (Sum.inl vertex) =

declarations.type:

declarations.type:

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.heavyCentreLocalDichotomy
declarations.doc_string:
**`cor:heavy-center-local-dichotomy`.**

At a high centre `h`, either two open ports at `h` are fan-compatible, or at
least `d_G(h) − 2` ports at `h` are triangular.

declarations.doc_string:
**The tester's reading on a target-avoiding residual.**

The minimal counterexample the spine argues about avoids the target, so the
tester answers `no` at every oriented edge: no root edge of any packed window
--- indeed no root edge at all --- admits a Mersenne completion, i.e. every
dart's exact return-length set misses `MersenneSet`.

This is what makes a barrier state *observable* in the sense of
`lem:p13-window-package`: a state whose tester answered `yes` would exhibit an
edge-rooted Mersenne completion and hence a dyadic cycle, contradicting the
retained avoidance.  Nothing is assumed here beyond the avoidance the residual
already carries.

declarations.type:
∀ (vertexCount : ℕ) {baselineDegree : ℕ},
  2 * Graph.cubicBaselineEdgeCount vertexCount baselineDegree ≤ vertexCount.choose 2 →
    (vertexCount - 1) ^ Graph.cubicBaselineEdgeCount vertexCount baselineDegree ≤
      Graph.cubicBaselineBudget vertexCount baselineDegree *
        (2 * (baselineDegree + 1)) ^ Graph.cubicBaselineEdgeCount vertexCount baselineDegree
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.pow_pred_le_cubicBaselineBudget_mul
declarations.doc_string:
**`lem:exact-cubic-baseline-budget`, lower half:**

  `(n−1)^{m₀} ≤ C(N, m₀) · (2(δ+1))^{m₀}`.

Taking `log₂`, this is `B₀(n) ≥ m₀·(log₂ n − log₂(2(δ+1))) = (δ/2)n log₂ n −
O(n)`, the manuscript's lower bound at the registered baseline.

The hypothesis is that the cubic baseline edge count leaves room in the pair
count, `2m₀ ≤ N`.  It is not decoration: below it the baseline stratum is empty
and `B₀(n)` has no lower bound at all, which is the sense in which the
manuscript's evaluation is an asymptotic statement.  It is the only hypothesis,
and it is a comparison of two observables of the object's own order.

declarations.type: ∀ (pairCount index : ℕ), (pairCount + 1 - index) ^ index ≤ index ^ index * pairCount.choose index
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.pow_sub_le_pow_mul_choose

descending factorial dominates `(N+1−k)^k` termwise, and `k! ≤ k^k`.

declarations.type: Graph.FiniteObject → ℕ
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.skeletonBudget
declarations.doc_string:
`lem:skeleton-dominates`: the number of labelled simple graphs on the
residual object's own vertex set carrying exactly as many edges as the
residual object itself.  A labelled simple graph on `[n]` is determined by
its edge set, a subset of the `C(n,2)` unordered pairs, so the class with `m`
edges has exactly `C(C(n,2), m)` members.

declarations.type: ∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject), Graph.skeletonBudget object = (object.vertexCount.choose 2).choose object.edgeCount
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.skeletonBudget.eq_1

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject),
  Graph.skeletonBudget object = Graph.edgeStratumCount object.vertexCount object.edgeCount
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.skeletonBudget_eq_edgeStratumCount
declarations.doc_string:
The skeleton budget *is* the object's own exact edge stratum.  Stating the
identification rather than leaving it to definitional unfolding is what lets a
node quote the edge-budget module's theorems about `edgeStratumCount` directly
on `skeletonBudget`.

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) {baselineDegree : ℕ},
  2 ≤ baselineDegree →
    Graph.cubicBaselineEdgeCount object.vertexCount baselineDegree ≤ object.edgeCount →
      Graph.skeletonBudget object ≤
        Graph.cubicBaselineBudget object.vertexCount baselineDegree *
          object.vertexCount ^ (object.edgeCount - Graph.cubicBaselineEdgeCount object.vertexCount baselineDegree)
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.skeletonBudget_le_cubicBaselineBudget_mul_pow
declarations.doc_string:
**The room the object's own edge count buys over the cubic baseline.**

An object whose edge count sits at `m₀ + s` carries a labelled skeleton budget
within a factor `n^s` of the cubic baseline budget.  This is
`lem:incremental-skeleton-room` at the object, which is how
`def:baseline-spine-demand` fixes a *common* baseline for a branch whose edge
count is above the cubic one.

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) {baselineDegree : ℕ},
  Graph.cubicBaselineEdgeCount object.vertexCount baselineDegree ≤ object.edgeCount →
    ¬Graph.cubicBaselineEdgeCount object.vertexCount baselineDegree +
            (object.edgeCount - Graph.cubicBaselineEdgeCount object.vertexCount baselineDegree) =
          object.edgeCount →
      False
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.skeletonBudget_le_cubicBaselineBudget_mul_pow._proof_1_1

declarations.type: ∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject), Graph.skeletonBudget object ≤ 2 ^ object.vertexCount.choose 2
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.skeletonBudget_le_two_pow
declarations.doc_string:
The near-cubic skeleton budget never exceeds the count of *all* labelled
graphs on the same vertex set, which is the capacity the adapter used to
register.  Fixing the edge count is therefore a strict sharpening of the
ambient class, and every cap the density comparison now survives is at least
as strong as the one it survived before.

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.skeletonBudget_le_variableEdgeBudget
declarations.doc_string:
**`rem:budget-robustness`.**  The retained skeleton budget survives when the
object's edge count is only known to lie in an admissible family: the exact
stratum is one of the family's, so the family's own union bound dominates it.
Every node that carries a cap against `skeletonBudget` can carry this beside it
without reproving anything.

declarations.doc_string:
The skeleton budget is positive: the residual object's own edge count is
one of the admissible edge counts on its own vertex set, so the class it
indexes is nonempty.  The bound `m ≤ C(n,2)` is the literal graph fact
`FiniteObject.edgeCount_le_choose_two`, not an assumption.

declarations.doc_string:
**`prop:single-graph-sparse-pressure-routing` (c): the alternatives are
exhaustive.**

No graph remains at node `[137]`.  Either every capacity ledger of the object
respects the geometric caps -- and then `σ(G) ≤ R_L(n)`, which is the near-cubic
route `[138]` -- or some ledger overloads, and then the coupled excess is
positive and forces a role-homogeneous same-token pattern whose token class
selects `[140]`, `[142]` or `[143]`.  The two arms are the two cases of the
excluded middle on `SparsePressureCapped`, so nothing is assumed to make the
split exhaustive.

declarations.type:
∀ {Baseline : Graph.FiniteObject → Prop} {LengthOK : ℕ → Prop} {object : Graph.FiniteObject} {Coordinate : Type u}
  {family : Finset Coordinate} {coordinateSupport : Coordinate → Finset object.Vertex},
  Graph.SurvivesSparseExits Baseline (Graph.HasCycleWithLength LengthOK) LengthOK object →
    (∀ (support : Finset object.Vertex),
        ¬Graph.Strategy.InterfaceReplacement.ReplacementSupport Baseline (Graph.HasCycleWithLength LengthOK) object
            support) →
      (Graph.FiniteObject.declaredQuotientSystem Baseline (Graph.HasCycleWithLength LengthOK) object family
            coordinateSupport).Survives
        ↑family
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.survives_of_exitFree
declarations.doc_string:
**`prop:sparse-pair-independence-dichotomy`.**

> If `G` survives the sparse surplus exits and no pair in `C(𝒜₀,2)` has a sparse
> surplus blocker, then the full family `{r_π}` is independently
> target-testable.

An admissible rank quotient carries no blocker separation: its two completeness
clauses are exactly the statement that identified realizations share a boundary
degree profile and are context-equivalent.  So at a survivor with no blocker the
first two alternatives of `blockerSeparation_of_reducing` are unavailable and
the remaining two are refuted, whence no member of the system reduces the
family — which is independent target-testability in the sense of
`def:target-rank`.

declarations.type:
∀ {Baseline : Graph.FiniteObject → Prop} {LengthOK : ℕ → Prop} {object : Graph.FiniteObject},
  ¬Graph.HasCycleWithLength LengthOK object →
    (∀ (smaller : Graph.FiniteObject),
        smaller.LexicographicallySmaller object → Baseline smaller → Graph.HasCycleWithLength LengthOK smaller) →
      (∀ (support : Finset object.Vertex),
          ¬Graph.Strategy.InterfaceReplacement.CompressibleSupport Baseline (Graph.HasCycleWithLength LengthOK) object
              support) →
        Graph.SurvivesSparseExits Baseline (Graph.HasCycleWithLength LengthOK) LengthOK object
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.survives_of_selection
declarations.doc_string:
**A selected minimal counterexample survives the sparse surplus exits.**

This is node `[125]`'s standing hypothesis, derived rather than assumed.  Only
the selection entry's own two halves are spent -- avoidance and minimality --
together with `lem:replacement` at that selection.

declarations.type:
∀ {Baseline Target : Graph.FiniteObject → Prop} {LengthOK : ℕ → Prop} {object : Graph.FiniteObject} {threshold : ℕ},
  Graph.SurvivesSparseExits Baseline Target LengthOK object →
    (object.excessPorts threshold).card = object.degreeSurplus threshold →
      (∀ (pair : object.Vertex × object.Vertex) (member : pair ∈ object.excessPorts threshold)
          (left right : object.Vertex),
          (∀ (vertex : object.Vertex),
              vertex ∈ (Graph.FiniteObject.surplusPortOfMem member).shoulders ↔ vertex = left ∨ vertex = right) →
            left ≠ right →
              Nonempty (Graph.FiniteObject.SurplusPort.PortReturn object pair.1 pair.2 left right) ∧
                (¬object.graph.Adj left right →
                    Nonempty (Graph.FiniteObject.SurplusPort.OpenPortWitness object LengthOK pair.2 left right)) ∧
                  (object.graph.Adj left right →
                    object.graph.Adj pair.2 left ∧ object.graph.Adj left right ∧ object.graph.Adj right pair.2)) →
        Graph.ActiveSurplusDemands Baseline Target LengthOK object threshold
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.surviving_active_family
declarations.doc_string:
**`lem:surviving-active-family`.**

> If `G` survives the sparse surplus exits, then `𝒜₀ := 𝒫_exc` is a finite
> family of active surplus demands and `|𝒜₀| = σ(G)`.

The proof is the manuscript's: every selected port has the canonical data by
`lem:sparse-excess-port-extraction` and `lem:sparse-port-activation`, and since
the object survives, no selected demand is removed by an exit.  Each of the
three inputs is a fact the branch already carries, in full -- node `[128]`'s
entry is read whole rather than projected, because all three of its clauses are
canonical data of an active demand.

declarations.type:
∀ {Baseline : Graph.FiniteObject → Prop} {LengthOK : ℕ → Prop} {object : Graph.FiniteObject} {Coordinate : Type u}
  {family : Finset Coordinate} {coordinateSupport : Coordinate → Finset object.Vertex},
  Graph.SurvivesSparseExits Baseline (Graph.HasCycleWithLength LengthOK) LengthOK object →
    (∀ (support : Finset object.Vertex),
        ¬Graph.Strategy.InterfaceReplacement.ReplacementSupport Baseline (Graph.HasCycleWithLength LengthOK) object
            support) →
      Core.TargetRank.targetRank
          (Graph.FiniteObject.declaredQuotientSystem Baseline (Graph.HasCycleWithLength LengthOK) object family
            coordinateSupport) =
        family.card
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.targetRank_eq_card_of_exitFree
declarations.doc_string:
The independently target-testable family attains full target rank: the
dichotomy read through `Core.TargetRank`'s own rank apparatus, which is the form
`def:baseline-spine-demand` consumes.

declarations.type:
∀ (LengthOK : ℕ → Prop) (k : ℕ) (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (vertex neighbor : object.Vertex),
  object.graph.Adj vertex neighbor →
    k ≤ object.minDegree →
      (∀ (w : object.Vertex), object.graph.Adj vertex w → k < object.degree w) →
        Graph.HasCycleWithLength LengthOK (object.deleteVertex vertex) →
          k ≤ (object.deleteVertex vertex).minDegree ∧ Graph.HasCycleWithLength LengthOK object
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.target_of_safeVertexDeletion
declarations.doc_string:
The complete, domain-generic "recursive step" of the minimal-degree
minimal-counterexample argument: deleting a *safe* vertex (degree at most
`k`, with every neighbour of degree strictly above `k`) both (a) keeps the
minimum-degree-`k` baseline on the smaller graph, and (b) transports any
registered cycle target found on the smaller graph back to the original —
for free, via `cycleProperSubgraphTargetMonotone`, since a cycle in an
induced subgraph is already a cycle in the source.  Neither fact depends on
any particular application (graph size, target length predicate, etc.).

What this lemma does *not* supply — and cannot, since it is real
mathematical content specific to the minimum-counterexample argument for a
given problem, not routing/recursion plumbing — is a proof that *some*
safe vertex always exists in a minimal counterexample (or a handling for
the case where none does).  That is exactly the remaining gap for a full
closure of any strategy built on this step.

declarations.type:
∀ {object : Graph.FiniteObject} {threshold : ℕ} {centre : object.Vertex},
  3 ≤ threshold →
    threshold + 1 < object.degree centre →
      object.degree centre - 2 ≤ (Graph.triangularEndpoints object centre).card →
        3 ≤ (Graph.triangularEndpoints object centre).card
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.three_le_triangularEndpoints_card
declarations.doc_string:
**"In particular, `h` has three triangular ports."**

The second alternative at a *heavy* centre -- one whose degree is at least two
above the baseline, `d_G(h) ≥ 5` at the manuscript's `δ = 3`.  This is the only
place the heaviness of the centre is used, and it is used exactly as the
manuscript uses it: `k − 2 ≥ 3`.

declarations.type:
∀ {object : Graph.FiniteObject} {threshold : ℕ} {centre : object.Vertex},
  3 ≤ threshold →
    threshold + 1 < object.degree centre →
      object.degree centre - 2 ≤ (Graph.triangularEndpoints object centre).card →
        ¬3 ≤ (Graph.triangularEndpoints object centre).card → False
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.three_le_triangularEndpoints_card._proof_1_1

declarations.type:
∀ (object : Graph.FiniteObject) (baselineDegree budgetBase : ℕ),
  baselineDegree * object.vertexCount ≤ 2 * object.edgeCount →
    3 * (object.vertexCount - 1) ≤ baselineDegree * budgetBase →
      3 * object.vertexCount.choose 2 ≤ object.edgeCount * budgetBase
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.three_mul_choose_two_le_edgeCount_mul
declarations.doc_string:
The alphabet-versus-edge comparison that makes the skeleton budget's `m !`
bite.

`\binom n2` is the number of edge slots; `m` is how many are filled.  The
labelled skeleton class therefore costs `\binom n2 ^m / m !` rather than
`\binom n2 ^m`, and by Stirling that is at most `(\lceil e\rceil \binom n2 /
m)^m`.  This lemma is exactly the statement that the base of that power is
bounded by `budgetBase`:

  `⌈e⌉ · \binom n2 ≤ m · budgetBase`.

Both hypotheses are the two halves of `def:near-cubic-spine`'s edge count.
Written out with `2\binom n2 = (n-1)n`, the proof is the single chain

  `2·(3\binom n2) = (3(n-1))·n ≤ (δ·budgetBase)·n = (δ n)·budgetBase
     ≤ (2m)·budgetBase`,

so no positivity of `δ` is needed anywhere.

declarations.type:
{Baseline : Graph.FiniteObject → Prop} →
  {BranchState : Graph.FiniteObject → Type v} →
    {Target : Graph.FiniteObject → Prop} →
      Graph.ProperSubgraphMinimalityProfile Baseline BranchState Target →
        Core.Minimality.SubobjectMinimalityProfile Target (Graph.lexicographicProgress Baseline BranchState)
          Graph.ProperSubgraph
declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.toCoreProfile
declarations.doc_string:
The graph minimality profile read as Core's subobject profile.  `toAmbient`
is the underlying graph of the certified proper subgraph, so every Core node
indexed by this profile speaks about the literal subgraph the graph layer
produced.

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.triangularEndpoints_card_of_no_compatible_pair
declarations.doc_string:
**`lem:heavy-center-triangular-alternative`.**

If no two open ports at a high centre `h` form a fan-compatible open pair, then
at least `d_G(h) − 2` ports at `h` are triangular.

The manuscript's argument exactly: the open endpoints are pairwise adjacent,
because a nonadjacent pair would be fan-compatible by
`lem:same-center-open-port-compatibility`; a matching has no clique of size
three, so there are at most two of them; and every remaining port is
triangular.

declarations.name: Hypostructure.Graph.two_mul_cubicBaselineEdgeCount_le
declarations.doc_string:
